## The lunar chain (M4-EVENT-15)

The apocalypse is a state chain, not a machine: the cultist's death в†’
`WorldGen.TriggerLunarApocalypse` (the four towers) в†’ the towers' deaths
в†’ `WorldGen.UpdateLunarApocalypse` + `StartImpendingDoom` в†’ the countdown
tick в†’ the Moon Lord's spawn.

- **The cultist's death** (`DoDeathEvents`'s 439 row,
  `NPC.cs:79393-79395`) clears `downedAncientCultist` and raises the
  apocalypse. The port's `AncientCultist` is the tower-shaped kind (its
  machine is the aiStyle-94 tower machine), so the vanilla's 439 row maps
  onto it directly.
- **`TriggerLunarApocalypse`** (`WorldGen.cs:86626-86691`) draws the four
  tower ids `{517, 422, 507, 493}` without replacement into the four world
  slots at `maxTilesX / 5 * (1 + j)`; the В±100-tile jitter retries 30
  times against the vertical clearance scan, with the
  `(num2 - 40) * 16` fallback when all fail. All four `TowerActive*` flags,
  `LunarApocalypseIsUp` and the four `ShieldStrengthTower*` (to
  `ShieldStrengthTowerMax` вЂ” 100, halved post-Moon-Lord) raise together.
  The port's fresh worktree brings the four towers up in the same
  draw-out order and clears the slot with its own tile lookup.
- **The towers' deaths** (`NPC.cs:79321-79344`) set the `downedTower*`,
  clear the `TowerActive*` and call `UpdateLunarApocalypse`, then
  `MessageLunarApocalypse` (`WorldGen.cs:86778-86801`) picks
  `Lang.misc[43 + down]` from the inactive count.
- **`UpdateLunarApocalypse`** (`:86693-86748`) re-derives the four flags
  from the live NPCs (plus the 398/396/397/400 boss family) and, when all
  four are down and the boss isn't up, `StartImpendingDoom(3600)`.
- **`StartImpendingDoom`** (`:86750-86760`) ends the apocalypse, arms
  `MaxMoonLordCountdown`/`MoonLordCountdown` and (in the vanilla)
  `GetRidOfCultists` kills the 437/438/439 ritual kinds вЂ” constants-off
  in the port (its ritual support isn't ported).
- **The countdown tick** (`Main.cs:64987-64994`) decrements once per world
  update and at zero calls `NPC.SpawnOnPlayer(Player.FindClosest(maxTilesX
  / 2, worldSurface / 2), 398)`; the port's single player stands in. The
  Celestial Sigil's route (`Player.cs:44028-44034`) is the same function
  with the item's 720 (`NPC.cs:6037`'s `ItemMoonlordCountdownTime`) and
  the Golem/hardmode/danger gates the vanilla's `CanStartInvasion`-like
  family uses.

Deviations: the Moon Lord's boss bar/head textures, the `MoonLordShake`
scene filter, the music ducking and the countdown UI are unmodelled; the
`GetRidOfCultists` ritual-cleanup arm is constants-off; the remix/no-
surface branch of the tower-place retry is constants-off.## .trwld v8 вЂ” the banner kill counts (M6-SAVE-1c)

The banner tally now rides the world file. The entry points grew a
`WorldSide { chests, banners }` (rather than more return tuples вЂ” new sections
extend the struct) and the v8 tail is a `u32` count, then per banner the id and
the kill count: the C# `BannerSystem.Save` shape (`int32` per banner id,
`BannerSystem.cs:172-186`).

- **The deviations.** The vanilla rides these counts inside the world-flags
  block as a dense array; the port's `BannerSystem` keeps them sparse
  (`BTreeMap` by banner id), so each record carries its id. `Load`
  (`BannerSystem.cs:188-212`) replaces the tally wholesale вЂ” the port's
  `load_pairs` inserts the recorded entries, and a recorded **0 stays in the
  map** so a zeroed banner round-trips (the C# keeps only the entries its
  count array carries). `claimableBanners` (the ushort array `:172-186`) is
  not modelled in the port and stays out.
- **The app wiring.** `save_world` collects `banners.pairs()` (ascending
  banner-id order) beside the chests; `App::new` restores the tally through
  `BannerSystem::load_pairs` at construction, so the placed banners' strength
  (`banner_buff_for`) reads the real counts after a reload.
- Tests: `dw_2_3_the_banner_counts_round_trip_in_v8` (zeroed and
  999999999-range counts), `dw_2_3_a_v7_payload_loads_no_banners`,
  `dw_2_3_a_truncated_banner_section_bails`,
  `dw_2_3_the_banner_section_is_deterministic`, and the app pair
  `dw_2_3_a_saved_banner_tally_round_trips_through_the_app` (two NPC
  families' counts survive, with an empty-store control). Suite 2632 / 0.

Out: the remaining C# sections вЂ” signs (no port store), the NPC block
(names/homes/homeless, App-side `App.npcs`), the bestiary kill pairs (today
the `.trplayer` sidecar v5; moving them into the world file), `SavedOreTiers`
(worldgen-local вЂ” needs a `World` field), the angler quest state (no port
fields), the TownManager rooms, the weighted pressure plates (no port store),
the creative powers/research вЂ” each needs its own scope.
surface branch of the tower-place retry is constants-off.

## Micro seeds (M5-SEED-2)

The 1.4.5 modular registry (`WorldGen.SecretSeed`) and the arms that landed
on `M5-SEED-2-micro-seeds`.

### The registry and the hash

**There are 37 micro-seeds, not 38** вЂ” `WorldGen.cs:341-413` declares 37
fields and the static ctor `:3022-3058` is 37 `SecretSeed.Register(...)`
lines; the "38" in the earlier notes is `AllSecretSeeds` (`:339`) or the
`Register` method definition (`:483`). The port's `MICRO_SEED_ORDER`
carries all 37 in registration order (which is also the `AllSecretSeeds`
walk order, so a future first-match tie-break matches).

Recognition is the hash, not a word list: `SecretSeed.Check`
(`WorldGen.cs:468-481`) normalises the text (`[^a-z0-9]`, lower-cased),
hashes it and compares to the stored code. `Utilities/Secrets.cs:16-26`:
`CryptRaw(utf8, salt, 4)` (BCrypt cost 4, the game's static salt decoded
from `"fT2JQQzNMJl2NRoMbo9RjA=="` = `7d3d89410ccd30997635 51a0c6e8f518c`),
then 1000 rounds of the deterministic `Utils.Swap` shuffle, then a second
`CryptRaw`, then standard Base64. The port is
`crates/tr-core/src/bcrypt.rs` вЂ” the full `CryptRaw` (the pi-derived
P/S tables transcribed mechanically from `BCrypt.cs:186-296`,
`Encipher`/`StreamToWord`/`Key`/`EKSKey`/`CryptRaw` verbatim).

Two things about the hash that cost the most debugging time and are now
pinned by tests:

1. **The additions wrap at 32 bits twice.** The C#'s
   `((S0 + S1) ^ S2) + S3` is unchecked u32 arithmetic; a u64 intermediate
   carries past the first overflow and every later byte diverges.
2. **`EKSKey`'s salt offset is a single counter across BOTH schedules**
   (`BCrypt.cs:110-133`) вЂ” resetting it before the S loop flips the state.
   (`Key` also had a duplicated P-encipher loop in the first draft.)

The golden vectors prove the semantics: `to_secret("pumpkinseason") ==
"Z4Odmvd5lScy/KGXHUO2nvqA9l3KRvm8"` (halloweenGen's registered code вЂ”
the word the game itself reveals in `SetSeedToRandomWithCurrentEvents`,
`WorldFileData.cs:409`) and `to_secret("arachnophobia") ==
"SPlOdka0fv8wUovao6u3VB7ZS+IbcPDu"` (noSpiderCaves). Those also prove the
port's key walk is the game's non-NUL-terminated one: the stock `bcrypt`
crate treats the key as NUL-terminated and would differ.

### Storage and the wire

`SeedFlags` (a `u16` mirror of `serializedSeedsSum`) is left byte-identical;
the 37 flags live in a new `MicroSeedFlags` (u64) beside it. They ride
`World.micro_seeds` / `GenOptions.micro_flags`, TRWLD **v7** (the u64
appended after the v6 u16; a v6 file loads as a classic world) and the
`.wld` seed text вЂ” the C# writes **no** micro-seed bytes at all
(`SaveWorldFlags`, `WorldFile.cs:1238-1250`), and recovers them from the
text at load (`WorldFileData.SetSeed` + `CheckInputForSecretSeed`), which
is what `wld.rs` now does instead of discarding the string. The port
cannot reproduce `GetFullSeedText`'s `size.difficulty.evil.sum.` prefix
form (no seed text is persisted) вЂ” recorded as the one deviation.

`InitializeSecretSeeds` (`WorldGen.cs:553-587`) maps eight of the 37 onto
`Main.*` statics (vampirism в†’ `vampireSeed`, endlessHalloween в†’
`forceHalloweenForever`, вЂ¦). The port reads those eight directly from the
flags at their use sites instead of a static pass, and the worldgen arms
read `MicroSeedFlags` directly вЂ” the net effect for each arm is the same
flag value.

### The arms

Ported (all gated, classic worlds byte-identical): `DoDigExtraHoles` and
the `surfaceIsInSpace` terrain parameters (the vanilla Grass slot,
`WorldGen.cs:12423`); `extraLivingTrees`
(`:15494-15623` + `extraLivingTreesReducedAmount`),
`extraFloatingIslands` (`:12942-13119` + its two Variations),
`biggerAbandonedHouses` (`:433-447`), `noSpiderCaves`' pass skip and the
`ILied` wall sweep (`:17358`, `:2618-2630`); the surface conversions
`DoSurfaceIsDesert` (+ Finish), `DoSurfaceIsInSpace`,
`DoSurfaceIsMushrooms`, `DoWorldIsFrozen`, `DoNoInfection`,
`DoHallowOnSurface`, `DoWorldIsInfected`, `DoStartInHardmode` and
`DoPooEverywhere` вЂ” the three Convert-driven ones go through
`spread.rs`'s opened `convert_tile`/`convert_wall`/`convert_tile_hallow`/
`convert_wall_hallow` (the port's own conversion tables, applied per cell
with the C#'s per-column type decision, including the drunk
`GenVars.crimsonLeft` half split); the `actuallyNoTraps` kill and
treasure-ring sweeps; the `paintEverythingGray`/`Negative` and
`coatEverythingEcho`/`Illuminant` sweeps with all nine `Variations`
predicates ported (`WorldGen.cs:43-337`, the count gates reading
`active_secret_seed_count`); `DoRainbowStuff`'s kinds; and the runtime
arms (the endless-holiday loot + spawner arms, vampirism's shop/pot/
regen/Zoologist, `halloweenGen`'s `PlacePumpkin`/`GrowPumpkin`/surface

## Yoyo on-hit effects (M4-PROJ-4b)

The yoyo family's hit-damage and hit-spawn arms, ported into the pool's
`damage_pve`.

### The shared counter

`Player.yoyoHitCounter` (`Player.cs:1220`'s `-1` start) lives on the port's
`Player` with `every_some_yoyo_hits(amount, countUp)` вЂ” the C#'s
`Player.EverySomeYoyoHits` (`Player.cs:4308-4316`). Three properties that
shaped the whole task:

1. **It is never reset.** No `ResetEffects` arm, no death/throw reset, no
   per-projectile reset вЂ” the counter is monotonic for the life of the
   `Player` object (the port therefore writes no reset code either).
2. **It is per-player, not per-projectile.** Every yoyo the player owns
   shares it.
3. **The -1 start shifts the schedule.** `-1 % 7 == -1` (C#'s truncated
   remainder, and Rust's `i32 %` matches it), so the first hit never fires
   вЂ” and the counter's *0* makes the **second** hit fire for every period.
   The doubling and the spawn therefore land on hits 2, 9, 16, вЂ¦ (555) and
   2, 5, 8, вЂ¦ (546), not 7/3.

### The hook order

The C# evaluates the doublings **before** `StrikeNPC`
(`Projectile.cs:13389-13396`) and the spawns **after** it
(`:13707-13809`) вЂ” and both read the same counter value on one hit. The
port folds that into `damage_pve`'s per-NPC loop: the doubling peeks
(`countUp: false`) into the `dmg` local just before
`hurt_from_projectile`, and `yoyo_on_hit` increments inside the `landed`
block. Getting these in one place is what keeps the periods aligned.

### The arms

| yoyo | effect | detail |
|---|---|---|
| 555 (TheEyeOfCthulhu) | `dmg * 2` every 7th hit | pre-strike peek |
| 546 (Chik) | `dmg * 2` every 3rd hit | pre-strike peek |
| 545 (Cascade) | spawns 1125 every 2nd hit | `damage * 2`, the `ai1` floor `dist/200` with the C#'s 208-seeded scan degenerate, the `localNPCImmunity` **-1** sentinel, the `ai[0] != -2` dropped-yoyo guard |
| 554 (Kraken) | spawns 3Г— 1135 every 4th | `damage * 0.5`, `l в€€ {-2, 0, 2}` at В±0.05 turns |
| 546 (Chik) | spawns 5Г— 1134 every 3rd | `ai0 = 1` for the four followers, the idStatic-20 stamp |
| 555 (TheEyeOfCthulhu) | spawns 1130 every 7th | `damage * 2`, 14-tile initial speed, `ai1` floor 80/200, the -1 sentinel |

The four shots carry their `SetDefaults` rows verbatim (1125:
32Г—32/aiStyle-189/`penetrate = 4`/local-immunity в€’1; 1130:
100Г—100/aiStyle-210/`timeLeft = 600`/local в€’1; 1134:
6Г—6/aiStyle-24/`penetrate = 1`/idStatic-20; 1135:
100Г—100/aiStyle-210/idStatic-10), and `AI_210_YoyoShots` ports the shared
fade lifecycle of 1130/1135: the 0.92 velocity decay, the
`MultiLerp`-driven alpha ramp (255в†’0 over 20 ticks) and the 20-tick
owner-local `Kill`.

Deviations: the counterweight on-hit spawn path (`Player.Counterweight`,
`Player.cs:12356-12415` - the yoyo-glove/counterweight scan) folds out
with the unported `yoyoGlove`/`counterWeight` grants (S1-P-i09 re-read:
the gate `!yoyoGlove && counterWeight <= 0` returns early, so the call
is a no-op until M3-EQUIP-3 lands the accessory rows); the aiStyle-99
hit arm AROUND that call (the recoil / facing / clock age / no-LOS cut
/ the dropped twin's squash+lift, `Projectile.cs:13256-13300`) IS
ported now (S1-P-i09, "The yoyo family" above); `AI_210`'s one-shot
sound and frame cycle are the render row's (the port's cue table has
no `Item20`); the spawned shots' own aiStyle-189 (1125) and aiStyle-24
(1134) families are their own tasks - the shots exist with their data,
their children-AIs do not run. The Hive-Five's bee arm
(`Projectile.cs:13699-13706`, the 1/3 `Next(3)` gate + `beeType`/

## The Old One's Army's lane spawn (M4-EVENT-18)

The etherian portal (549) is the gate every lane's monster climbs out of,
and its pick is the whole wave's spawn table вЂ” three difficulties, each a
per-wave `switch` with its own caps and rolls.

- **The gate's machine** (`AI()`'s aiStyle-106 block, `NPC.cs:40970-41047`)
  is a counter plus an idle timer. `ai[0]++` runs only while
  `!EnemySpawningIsOnHold` (the event's `_timeLeftUntilSpawningBegins`), and
  at `ai[0] >= LaneSpawnRate` the gate asks for a spawn; the 3x reset is
  written _before_ the modulo test, so the reset frame's `0 % rate == 0`
  opens an attempt too. `localAI[0]` caps at 180, and at 180 the arm either
  returns (with `dontTakeDamage = true`) while `NPC.AnyNPCs(548)` вЂ” the
  etherian crystal вЂ” stands, or flips `ai[1]`, zeroes `ai[0]` and enters the
  fade: `scale = Lerp(1, 0.05, GetLerpValue(500, 600, ai[0]))`, dying at
  `ai[0] >= 550`. The lane side rides `ai[2]` (`leftGate = ai[2] == 0`), and
  `LaneSpawnRate` is the wave's own rate вЂ” the tier-1 table's
  90/60/55/50/40, the tier-2's 90/70/60/55/50/45/42 and the tier-3's
  85/75/60/60/55/60/90.
- **The picks are three separate functions**
  (`Difficulty_1/2/3_SpawnMonsterFromGate`). Two traps mattered when porting
  them. First, the C#'s short-circuit: a branch whose _first_ condition is a
  cap check does not draw its `Main.rand.Next` at all when the cap is full,
  so the port's roll order has to match condition for condition вЂ” several
  arms had the roll hoisted ahead of the cap. Second, the `num`/`num8`/
  `num9` pair: the squire branch always spawns the squire and _also_ the
  second body on a roll (the 556 beside the 553, the 557 beside the 554),
  which `LaneSpawn` carries as `first`/`second`.
- **The bosses each have their own shape.** The Dark Mage (564, tier-1 wave
  5) rides a separate `if ((!leftGate || Next(2) == 0) && kills > required В·
  0.5 && !AnyNPCs(564))` вЂ” but the `if/else if` chain that follows it
  re-assigns `num4` whenever it fires, so the boss only survives when the
  goblins already sit at their cap. The Ogre (576, tier-2 wave 7) heads the
  chain instead. Tier-3 wave 6 runs _two independent chains_: the second
  (`:1708`) always executes and overwrites the first's pick.
- **The resolve** lives in the sim, which owns the NPC vec and therefore the
  live pool the caps count (`NPC.CountNPCS`). `FindProperDifficulty` picks
  the tier from `hardMode` / `downedMechBossAny` / `downedGolem`,
  `GetInvasionStatus` supplies the kill pair, and the pick's kinds spawn at
  the gate's bottom. The port's DD2 roster is partial вЂ” the wyvern, the
  archers, the drakes, the mystics, the ogres, the hounds, the sapper and
  the glider have no kind yet, so those picks drop out until they land
  (`nid_of`/`dd2_pool_id`).

## Yoyo string + sprite (M4-PROJ-4c)

The row's pure half is `crates/tr-app/src/yoyo_string.rs`; the draw call is
`Projectile::draw_with_hand` (frame.rs hands it the player's centre).

### The colour chain

`Main.TryApplyingPlayerStringColor` (`Main.cs:35474-35519`) is ported as
`string_color(string_color_id, disco, rainbow)` в†’ RGBA 0..1:

- the paint path (`WorldGen.paintColor` вЂ” the port's
  `tr_core::tile_light::paint_color`) with the **75-per-channel floor**
  (`:35479-35490`), which also lifts the explicit dark rows;
- the special ids 13 (20,20,20), 0/14 (200,200,200), 28 (163,116,91),
  30 (226,228,142), 27 (the animated `Main.DiscoR/G/B` вЂ” the caller's
  per-frame triple) and 29 (the rainbow: the `(mouseTextColor-190)/65` lerp
  with the `В±40` channel jitter, `:35511-35516`);
- the 0.4 alpha (`:35410`); the id-0 path's alpha comes from the caller's
  `:28038` instead, so both end at 102/255.

The itemв†’colour table is `Item.cs:30220-30255` (3293в†’1 вЂ¦ 3304в†’12, 3305в†’28,
3306в†’14, 3307в†’27, 3308в†’13) plus `Item.cs:43716`'s 30 вЂ” `string_color_for_item`.

### The walk

`string_segments(hand, target, sag_factor)` is the 12-px walk of
`Main.cs:27966-28046`: the remaining-length step (with the partial final
step), the rotation `Atan2(dy,dx) - ПЂ/2` (`:28036`), the sag bow scaled by
the remaining distance (`:27995-28035` вЂ” the speed curvature is an input
the caller folds in), and the per-segment light tint (`segment_color`'s
0.5 light multiply + the `num10` half dim, `:28043`/`:28045`).

The draw path emits one `push_sprite_origin_rot` per segment
(`render/sprite.rs`'s `origin`-anchor analogue of
`EntitySpriteDraw(origin: (W*0.5, 0))`, `:28042-28045`) and then the yoyo
sprite quad centred and rotated by the slot's `rot`/`scale`/`alpha`, with
the `FishingLine` sheet's 12-px slice as the source rectangle
(`new Rectangle(0, 0, Width, (int)num5)`).

### Deviations

- `player.stringColor` rides M3-EQUIP-3 (the accessory system): the row
  ships the id-0 white path (`A=102`) with the table ready, exactly as the
  AI row shipped `meleeSpeed = 1.0`.
- `drawLayer` 7's player-pass interleave (`Main.CacheProjDraws` +
  `PlayerDrawLayers.DrawHeldProj`, `Main.cs:22196-22202`,
  `PlayerDrawLayers.cs:4185-4235`) has no port analogue вЂ” the port has one
  projectile loop; the counterweight-before-yoyo order is encoded by the
  loop's push order, and the layer-8 counterweight-over-arm case is not
  modelled.
- `Lighting.GetColor`'s alpha behaviour (the XNA `Color(Vector3)` drops to
  255) is not reproduced: the port's `LightMap` is RGB-only and the row's
  alpha chain is explicit (documented in the module doc).
- The drawn shots' frame/sound arms and the counterweight's own string are
  the render rows' scope; `ApplicationItemPositionOffsetFromMount` is a
  mount row's input (the port has no mounts yet).

## Grappling hooks (M4-PROJ-5)

The hook family landed as a pool aiStyle-7 projectile: `grapple.rs` holds the
state machine and the tables, `ProjectilePool::update` drives it, and
PHYS-6's single-hook stand-in is retired. All 32 vanilla kinds carry a
`proj_data` row (18x18 for the Hook through 6x6 for the Skeletron Hand,
20x16 for the Worm Hook, `timeLeft *= 10` = 36000, `extraUpdates` 1 for 256
and 3 for 935).

- **The update order is the source's own.** `Main` runs players before
  projectiles, so `GrappleMovement` reads `grappling[]` written by the
  *previous* tick's pass and `Player.Update` clears it at its end
  (`Player.cs:28300-28301`). The port clears at the top of the projectile
  pass вЂ” the same one-tick latency, preserved rather than optimized away.
- **The latch scan is the source's box, not a tile under the tip.** The
  10x10 box at `Center - (5,5)` over the x-major range `[tile(Center-21),
  tile(Center+37)]`, first match wins; the position pins to
  `GetTileVisualHitbox`'s center (`:66577-66595`) and stops integrating.
- **Two fire-time tables disagree and are ported verbatim.** `QuickGrapple`'s
  `num6`/`num7` (in-flight cap and the recycle) and `AI_007`'s `num14` attach
  cap differ for 73/74, 652 and 372; and 73/74 are not symmetric with each
  other (only `num == 73` is special-cased at `:6369-6372`, so 74 keeps the
  default budget while both share the attach cap of 1).
- **The pull averages every registered hook** and takes its speed cap from
  `grappling[0]`'s type (`:22832-22851`), as the source does вЂ” a mixed set
  uses the first hook's cap, not each hook's own.
- **The Static Hook hangs the player still with no input held.** With no
  direction its contribution is the player's own center, so the pull
  collapses; the 6 px slack only engages once a direction is held.
- **The cracked-brick 1/16 break rides the hook's own `u64` stream.** The
  C# draws `Main.rand.Next(16) == 0`, whose interleaving with the other
  consumers of that global stream is not replayable in this port. The hook
  therefore owns a per-consumer stream seeded from the world seed beside
  `ambience_rng` (the house pattern) instead of sharing the item stream вЂ”
  a documented deviation, chosen so the roll is deterministic and testable.
- **PHYS-6's four wrong constants are corrected, and its tests untouched.**
  The max distance for 256 (425) and 935 (500) and the pull caps for 487
  (12) and the Lunar four (16) had been inherited as the defaults; PHYS-6's
  grapple tests pin type 13 (whose values were and stay right) and are left
  as the regression anchor, with the new values asserted separately.

S1-L-10a landed the item-driven fire and the latch blacklist:

- **The hook kind comes from the item.** `Player.QuickGrapple_GetItemToUse`
  (`Player.cs:6481-6500`) picks the grapple slot (the misc-equip 4) first and
  then the first inventory item whose `shoot` is an aiStyle-7 projectile
  (`Main.projHook`, `Main.cs:6620-6624`); the hook fires with that kind.
  The C# returns when no hook item is held (`:6320-6323`); the port keeps the
  `TR_HOOK` pin as the stand-in for the granting items (M3-EQUIP-3).
- **The latch blacklist is rebuilt on every latch.** The C#'s
  `UpdateBlacklistedTilesForGrappling` (`Player.cs:6210-6248`) puts the
  non-solid 3x3 around each attached hook into the refused set, and вЂ” when the
  hook sits on a minecart track or a platform вЂ” the track and platform tiles
  of the 5x5 around it; the latch scan refuses those tiles
  (`Projectile.cs:52699` в†’ `Player.IsBlacklistedForGrappling` `:6205-6208`).
  The port keeps the set per owner in the projectile pool and rebuilds it when
  a hook latches (`Projectile.cs:52772`).
- **`RemoveAllGrapplingHooks` is no longer "the player is not grappling".**
  The C# calls it from the jump-off (`Player.cs:22733`), the sign interaction
  (`:33379`), the minecart-hook launch (`:33557`) and the TrackHookв†’cart
  transfer (`:22675`); the port's stand-in killed every hook on every tick the
  player was unattached вЂ” which killed the hook in the tick it fired. The
  port now raises the request from the jump-off (`Player::release_grappling_hooks`)
  and the caller applies it.

S1-L-10b landed the two hand-overs:

- **The Queen Slime's hook drags the player to itself.**
  `Player.DoQueenSlimeHookTeleport` (`Player.cs:22742-22755`) walks the
  position to the hook in 150 tile-collision steps of 12 px (the direction
  runs from the player's centre to the hook) and lands the style-10
  teleport. The C# calls it from the latch of the hook type 935
  (`Projectile.cs:52773-52774`); the port calls it from the same latch.
- **The Track Hook hands the player to the minecart.**
  `Player.GrappleMovement` (`Player.cs:22659-22693`) checks the Track Hook
  (403)'s box against the player's, and over a track tile it removes the
  hooks, snaps the player onto the rail sub-column
  (`Minecart.GetOnTrack` `:1200-1241`), refuses a solid body
  (`Collision.SolidCollision`) and mounts the cart (`Mount.SetMount`) with
  the 25-spark wheel burst. The equipped cart (the misc-equip 2) wins over
  the wooden minecart (`:22676-22679`); the port reads it per tick.

S1-L-10c fixed the mount dismount's gate: `Player.GrappleMovement`
(`Player.cs:22620-22623`) and the fire edge (`:6334-6337`) dismount only a
mount **outside** `MountID.Sets.CanUseHooks` ({54, 57-60}) вЂ” the port
dismounted every mount, so a cart or a grappling mount was dropped the moment
a hook went out. The fire edge is now the C#'s own per-player latch
(`Player.releaseHook`, `:27481-27489`) instead of a process-global flag that
fired the hook for the wrong player.

Deferred to their own rows: the chain/sprite rendering and the `light` /
`projFrames[652]` animation (nothing in `render/` reads `proj_data`),
`Minecart.FrameTrack` (the track switch table needs `Tile.FrontTrack` /
`Tile.BackTrack`, which the decompile does not carry) and the net messages
(13/17/29).

### The grapple census (W3-i39, code-only — tests written NOT run)

A line-by-line re-read of `AI_007_GrapplingHooks` (`Projectile.cs:52565-52866`),
`QuickGrapple` (`Player.cs:6296-6478`), `GrappleMovement` (`:22613-22740`) and
`GetGrapplingForces` (`:22757-22856`) against the port. The hook `UseSound`
(S1-E-21f, `:6408`) is KEPT untouched. Fixes, each C#-cited:

- **`ai_hook` statement order.** The source runs: dead‖CCed kill (`:52567`) →
  rotation `atan2 − 1.57f` (`:52577`, the literal 1.57, NOT π/2) → Squirrel
  banker's quarter-turn snap (`:52581`, `Math.Round` → `round_bankers`) →
  cracked-brick `Next(16)` break (`:52583-52595`, `nactive()` gate, BEFORE the
  cap) → 2500 cap (`:52596`) → 256 `+3.9250002f` offset (`:52600`) → 652 7-tick
  frame machine (`:52615`, `projFrames[652]=6`) → the state machine. The port
  had the cap before the crack (RNG order), π/2 for the rotation, half-away
  rounding, and skipped the 256 offset + 652 frames.
- **The Fly latch scan runs on the distance-flip tick.** The scan (`:52663`)
  sits INSIDE the `ai[0]==0` block, after the distance if/else — it is NOT
  re-gated on the state, so a hook that just flipped to Retract still scans and
  can latch the same tick. The upper bound is EXCLUSIVE (`i < num8`, `:52689`).
  The port gated the scan on `ai[0]==0` after the flip (missed the same-tick
  latch) and used an inclusive bound.
- **The attached re-validation has NO blacklist.** `:52852` calls
  `CanTileBeLatchedOnTo` only; the port passed the blacklist (a blacklisted tile
  the hook sits on would wrongly detach).
- **`can_latch` reads `Tile.nactive()`** (`Tile.cs:240-247`: active bit set AND
  inactive bit clear) — an actuated solid tile is not latchable. The port checked
  `active()` only.
- **The latch dig cue** `PlaySound(0, i*16, j*16)` (`:52757`) rides the
  `UpdateProjectiles` stream (case-0 `Next(3)` + `Next(-10,11)` pitch,
  attenuation-gated) via the `wants_sound` → `pending_proj_sounds` drain.
- **The pull cap has no epsilon** (`:22852-22855`: `num8 > num9 ? num9/num8 : 1`).
  The port's `dist > 0.001` guard zeroed tiny pulls.
- **`GrappleMovement`**: `flag`/`flag2` read the PRE-pull velocity (`:22627-22628`,
  `base.wet` = ANY liquid); the jump-off gate is `flag3 && !controlUp` (`:22717`,
  NOT `!controlJump`); `GoingDownWithGrapple` is cleared per tick by
  `ResetEffects` (`:18506`) and SET only on a down pull (`:22655`). The port
  added `PlayerInput.up` / `Player.control_up` (the Confused swap `:24996-25004`
  now writes it), the carpet/wing/rocket head (`:22624-22644`), and the reset.
- **`QuickGrapple` order**: the recycle (`:6416`) reads `num7` of the ORIGINAL
  `item.shoot` BEFORE the Dual (`:6420`) / Lunar (`:6430`) kind cycles; the spawn
  reads `item.shootSpeed/damage/knockBack` (`:6413-6415`, not a hardcoded 16/0/0);
  the blacklist rebuilds at fire (`:6407`); the Lunar scan keeps the FIRST slot on
  a `timeLeft` tie (`num9 < timeLeft`, strict); the `CCed‖tongued‖dead` gate
  (`:6298`). The port cycled before recycling, hardcoded the stats, and used
  `max_by_key` (last-wins tie).
- **Hook items never fire via LMB.** `Item.SetDefaults`' epilogue
  (`Item.cs:48893-48898`) zeroes `useStyle/useTime/useAnimation` for every
  `Main.projHook[shoot]` item, so `ItemCheck_Shoot` never fires them — the hook
  launches only via `QuickGrapple` (the `controlHook` edge). The port's generic
  editing shoot path now skips aiStyle-7 projectiles.
- **`spawn_hook` centres the box** (`Projectile.cs:10876-10877`:
  `position = X − width/2`); the port passed the center as the top-left.
- **The Track Hook (403) has no distance row** (`:52648`): its Fly state never
  distance-retracts (it latches the rail it spawns on, `LaunchMinecartHook`
  `Player.cs:33553-33559`); `hook_spec(403).max_distance = ∞`.
- **The blacklist 5x5 track/platform reads have no `active()` gate**
  (`Framing.GetTileSafely` `:6230`/`:6241` reads `tile.type` directly).

RNG order: the crack `Next(16)` and the latch dig cue ride `UpdateProjectiles`
(`Main.cs:17775-17777`); the rotation/snap/frames/latch are RNG-free; the
`QuickGrapple` `UseSound` rides `UpdatePlayers` (kept from S1-E-21f). The crack
draw stays gated by `nactive() && CrackedBricks` (short-circuit), now before the
cap — the draw count per tick is unchanged for a live hook.

Deferred (out of grapple-core scope): the 446/646-649 `AddLight`/`PlotTileLine`
(`:52604-52645`, render seam), the chain rendering, the net messages, the
`oldStyleParkour` jump-height halving (`:22724`), and the
`noItems`/`cursed`/mount-`DismountOnItemUse` QuickGrapple gates (`:6326-6341`,
those player flags are unported).

#### W3-i39 retry — the second-pass census fixes (code-only, tests written NOT run)

A retry worker re-read the landed `48e3bc73` diff line-by-line against the C# and
fixed the remaining deviations (the wings-4/30 overrides moved OUT of deferred —
they landed):

- **The fire-gate `return` no longer aborts the player tick.** The port's
  `if !fire_allowed { return; }` sat inside `update_player`, so a refused budget
  skipped the rest of `Player.Update` (movement, the mount key, the pull bridge).
  The C# `return` (`Player.cs:6401`) exits `QuickGrapple` ONLY. The fire tail is
  now wrapped in the gate's positive form.
- **The mount dismount sits INSIDE the `CCed‖tongued‖dead` gate.** The port
  dismounted before the gate; the C# returns at `:6298-6301` before reaching
  `TryDismount` (`:6334-6337`), so a CCed/tongued/dead player keeps the mount.
- **`GoingDownWithGrapple` now forces platform fall-through.** The flag was
  computed but never consumed. `Player.cs:28085-28092` ORs it into `flag31`,
  which sets `fallThrough`/`ignorePlats` both true for `DryCollision`/
  `TileCollision`; `move_vanilla` now feeds it (and the pulley) into the
  collision args, and `SlopingCollision`'s `stairFall` arms on
  `ignorePlats‖controlDown‖grappling[0]>=0` (`:23679`).
- **`RemoveAllGrapplingHooks` clears the blacklist + registration.** The C#
  (`:33562-33574`) calls `ClearGrapplingBlacklist` (`:33563`) and resets
  `grappling[0] = -1; grapCount = 0` (`:33564-33565`) before the kill sweep. The
  pool's `remove_all_grappling_hooks` carries all three; the world-sim removal
  request calls it.
- **The Webbed (149) buff detaches the hooks.** `Player.cs:11880` calls
  `RemoveAllGrapplingHooks` in the webbed arm; the port raises the same
  `release_grappling_hooks` request.
- **`GrappleMovement` runs `StopVanityActions`** (`:22619` → `:33458-33463`):
  `sit_up` + `stop_sleeping` (the port carries sitting/sleeping; petting is
  unported). The wings-4/30 frame overrides (`:22633-22640`) also landed.
- **The latch recycle runs BEFORE the blacklist rebuild + Queen Slime teleport.**
  The C# order is recycle (`:52711-52754`) → `UpdateBlacklistedTilesForGrappling`
  (`:52771`) → teleport (`:52772-52775`); the port had the rebuild/teleport first.
- **The PlayerFrame centroid averages only the REGISTERED attached hooks**
  (`grappling[0..grapCount]`, `Player.cs:36497-36503`), not every aiStyle-7 slot —
  an in-flight hook does not lean the body.
- **The latch scan bounds use `ToTileCoordinates` faithfully** (`Utils.cs:1809`:
  `(int)vec >> 4`, no pre-clamp) with the upper clamped to `maxTiles` (not
  `maxTiles-1`), so the last in-bounds column is scanned; the attached
  re-validation uses the same `tile_coord`.

RNG order unchanged by the retry: the crack `Next(16)` and the latch dig cue ride
`UpdateProjectiles`; the `QuickGrapple` `UseSound` rides `UpdatePlayers` (kept).
6 new `i39_*` witnesses (the fire-gate fall-through is behavioural, witnessed via
the platform drop; the removal/blacklist/registration, webbed detach, vanity stop,
scan edge column and `tile_coord` shift).

## Thorn bushes + the wall-brick conversion tables (M5-SPREAD-2c)

The M5-SPREAD-2 row's deferred "next slice".

### The thorns

`TileID.Sets.SpreadOverground` (`TileID.cs:621`) is the gate the port's
overground arm reads; it was missing the thorn tiles 32/352 and the
golf-grass 477/492, so the arm the C# triggers on the *thorn* itself was
unreachable. With the set fixed, `:72362-72370`'s arms land: the corruption
thorn (32) grows into the corrupt grass 23 and the crimson thorn (352) into
the crimson grass 199, each at `genRand.Next(3)` вЂ” drawn only for a 32/352
cell вЂ” plus the jungle `:73658-73661`'s thorn-69 arm (no roll). The
underground twin (`:73280-73294`) stays dead code in both the C# and the
port (`Sets.SpreadUnderground` excludes 32/352).

`grow_spike` carried two deviations, both fixed:

- the "converted grass" map's sentinel was `0` (the C# `-1`); it is now
  `u16::MAX`, which is what the knife-edge `t.kind != converted` compare
  needs;
- the write replaced the whole `Tile`, zeroing the frames and the liquid;
  the C# (`:45476-45481`) sets the kind and the active bit on the existing
  tile, `CopyPaintAndCoating`s from the seed tile and runs
  `SquareTileFrame` вЂ” the port now does all three.

### The wall chains

`convert_wall_by_case` (growth/grass.rs, re-exported from growth) was the three evil types' flat
Grass/Stone/HardenedSand/Sandstone/NewWall ladder. It now carries every
conversion type's wall arm in the C#'s order: the missing `Dirt`/`Snow`/`Ice`
sets (`WallID.cs:39-41`), the glowing-mushroom set (`WallID.cs:88`), and the
0/3/5/6/7/11/12 arms вЂ” cleanse's grass-family `Next(10)` surface roll and
262/274/292-295 switch, desert's two set unions (187/216), snow's (71/40),
purify's natural-wall 349 plus its dirt/NewWall arms, jungle-mud's variant
of the same, and corruption-II's four separate NewWall guards followed by
the ebonstone fallback. `spread::convert_wall` routes through it, so the
evil callers now get the C#'s chain: the stone wall 1 converts to 3/83 (the
port's old natural-slice 3/192 was the deviation) and the dirt wall's arm
lands on the cleanse types.

### Deviations

- The torch arms (`TileID.Sets.Conversion.Torch`) of every conversion type
  are still deferred: one shared helper would cover them but they need the
  frame-x/y predicate.
- `SpecialSeedFeatures.RainbowSandAndBlackSandWalls` (the paint reset inside
  `Convert_ActuallyConvertWall`, `:56329-56343`) is not modelled вЂ” it is a
  secret-seed runtime flag.
- The `NetMessage.SendTileSquare` broadcast is not ported (single-player).
## The Old One's Army's tier-2/3 families (M4-EVENT-19)

The lane spawn table's unported members landed: the 13 kinds the D2/D3
rosters pick (the port ids 169-181), each with the vanilla row and its
machine arm.

- **The diving flyers** (`AI_108_DivingFlyer`, `NPC.cs:65392-65788`) are a
  new machine in the port вЂ” the etherian wyverns (558/559/560) and the
  kobold gliders (574/575). It is a five-state machine on `ai[0]`: the
  approach (the 500-px engage gate with the `num4 = 90` smoothing toward a
  point `num2 = 400` above the player and the `ai[3]` blocked-tick
  counter), the wind-up (20 ticks for the wyverns, 30 for the gliders, at
  0.95 damping with the gliders' `-0.1` drift), the dive (the `num11`
  homing with the `num12 Г— num11` drag вЂ” 3.0 for the wyverns, 0.5 for the
  gliders вЂ” and the 30-tick / 150-px / min-speed exits), the 45-tick
  post-dive rest and the gliders' impact. The families differ by flags not
  by numbers: the wyverns' `flag2 = false` keeps them out of the crash
  state entirely, while the gliders' `num13 = 0` means their only dive
  exits are the solid-collision and the 64-px proximity, both of which open
  the 192-box impact вЂ” an 80-damage blast, the `alpha = 255` full-box
  flash and the death at the third tick (the port's `wants_blast` intent +
  `damage_override`, read by the contact path).
- **The walkers** ride the port's `AI_107` arms: the Wither Beast T3 (569)
  is the T2's aura/self-heal вЂ” it charges at `num5 = 110` frames with the
  1.4/0.16/0.7 walk tuning and heals `lifeMax / 20` every 60 ticks; the
  Drakins (570/571) run the flag12 stand-and-shoot, where `num8 = 60`
  opens the burst, `num9` re-writes itself every 6 (571) or 9 (570) ticks
  between 10 and 40 so they fire repeatedly, and the 671 leaves from the
  22-px muzzle with the `Math.Abs(v.X) * num15` ballistic drop at 35/60;
  the Kobold walkers (572/573) are the ignite-and-explode kamikaze вЂ” the
  lit state sets `ai[1] = 1`, the 192-box blast follows on the third tick
  of `ai[1] == 2`, and the sprint's `num23 = 4` (four times the 0.88 walk)
  rides the flag5 charge arm; the Ogres (576/577) carry all three attack
  arms at once вЂ” the flag5 chase (`velocity.X *= 0.7`, the 60-tick
  cooldown), the flag3 throw (the 676 spit at 40 from the offset, the 683
  ground pound at 60) and the flag4 hop (`velocity.Y = -13` at `num = 56`),
  with `ai[1]`'s sub-state machine picking chase vs spit vs pound on the
  distance and the 300-tick `localAI[0]` chase latch.
- **The ports' roster is now complete** for the spawn tables: `nid_of` and

  Old One's Skeleton's 566/567, already ported) sit outside the spawn
  tables.

  (`High = maxTilesY`, `Low = 0`) вЂ” the deep table below three sevenths of

  && chestStyle == 10`) overlaps the port's jungle family, which keeps the

## The flail family (M4-PROJ-3b)

`AI_015_Flails` (`Projectile.cs:43724-44169`) ports as `ai_flail` in
`crates/tr-app/src/projectile.rs`, driven by the `FLAIL_PARAMS` per-kind
table (`:43761-43823`'s switch вЂ” num/num2/num5/num7/num12/num15 over the
defaults 10/24/16/48/15/30, with `num2/4/5/6/7/8/9` scaled by
`1/meleeSpeed`). The ten kinds (25/26/35/63/154/247/757/947/948/1058) ride
`DefaultToFlail` (`:10753-10762`: aiStyle 15, drawLayer 7, friendly,
`penetrate = -1`, melee, `usesLocalNPCImmunity` with cooldown 10) and the
three helpers (928 aiStyle 14 pen 2 timeLeft 250, 248 aiStyle 1, 405
aiStyle 70 pen 1 alpha 255 timeLeft 120) land rows beside them.

The state machine (`ai[0]` 0..6) runs inside one tick per
`ProjectilePool::update`; the C#'s `HandleMovement` peer is the port's
`flail_move` (the face-clamped per-axis advance with the blocked
component zeroed) followed by `ai_flail_bounce`
(`AI_015_HandleMovementCollision` `:43655-43717`), gated on the velocity
change exactly like the C# `flag` (`:17896-17904`) вЂ” without the gate the
handler's unconditional state-1 arm would stagger every fly-out tick.
The state-1 bounce's `position -= vector` undoes the whole move; the port
steps the blocked axis 1 px at a time instead of `Collision.Move`'s
sub-steps (agrees to the sub-pixel; the only numeric approximation in the
family). The throw path gains `speed /= meleeSpeed` (`Player.cs:47063`,
Г—1 at the port's default bonus) and the Flairon's 1 px aim offset
(`:47239-47245`); `Player::melee_speed()` and `Player::mounted_center()`
(`Player.cs:3335`, equal to `center()` with no mount offsets) back the
AI's reads. The `948 в†’ 947` water morph reads the mid-tile liquid kind
(the port's Player liquid-pass idiom) for `wet && !lavaWet`; the map-
fullscreen kill and the `noItems` gate have no port arms (documented).

Hit side: the held state's first 12 ticks deal nothing
(`:12448`), the state-0 hitbox is the 55-px ellipse around the owner's
mounted center with the 0.8/0.4 Y squash (`:15336-15356`, replacing the
box test), the held damage is Г—1.2 with the Blue Moon/Sunfury dual Г—0.8
(`:14447-14465`), the knockback Г—0.35 held / Г—0.5 spinning with the hit
direction from the player's center (`:13614-13619`). The atlas В§17 note
"damage Г—0.35/Г—0.5" is wrong: those are knockback multipliers (recorded
here so the row can be corrected).

Deviations (all deferred to a decor/render follow-up, none simulated):
`AI_015_Flails_Dust` (`:44399-44474`), `CreateImpactExplosion` +
`CreateImpactExplosion2_FlailTileCollision` (`:69633`/`:69774`), the
bounce's `Collision.HitTiles` Г—count (no generic projectileв†’tile seam in
the port) and `SoundEngine.PlaySound(0, вЂ¦)` (the AI has no audio
access), the `player.heldProj` / `SetDummyItemTime` / `itemRotation`
writes and `ownerHitCheck` (no consumers), the drawLayer 7 vs the 26/35
`ai[2] == 1` branch (no drawLayer consumer; `ai[2]` is only written by
the sentry-backpack tail, unreachable for flails), and the chain/string
render (cf. the yoyo string, M4-PROJ-4c). The `player.ChangeDir` writes
ride back in `FlailTick.facing` with the same-tick reads served by a
local `eff_dir` (the port's facing is run-key driven). The Flairon's
bubble cadence and jitter (`Main.rand.Next(3, 6)`, `Next(45, 65)`,
`NextDouble`) draw from the pool's rng stream вЂ” the item stream by the
yoyo convention. 22 seeded tests cover the data table, the per-kind

## The spear family (S1-P-i06)

The held-spear thrust (useStyle 5, aiStyle **19**) ports as
`crates/tr-app/src/projectile_ai_spear.rs`, driven by the dispatch arm
`AI()`'s `else if (this.aiStyle == 19)` (`Projectile.cs:25477-25480`) →
`AI_019_Spears` (`:45857-46073`). The 21 kinds (46/47/49/64/66/97/105/130/
153/212/215/218/222/342/367/368/730/877/878/879/1103) all ride
`DefaultToSpear` (`:10720-10730`: aiStyle 19, friendly, `penetrate = -1`,
`tileCollide = false`, drawLayer 7, `usesOwnerLight`, `ownerHitCheck`,
melee); their `SetDefaults` rows + the 8 sub-shot rows land in
`projectile/data.rs` (cited per field). The legacy `AI_019_Spears_Old`
(`:46222+`, the ai[0] accumulator form) has **no caller** in the 1.4.5.8
decompile — it is dead and is NOT ported; the live arm is the offset-curve
form.

The Player side spawns the spear through the GENERIC `ItemCheck_Shoot` tail
(`Player.cs:49437`, `ai0/ai1/ai2 = 0`): the aim normalized to `shootSpeed`
(`:47277-47307`), the spawn at `RotatedRelativePoint(MountedCenter)`
(`:47196`). There is **no spear-specific ai payload** — the extension is
driven by the OWNER's `itemAnimation` countdown, read each tick by the AI.
The `useStyle == 5` block (`:47349-47375`) only sets `itemRotation` (the
port's `item_rotation_for_aim`, already wired). The melee
`speed /= meleeSpeed` (`:47061-47064`) applies to every spear EXCEPT the
jousting lances 877-879, which ride
`ProjectileID.Sets.NoMeleeSpeedVelocityScaling` (`ProjectileID.cs:547`);
the shoot path's exception list now carries them (the prior comment claimed
no ported kind rode the set — corrected).

The arm: re-centre the box on the owner anchor (`:45864`), add
`velocity * spear_offset` (`:45880`), the per-kind sub-shot switch
(`:45881-45938`), the rotation `atan2(vy,vx) + π/2 + π/4`, minus π/2 when
`spriteDirection == -1` (`:45943-45947`), then `ai[0]++` and the kill at
`ai[0] >= itemAnimationMax` (`:46063-46072`) — the lances (877-879) hold
while `player.channel` (`flag3 &= !channel`). The offset curve
(`AI_019_Spears_GetSpearOffsetRelativeToPlayer` `:46075-46184`):
`num3 = max/3` (integer), `num4 = min(anim, num3)`, `num5 = anim - num4`,
the per-kind `(num6 base, num7 extend, num8 retract)` triple feeds
`num6 + num7·((max−num3)−num5) − num8·(num3−num4)`. The extension hitbox
(`:46186-46220`) exists only in the extension phase (`anim >= max/3`) and
only for 46/105/153: reach `10 + reachScale·(1/meleeSpeed)·t`, side
`10 + widthScale·t`, `t = Remap(anim, max, max/3, 0, 1)`, centred at
`Center + aimUnit·reach`.

Movement: aiStyle 19 is NOT in `UpdatePosition`'s skip list (`:20435`), so
the generic `HandleMovement` → `position += velocity` (`:20445`) runs AFTER
the AI (`:17015`) — the dispatch runs `kill_step` (the `tileCollide = false`
free-move branch) after the arm. The AI's own `velocity * offset` and the
post-AI `velocity` step are both kept, in order.

Hit side: the `ownerHitCheck` gate (`Damage_PVE_Inner` `:12637`:
`!noTileCollide && ownerHitCheck && !CanHitWithMeleeWeapon` → return) is
keyed on `SPEAR_KINDS` (the only ported ownerHitCheck family); the sight
lines (`CanHitWithMeleeWeapon` `:12400-12411`) read the owner snapshot. The
`Colliding` aiStyle-19 arm (`:15815-15843`) steps a box-sized rect from the
projectile centre toward the extension-box centre (step = max(side, 12)),
then tests the box itself; it only returns on a HIT — a miss falls through
to the base-rect test (`:15888`), so the port ORs the two.

The owner snapshot (`SpearOwner`) rides the pool's `set_spear_owner` seam
(the `set_disco`/`set_wind` setter pattern — no `update` signature churn);
`world_sim/projectiles.rs` builds it per fixed step from the live player +
the swing timers (`itemAnimation = round(app.swing·60)`, the `ticks_of`
convention). The lances' channel-hold (`SetDummyItemTime(max/3)`,
`:45941` → `Player.cs:4432-4441`) drains via `take_spear_hold` and re-arms
`app.swing`/`app.item_time` (the `FlailTick.facing` write-back precedent).

The sub-shots ride their OWN aiStyles, ported here so the spawns are not
inert: the Mushroom Spear's spore **131** (aiStyle 30 default arm

Chlorophyte Partisan's cloud **228** + the Thunder Spear's bolt **732**

`AI_001` type hook `:57062-57114`: the tile-kill probe, the localAI[1]
fade/gravity/sibling-push machine, `frame = (int)ai[1]`, the 60-px
same-kind separation scan — precomputed pool-side, the `minion_separation`
pattern; the 344 has its OWN gravity-chain arm so the generic `ai[0] >= 15`

RNG (the `UpdateProjectiles` stream, `Main.cs:17775-17777`): the
behaviour-feeding draws stay in C# order — the swordfish bone burst

The spore/cloud/bolt spawns are RNG-free cadences.

CODE-ONLY MODE: the 9 witness tests in `projectile_ai_spear.rs` are WRITTEN

## The full `PlayerFrame` chain (M2-DRAW-3, 2026-11-11)

`Player::update_frames` now ports `PlayerFrame()` (`Player.cs:35755-36647`) arm for arm
instead of the three-branch approximation (idle / air / walk) it started with. The chain
order is the vanilla `else if` ladder, and that order is the point: the item-use arm comes
BEFORE the rope/hold/shield/mount/grapple/water/air/walk arms, so a swing no longer leaks
the walk row, and the held-item rows no longer have to be patched in at draw time (the old
`apply_item_use_frame` + `frame.rs` post-pass are gone; the app feeds the same inputs in
through `player::FrameInputs` before the fixed step, beside `swing_aim`).

Legs (`:36219-36291`): the swim paddle (`swimTime > 0`, a flat `+2.0` counter with no
velocity term), the jump/fall/hang row 5 (`velocity.Y != 0 || grappling[0] > -1`) with the
three always-animated wing sets (22/28/45 inside `ShouldDrawWingsThatAreAlwaysAnimated`)
keeping row 0, the walk cycle with the slippery no-input and roller-skate
(`MountID.Sets.IsRollerSkates` = 57-60) rest-row pins and the skates' `num19 = 2f` lock at
`maxRunSpeed`, the rest row, then the Magic-Carpet (`carpetFrame >= 0`) and sandstorm
pins and the post-chain Moon Lord legs (`legs == 140`: `velocity.Y != 0 ? 5 : 0`, row 7
when `Main.OffsetsPlayerHeadgear[bodyRow].Y == 0`, row 0 for wings 22/28) and the sitting
legs (`legs == 217`) row 5.

Body (`:36312-36633`): the full useStyle table (1/0, 7, 2, 11, 9, 6, 3, 4, 8, 12, 13, 5
with the `type == 281/986` carve-out and the `gravDir`-flipped aim rows), the rope pose
(`pulleyDir == 2 ? 1 : 2`), holdStyles 1/2/3/5/7 and 4 (row 3/2/3/3/11/0 with the
`CanVisuallyHoldItem` and dry-torch gates), the raised shield row 10, the mount body row,
the grapple lean (the hooks' centroid vs the body centre в†’ rows 2/4/3), the water float row
10, the swim window (>20 в†’ 0, >10 в†’ 5, else 0), the airborne rows (sliding 3, sandstorm /
carpet 6, EOC dash 6, wings: 22/28/45 в†’ 0 and otherwise 6 rising / 6 under thrust / 5
falling, plain 5), the walk rows (`legs == 140` runs its own `|velocity.X| * 0.5` counter,
everything else copies the leg row after a `|velocity.X| * 1.5` body counter) and the rest
row 0.

The draw side needed no new offsets. The port's part tables were audited against the C#
and already match: `PlayerDrawSet.CreateCompositeData`'s front-arm switch
(`PlayerDrawSet.cs:1952-2023`), the back arm's `+2` rows (`:2034`), the
`compShoulderOverFrontArm` clears at rows 1/2/5 (`:1961,1966,1976`), the torso column-1
override at row 5 (`:1975`), `UpdateCompositeArm`'s stretch columns 7/8 (`:2246-2274`),
`GetCompositeOffset_BackArm (6,2)` / `_FrontArm (-5,0)` applied to BOTH the position and
the origin (`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:4082-4090`, `:1272-1277`) and the
`Main.OffsetsPlayerHeadgear` composite shift (`Y - 2`). The visible breakage was that the
chain fed those tables wrong rows; with the rows correct the existing tables are correct
too. `render/player_layers.rs` now reads the headgear table from `player.rs` instead of
duplicating it, and `every_row_the_frame_chain_can_emit_has_draw_tables` pins all 20 rows.
(The composite-shift SIGN was later corrected from `2 - Y` to `Y - 2` вЂ” see
"The head/torso gap" below; the row-feeding audit above was unaffected.)

Deviations, all `TODO`-flagged in the code rather than silently approximated: the inputs

## The composite arm stacks (S1-G-15, 2026-11-13)

The player's two composite arm stacks are built from the same `PlayerDrawSet`
cells, but the C# draws them in two different places, and the two places
disagree on what a chest armor replaces. The port had merged both into one
"arm stack" helper, so two layers came out missing and a third was drawn that
the vanilla never draws.

**The back arm** вЂ” `DrawPlayer_12_SkinComposite_BackArmShirt`
(`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:1260-1393`). The vanilla draws the `Players[skinVar, 5]`
under-skin layer on BOTH armor paths: with a chest armor the
`flag2 && missingArm` block paints it right behind the arm skin
(`:1294-1302`), without one the `!flag6` block paints it (`:1346-1353`).
`missingArm` is true for every body id except 83 (`PlayerDrawSet.cs:377-384`),
so the armor path is the normal one. The port dropped the layer under armor
(the `BackUnder` push was gated on `body_armor < 0`), so the armor's
under-arm art showed through where the vanilla paints the skin. The
under-shirt sleeve (`Players[8]`) and the shirt sleeve (`Players[13]`) do
live in the `!flag3` block (`:1355-1360`), so those two stay armor-only skips.

**The front arm** вЂ” `DrawPlayer_28_ArmOverItemComposite`
(`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:3576-3737`). Its armor branch paints the skin arm
(`Players[7]`) at the ARM frame (`:3611`) and the hand (`Players[9]`, `:3618`
вЂ” the `missingHand` list of `PlayerDrawSet.cs:373`) вЂ” but never a skin piece
at the SHOULDER frame: the shoulder skin only exists in the no-armor branch
(`:3670`). The port's shared stack helper painted the shoulder skin in both
cases, so a bare shoulder stripe showed through the armor.

The C#'s `i`-loop order is reproduced verbatim: `num2`/`num3`/`num4` pick the
shoulder slot, the arm slot and the skin slot out of the two passes, so row 0
(`compShoulderOverFrontArm`) gives skin arm в†’ armor arm в†’ armor shoulder, and
rows 1/2/5 give armor shoulder в†’ skin arm в†’ armor arm.

The port's armor slots are the vanilla body ids 1-4 (copper/iron/silver/gold вЂ”
the `body_slot` of the worn chest piece, `render/entities.rs:1378`); none of
them is in the `missingHand` list, so the `Players[9]` hand layer is correctly
absent for the port's armors.

### The head/torso gap (fix/player-head-torso-gap, 2026-11-18)

The composite torso/arms carry a per-body-row Y shift so the shirt follows the
head's walk bob. Every consumer computes it the same way
(`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:1217-1219` skin torso, `:1263-1265` back arm,
`:1940-1942` shirt torso, `:3579-3581` front arm):

```csharp
Vector2 vector2 = Main.OffsetsPlayerHeadgear[bodyFrame.Y / bodyFrame.Height];
vector2.Y -= 2f;
vector += vector2 * -((playerEffect & SpriteEffects.FlipVertically) != 0).ToDirectionInt();
```

`ToDirectionInt(false)` returns **-1** (`Utils.cs:2010-2017`), so for the
un-flipped player the multiplier is `+1` and the shift is
`OffsetsPlayerHeadgear.Y - 2`. The table (`Main.cs:66638-66660`) is `0` on rows
7-9/14-16 and `2` elsewhere, so the torso/arms sit **2 px UP** on those rows and
unshifted on the rest; the head and legs never shift. Those zero rows are the
walk-bob peaks where the head frame's art rides 2 px up inside its 56-px cell,
and the torso must rise with it or a background band opens under the chin.

The port computed `2 - Y` (the sign inverted), dropping the torso 2 px on the
zero rows instead of lifting it вЂ” a 2-px transparent gap between head and torso
on every bob peak (body rows 7-9/14-16), most visible mid-walk. The fix flips
`headgear_composite_shift` to `Y - 2` (`render/player_layers.rs`); the raw
`headgear_offset` (used by the held-item anchors and the Moon Lord leg rows) is
unchanged. `t2_player_frame_offsets_match_csharp` /
`t3_no_head_torso_gap` / `test_dw_1_3` / `test_dw_2_6` now pin the corrected
sign for all 20 rows. Verified with `TR_HOLD=right TR_ZOOM=2 TR_NO_BG=1`
walk screenshots: the gap frames (120/130/160/170) show a continuous
chinв†’shirt join after the fix.

**Not the sampler / not rounding.** The reported "motion blur" was the same
gap flickering as the walk cycle crossed the zero rows, not sub-pixel
smearing: the player pass already snaps every unrotated layer to an integer
screen pixel (`render/entities.rs::snap_to_screen` via `push_layers`) and the
world camera is snapped to `round(cam*zoom)/zoom` (`app/frame/draw.rs`), and
the atlas sampler is nearest (`tr-render/src/sprite.rs`, mag/min/mipmap =
`Nearest`), matching the C#'s `SamplerState.PointClamp`
(`Main.cs:2774-2784`, `Graphics/Camera.cs:44`). The C# player layers floor
their screen position with `(int)` casts / `.Floor()` (e.g.
`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:2062`, `:1939`), not `Math.Round`; the port's
integer-snapping is the equivalent crispness guarantee. A zoom-2 capture shows
uniform 2Г—2 texel blocks and a discrete ~50-color palette (no linear-filter
blend gradient), confirming the sprite is already crisp.

**The shoulders on the falling row** вЂ” `PlayerDrawSet.cs:1933-1937` reads
`ArmorIDs.Body.Sets.showsShouldersWhileJumping[body]` into `flag`, and the
body-row-5 arm of the frame switch raises `hideCompositeShoulders` when the
armor does not show its shoulders while jumping (`:1984-1987`); the flag is
cleared at `:1932` and raised for a coat (`:1940`) or a front accessory
(`:1944`) вЂ” the port has neither. The vanilla then skips the shoulder pieces
(`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:1307` the back shoulder, `:3624` the front one). None of
the port's armor ids is in `showsShouldersWhileJumping` (`ID/ArmorIDs.cs:714`),
so a worn chest armor loses its shoulders on body row 5 вЂ” the falling pose.
The port drew them on every row.

### The animation inputs that are still unreachable

The `PlayerFrame` chain is fully ported, but six of its inputs have no writer
in the port, so the poses they select can never be reached. Each row is the
C# writer, so the follow-ups can be opened without re-reading the source:

| state | C# writer | what the port is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sliding` (body row 3, `Player.cs:36552`) | `Player.WallClimbMovement` (`:21607-21706`, the set at `:21705`) and `Player.WallslideMovement` (`:21750-21840`, the sets at `:21812`/`:21825`) | the port has no `slideDir` and no `spikedBoots`; the wall slide needs the Spiked Boots accessory and the wall climb the grappling climb |
| `pulley` / `pulleyDir` (the rope pose, `Player.cs:36444-36448`) | `Player.FindPulley` (`:19644-19749`) + the update block (`:26120-26300`) | the port has no rope tiles (`WorldGen.IsRope`), so the pulley can never be found |
| `shield_raised` (body row 10, `Player.cs:36481`) | `Player.ItemCheck_ManageRightClickFeatures_ShieldRaise` (`:31706-31739`) + `TryTogglingShield` (`:31741-31764`) | the port has no `hasRaisableShield` and no shield accessory row |
| `carpet_frame` (body row 6, `Player.cs:36556`) | `Player.CarpetMovement` (`:21842-21890`) | the port has no Magic Carpet mount |
| `sand_storm` (body row 6, `Player.cs:36556`) | the Sandstorm jump chain (`:21919` sets it; `:26743`/`:26770`/`:26810` clear it) | the port has no Sandstorm in a Bottle accessory |
| `can_float_in_water` (the float pose, `Player.cs:36527`) | `Player.ShouldFloatInWater` (`:3872-3886`); writers: accessory 4404 (Floating Tube, `:13265-13268`) and buff 265 (Flamingo, `:9895-9899`); reset in `ResetEffects` (`:18332`) | the port has no accessory-effect flag table, so `should_float_in_water()` returns false (`player.rs:4361`) |

Note that `PlayerFrame` reads `accFlipper` nowhere: the flipper *pose* is
selected by `ShouldFloatInWater`, while `accFlipper` drives the movement
(`Player.cs:20637`/`:20681`) and the merman block (`:25577-25589`).

## The followup caster families (M4-PROJ-6b)

The port's remaining caster AI families land beside the PROJ-6 set (rows,
arms, shoot specials), plus the render pass: the frame state and the
frame-sliced draw, and the trails as the C#'s cheap fallback strips.

Deliberate deviations and skips:
- **The Spectre Wrath 356's spawn stays out** вЂ” the kind is item-fired by
  nobody in vanilla; it comes from the Spectre ghost armour set bonus
  (`Projectile.cs:12012-12028`'s `ghostHurt`, spawn `:12060`), which needs
  the M3-EQUIP set-bonus seam. The 59 arm itself landed, so the kind stays
  rowless-but-armed until the set bonus lands.
- **aiStyle 75/84 scoped to the Last Prism pair** вЂ” the guns (439/445/460/
  595/600/611/615/630/705/714/735/927) and the remaining hostile lasers
  (461/537/642) keep their out-of-scope status; the 633 holder and the 632
  laser run their full machines.
- **The trails are the `Main.DrawTrail` approximation, not the VertexStrip
  pipeline** вЂ” the renderer has no dynamic-geometry strip; the ported strips
  are the C#'s own fallback shape (stretched quads, the verbatim anchor and
  `rot = delta + PI/2` geometry) with the drawers' width curves and
  StripColors per segment. The true strip (the wgsl pass, the CatmullRom
  padding, the TrailCache cycle) is the render row's.
- **The drawers' shader alpha quirks are dropped** (`A /= 2`, `A /= 8`,
  `A = 0`) вЂ” they feed the VertexStrip/shaders, and verbatim they blank
  the Rainbow Rod's strip; the end fade alone drives the port's tint.
- **The Nebula arm 618's parent-follow keeps the last-seen parent position
  in `local_ai[0..2]`** вЂ” the C# reads `proj.oldPos[1]`, and the port has no
  per-slot history until Phase 7's TrailingMode rings; the arm's accel
  (`sign(delta) * 0.15`, clamp 6) and the parent-death kill are 1:1, with
  one tick of spawn slack recorded.
- **The frame-sliced and trail quads push into the ui range** like the
  ported shuriken path вЂ” the C# draws the projectiles in the world layer,
  but the port's world range is retained by the G6 cache
  (`begin_frame_keep_world`) and the yoyo merge's world-range draw sits on
  a latent staleness hole the current `WorldFrameKey` has no projectile
  input for; the unification (and the cache-key widening) is the render
  row's.
- **The `projFrames` port is an in-scope slice** вЂ” every animated followup
  kind (206/409/633 + the trail families' 34) plus the default-1 case; the
  overrides outside the ported rows (the source's ~200-entry init) default
  here exactly like the source's own init default.
- Dust/sound spawns stay skipped across the new arms (no dust or sound
  layer in the pool); the seeds' rng draws are consumed where the C# rolls
  them mid-arm, so the ported rolls land at the source's stream positions.## The in-game options window (M7-UI-4)

`IngameOptions.Draw` (`IngameOptions.cs:103-1441`) is the vanilla's in-game
settings window: a 670x480 panel (`:125-129`) split into a **left navigation
column** and a **right page of setting rows**, both animated per row.

**What landed.** The window is now the C#'s two-column shape instead of the
port's flat six-row list:

- the left column is the eight navigation rows вЂ” `Lang.menu[114]` General,
  `[210]` Interface, `[63]` Video, `[218]` Controls, `[66]` Controlsв†’keybinds,
  `[131]` Achievements, `[118]` Close Menu and `Lang.inter[35]` Save & Exit
  (`:214-330`). The `Invite Friends` row (`:257-270`) is the social-API arm and
  stays out (AGENTS.md non-goals), so `num7 + 1 = 8` slots;
- the right column carries the four pages as static tables вЂ” 17/14/15/15 rows
  (`page()`, the C#'s `:400-1441` sequential `DrawRightSide` calls). Each row
  is a `RowAct`: a header, a value bar, an on/off toggle, a multi-state cycle,
  or a `Parked` row for a vanilla setting the port does not model;
- both columns reproduce `DrawLeftSide`/`DrawRightSide` (`:1457-1504`): the row
  position is `anchor + offset * (1 + i)`, the label is **centred** on it
  (`origin 0.5, 0.5`), the tint is `Color.Lerp(Gray, White, scaleFraction)`
  with **Gold** for the selected category, and the per-row scale animates at
  `0.01`/frame in the left column (`0.7..0.8`, `:157-199`) and at
  `0.001`/frame on the right (`1.0..1.001`, `:333-390`) вЂ” including the
  culture shrink for the long translated labels (`:167-185`, `:345-357`:
  ru/pt/pl/fr shrink the left to `0.4..0.44` and pull the right column to the
  2/3 mark; German `0.55..0.6`; the It/Sp and German deltas are
  category-bound);
- the hover pass emits the vanilla's cues вЂ” `SoundEngine.PlaySound(12)` on a
  hover change (`:187`, `:191`) and `(10)` on a category click (`:222`) вЂ”
  through `App::audio` from the frame loop (`update()`, called beside
  `tick_pointer_clock`), and clears `rightLock` on the button release
  (`:385-388`);
- the value bars drag while locked (`Main.musicVolume = ...`, `:424`) and the
  geometry is the C#'s `valuePosition.X = vector3.X + vector2.X - num3/2 - 20`
  (`:437`) with the label hanging 70 px left (`vector6.X -= num`, `:417`).

**Deviations (all deliberate, each row cited in `page()`):**

> **Superseded in part by "The Settings menu layout + dead buttons
> (fix/settings-menu-layout, round 2)" below** вЂ” the parked rows of item 1
> are wired now (only the Video page's window-mode/resolution pair stays
> parked), item 3's wave-quality label and item 4's Keybinds/Save & Exit
> arms are ported, and item 5's metrics are the measured boxes. The list is
> kept as the M7-UI-4 record.

1. **Parked rows.** A vanilla row whose state the port has no field for is
   drawn dimmed and inert rather than invented: the UI scale (`:561`), the
   door-opening preference (`:644`), auto-reuse-all (`:677`), the map frame /
   health style / portrait preference / opaque tooltip box (`:751-840`), the
   window mode + resolution (`:876-910`), the cursor/border colour pickers
   (`:1075-1371`). Their settings are the named follow-ups of M7-UI-3
   (equipment/dye), M7-UI-5 (keybinds) and the window backend row.
2. **The video page's slot count.** The C# sets `num11 = 14` for the video
   category but draws 15 rows and compensates with `vector7.Y -= 2f`
   (`:362-365`); the port keeps both verbatim (`right_slots(2) == 14`,
   `right_pitch(2) - 2`).
3. **The wave-quality label.** `:1022-1036` switches on the level with a
   per-level `GameUI.*` key; the port renders `GameUI.WaveQuality` plus the
   level ordinal instead of inventing key names.
4. **Keybinds / Save & Exit.** The C# calls `IngameFancyUI.OpenKeybinds()` and
   `WorldGen.SaveAndQuit()` inline (`:252-256`, `:300-310`); the port records
   the action on `IngameOptions::pending` and closes, because the keybinding
   screen is M7-UI-5 and the quit path belongs to the front-end flow.
5. **Text metrics.** The vanilla measures with the retail font
   (`DrawBorderStringBig`); the port centres with `text::hud_text_width` and
