Observations (cave scene, the torch ring right of the centre torch, screen
row at torch height; mean-of-RGB per tile step): Retro's subtractive carry
(в€’0.04/air) out-reaches White's Г—0.9 at distance вЂ” 5..8 tiles out Retro reads
130/101/54/43 vs White 87/47/19/15 and Color 113/56/24/18; Trippy's
per-channel subtraction kills B first (8 tiles out: (36,19,0) вЂ” the RGB
fringe), matching `doColors_Mode3_Swipe`'s independent `<= 0` gates
(`:1331-1435`). White's LIGHT field is grey (the `white_engine_golden`'s
every-cell-grey assertion); the warm cast on lit dirt is the texture's own
colour under grey light вЂ” the no-bleed property is the light, not the tint.
The surface scene shows the engines' different reach: Color leaves the
sealed caves below the surface black, while the legacy engines light cave
pockets through the shafts вЂ” their `OffScreenTiles = 35` working area
(`Lighting.cs:45-56`) vs the modern engine's 28/18 padding carries sunlight
further down; both shapes are the C#'s. No engine defect found вЂ” the modes
render distinctly and match the C# expectations.

**The wave-B harness defect (fixed, not an engine change).** The first shot
matrix came out Color-identical for all four modes: `App::new` seeds
`light_mode` from `TR_LIGHT_MODE` (`mod.rs:3361`), but the boot
`apply_settings()` (`main.rs:199`) then re-read `settings.light_mode`
(the config's Color) and clobbered the pin. Fix: `apply_settings` re-reads
`env::light_mode()` first (the `TR_ZOOM`/`zoom_pinned` precedent), and
`env::light_mode` became a live read (the `TR_SUNDIAL` precedent) so the
settings-screen close path cannot drop a live pin either. Test
`s1_e_19b_light_mode_pin_survives_apply_settings` (settings_ui.rs) pins the
boot order, the repeat-apply and the no-pin config fallback.

**Post-merge re-pin (MERGER-L6, 2026-11-19).** After the sync over main's
S1-G-1 waves (vines/ropes/cracks/pylons), one shot pair per mode was re-taken
on the merged state (Г—2 SHA256-equal each; the recipe above, pristine
`Terrustaria.trwld` copy per run via `TR_WORLD`). The color-surface baseline
stayed byte-equal; the other seven shifted (2.7k-21.7k px). Investigated, not
silent: an A/B build at the pre-vine base `8ab0ede3` reproduces every old
baseline byte-exactly, and the shift bisects to the vine-strip pass
(`934e8242`, S1-G-1 wave A): `draw_tiles` now routes `VineThreads` cells to
the deferred `DrawVines` strip pass (`TileDrawing.cs:429`, `:536-545`), which
lights every segment with its OWN `Lighting.GetColor(x, i)` (`:9081`) - the
old inline draw tinted vine cells through the generic tile path (dimmer,
pre-strip approximation). The bright strips in the new shots are the C#'s
per-segment lighting; the engine behaviour is the landed, cited correction,
so the baselines are re-pinned to the merged state (the SHAs above).
MERGER-L7 re-verified one pair (white surface+cave) after the further sync
over main 5d1bd25c (E-7a/F-7b/F-9c waves): x2 SHA256-equal runs, byte-equal
to the committed baselines and the re-pinned SHAs above вЂ” no further scene
shift from those landings.

## The bestiary cursor and portrait (fix/bestiary-cursor-and-icon, 2026-11-18)

Two bugs: no mouse cursor over the bestiary, and the entity icon showed the
whole animation sheet squashed into one frame-sized box (or spilled the cell).

Cursor: the `bestiary_open` branch of `ui::draw_hud` returned before the
global `cursor::draw` tail. The C# bestiary is a fancy-UI state:
`DrawInterface_12_IngameFancyUI` (`Main.cs:46148-46158`) returns false for
it, stopping the layer loop before layer 36's cursor; `IngameFancyUI.Draw`
draws the cursor itself after the state (`IngameFancyUI.cs:220-223`,
`Main.DrawCursor(Main.DrawThickCursor())`). The fix draws the cursor inside
the bestiary branch before the early return - the same structure.

Icon: `draw_portrait` passed `(frames_x=1, frames_y=1, frame=0)` to
`draw_sheet_frame`, sampling the entire NPC animation strip as one rect.
`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.Draw` (`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.cs:194-207`) draws
`DrawNPCDirect` with the NPC's single `npc.frame`; frame geometry from
`FindFrame`/`SetFrameSize` (`:100-109`, `:185`; the division itself
`NPC.cs:66666`/`:66694` - `frame.Height = tex.Height /
Main.npcFrameCount[type]`, integer data). The fix slices frame 0 of
`frames_y = sheet_h / frame_h` rows (the `.round()` is an inverse
derivation of the integer row count, not a `Math.Round` port) and applies
the 8 px bottom inset / floater centring from `UpdatePosition` (`:112-123`).

The interim `portrait_fit` uniform scale-down stand-in is GONE
(fix/bestiary-per-npc-scale, 2026-11-18): the per-NPC
`NPCID.Sets.NPCBestiaryDrawOffset` table landed as a generated static table
(`tools/gen_bestiary_draw_offsets.py` -> `ui/bestiary_draw_offsets.rs`, 666
rows; sources `NPCID.cs:393-412` merge order + `GetRedigitEntries`
`:414-770`, `GetGroxEntries` `:772-786`, `GetLeinforsEntries` `:788-...`,
struct defaults `:15-42`). `portrait_layout` applies
Scale/PortraitScale/Position/PortraitPositionX-YOverride/Frame per
`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.cs:52-82` + `UpdatePosition` `:112-123` (floor
included); the 68 px inner box clips via `SpriteRenderer::push_clip`
(`UIBestiaryEntryButton.cs:30-38` `OverflowHidden`, the info-page card the
same per `UIBestiaryNPCEntryPortrait.cs:20-28` with `isPortrait: true`
`:56`). `CustomTexturePath` portraits (`UI/Bestiary/NPCs/NPC_*`, 25 ids)
are packed in `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` and drawn centred per `:197-201`.
`Rotation` rides `push_ui_sprite_rot` about the frame centre
(`DrawNPCDirect`'s centre-origin draw). Remaining approximation: the
`Direction`/`SpriteDirection` horizontal flip (`Main.cs:23123-23127`,
default -1) is not modelled вЂ” the UI pipeline has no flip seam yet; the
`Velocity`-driven hover animation is likewise still frame 0 at rest
(faithful for the idle icon, `Velocity` rows animate only while hovered).

## Save & Exit was a no-op (fix/settings-menu-layout, 2026-11-18)

The Settings menu's Save & Exit row armed `pending = Some(SaveAndExit)` then
called `close()`, which clears `pending` (`ingame_options.rs`); no caller
ever drained it, so the button only closed the window. The C# row
(`IngameOptions.cs:296-305`) does `Close()` + `menuMode = 10` +
`gameMenu = true` + `WorldGen.SaveAndQuit()`; `SaveAndQuit`
(`WorldGen.cs:6701-6719`) plays sound 11, resets the invasion bar
(`:6705-6708`) and queues `SaveAndQuitCallBack` (:6664-6687`:
`Player.SavePlayer` + `WorldFile.SaveWorld` on the `netMode == 0` arm,
sound 10, fast-forward flags cleared, `menuMode = 0`).

The fix wires the row to `App::save_and_quit` (`saveglue.rs`): sound 11 ->
invasion reset -> the existing `save_world` funnel (world + player sidecar +
map + achievements) -> sound 10 -> fast-forward flags -> reopen the main menu
(the `net_disconnect` shape). Deliberate deviation: the C# mode-10 "saving"
screen exists only to cover the ThreadPool async save; the port's synchronous
single-player save has no window to cover, so mode 10 is skipped (documented
in the fn's doc comment, alongside the unmodelled `StopTrackedSounds` /
`ResetFocus` halves covered by the `game_menu` audio listener). The
multiplayer `netMode == 0` gate + force-disconnect arm is out of scope until
the MP pause-menu flow lands. The Settings panel layout deviations remain a
follow-up round.

## The Settings menu layout + dead buttons (fix/settings-menu-layout, round 2)

The window's geometry and several rows were still the port's own invention
after M7-UI-4/4b. This round ports them to the C# constants
(`IngameOptions.cs` unless noted) and wires every row whose backing feature
the port already has.

**Layout corrections (the misplaced panel contents):**

1. **Left pitch** вЂ” `vector5.Y = (480 - 100) / (num7 + 1) = 380 / 8 = 47.5`
   (`:181`, `num7 = 7` without the social invite row). The port divided by
   `LEFT_SLOTS + 1 = 9` (42.2 px), compressing the column and lifting every
   row off its vanilla position. Fixed: `left_pitch() = 380 / LEFT_SLOTS`.
2. **Left hit boxes** вЂ” `DrawLeftSide` hit-tests the *measured string box
   centred on the anchor* (`:1470`); the port's rect started **at** the
   anchor and extended 120 px right, so the left half of every label was
   unclickable and the right half of the column swallowed clicks that
   belong to no row. Fixed: `left_row_rect` measures the DeathText label at
   the row's scale and centres it, with the C#'s int truncations.
3. **Left column font** вЂ” `DrawBorderStringBig` draws **DeathText** with the
   3x3 black ring (`Utils.cs:2520-2536`); the port drew the MouseText font
   with no border. Fixed (`centred_big_text`).
4. **Right labels** вЂ” `DrawBorderStringMeasured` carries ChatManager's
   four-way shadow at `spread = 1.5f` (`Utils.cs:2506`); the port drew flat
   text. The per-row scale multipliers are now ported: zoom 0.85 (`:519`),
   UI scale 0.75 (`:561`), map scale 0.85 (`:766`), lock-on/smart rows 0.9
   (`:1372-1399`).
5. **Value bars** вЂ” the window draws every `DrawValueBar` at `scale = 0.75f`
   (`:116`), not the menu screens' 1.0; the track is 133x12 (int-truncated
   178x16 * 0.75) and its centre is the row anchor's Y **minus 3**
   (`valuePosition.Y -= 3f`, `:417`). The port drew full-size bars centred
   on the raw anchor. Fixed: `sliders::value_bar_rects_at` /
   `draw_value_bar_at` carry the scale; `bar_center_y` the -3.
6. **Hover/lock state machine** вЂ” the C# steps the scales off the *previous*
   frame's hover, keeps the **selected** category's left row at the plateau
   (`(leftHover == j) | flag6`, `:194`), re-arms `rightLock` from the hover
   at the end of every Draw (`:1409-1412`) and gates the bar write on
   `!notBar` (a label/band hover must not drag the bar, `:409-412`). The
   port now models `notBar`, the selected-row plateau, the wide hover band
   (`:427-434`) and the end-of-draw lock re-arm; the bar's value write moved
   from the click to the held-drag tick (`:422-425`), so a click on a bar
   label no longer zeroes the value.
7. **Settings apply** вЂ” the options clicks wrote `App.settings` but never
   ran `apply_settings`, so zoom/lighting/quality changes did not reach the
   renderer (`App.zoom`/`App.light_mode`). Every mutating click and the bar
   drag now apply, like the menu's close does.
8. **The bar drag's held-button source** вЂ” `frame_head` fed
   `pointer.left_held()` (the front-end pointer machine, which only tracks
   the 888 screens' presses) into the window's drag, so in-world the button
   never read as held and the bars could not be dragged at all. The C# reads
   `Main.mouseLeft` вЂ” the physical button, the port's `mine_down`
   (`app/frame.rs`).

**Rows wired (were dead or wrong):**

**Still parked (deliberate, the backing feature is unported):** the Video
page's **Go Fullscreen/Windowed** (`:876-884`, `Main.ToggleFullScreen`) and
**Resolution** (`:885-910`, `Main.SetResolution`) rows вЂ” the port has no
display-mode/resolution switch (the window backend row). They draw dimmed
and inert, exactly as before.

**Test-harness fix:** the process-global `LanguageManager` was mutated and
read by tests without a consistent `test_lock` discipline, so a culture
reload in one test could land between another test's registration and its
assertions (bare keys mid-reload) вЂ” the source of the flaky
`s1_e_20_the_hover_name_carries_the_affix_and_the_stack` and options-label
failures. `lang::test_register_source` now loads the shipped sources first
when the manager is empty (a partial fragment could become the *only*
registered file, since `lang::init` early-returns on a non-empty source list)
and documents that the **caller holds `test_lock`** for the whole test (the
lock is not reentrant); the tooltip/buff-tooltip registration tests and
`npc_chat::init_lang` now take the guard.

**Follow-up (fix/ingame-options-culture-flake):** five more
`ui/ingame_options.rs` tests still read the culture without the guard вЂ”
`the_value_bar_geometry_is_the_c_sharp_scaled_track` (the 1045-vs-979 flake:
`color_bar_right_x` shifts 60 px in English but 126 in the long cultures,
`IngameOptions.cs:1071`), `refresh_button_latches_the_hover_and_the_layout`
(`measure_button` reads `Lang.inter[62]`),
`save_and_exit_click_saves_the_world_and_returns_to_the_menu`,
`the_keybinds_row_opens_the_in_game_keybinding_screen` (culture-shifted
`left_row_rect`) and `a_toggle_click_applies_the_setting_to_the_app`
(`right_row_rect`). Under parallel load a sibling's `lang::init`/
`set_language` flipped the culture between their geometry reads and their
assertions. Each now takes the same house guard вЂ” `crate::lang::test_lock()`
acquired **once** at the top of the test (never twice: the mutex is
non-reentrant and a double acquire self-deadlocks the whole gate) plus
`lang::init(GameCulture::English)` to pin the culture for the test's whole
run. The six previously-guarded tests that used a bare
`lang::set_language(English)` were switched to `lang::init(English)` under
the same single guard: on an empty manager `set_language` marks the culture
active **without loading any sources**, and every later `init` then
early-returns in its trailing `set_language` (culture unchanged,
`localization/mod.rs:196-200`), leaving all texts as bare keys for the rest
of the process вЂ” the second half of the flake (only the tests asserting
real key resolution failed; bare-key-vs-bare-key comparisons passed
vacuously, and `--test-threads=1` passed because an `init` test happened to
run first). No game logic or value-bar maths changed вЂ” test synchronization
only.

**Verification.** 11 new unit tests: the left anchors/pitch (47.5) and the
centred hit box, the per-category right anchors + bar shift, the 0.75 bar
geometry (133x12, the -3 centre, the 60 px colour offset), the per-row draw
scales, the Interface/Controls wiring, the map-scale round trip, the colour
bars' HSL round trips + floors, the new cycles' ladders, the Keybinds
clickв†’screen mapping and the toggle clickв†’`apply_settings` path; the stale
pitch/label expectations were corrected to the C# values.

## The C#-written golden fixture (S1-J-3)

`assets/test/golden.wld` (3666 bytes) and `assets/test/golden.plr` (3840 bytes)
are written by the **real decompiled save path** through
`tools/WldFixtureHarness`: `extract.ps1` slices the save-path method bodies
verbatim out of `decompiled/` (`WorldFile.SetTempToOngoing` +
`SaveWorld_Version2` and every section writer, `WorldFile.cs:1040-1758`;
`Player.Serialize`, `Player.cs:54750+`; `Tile`, `TileEntity.Write` + the
per-kind `WriteExtraData`, the bestiary/creative/town/banner/DD2/spawn/treetops
`Save` bodies, `Item.Serialize`), and `Program.cs` builds the smallest real
world вЂ” a fixed 40x30 tile array, every value a literal, no genRand вЂ” plus a
fresh player. The shims (`Shims/*.cs`) carry only the global statics the bodies
read, at the C# types/defaults; no serialization logic is reimplemented.

**The one substitution:** `DateTime.UtcNow` -> `FixtureClock.UtcNow` (pinned
2026-11-18T00:00:00Z). The vanilla writers stamp the wall clock
(`SaveWorldFlags:1251`, `Player.Serialize:54909`); a reproducible fixture
cannot carry it. Everything else is byte-for-byte the decompiled body. The
importance bitmap is parsed from the real `Main.cs` at runtime (direct
assignments + for-loop ranges + `AddEchoFurnitureTile`), not transcribed.
Regen: `powershell -File tools/WldFixtureHarness/extract.ps1` then
`dotnet run --project tools/WldFixtureHarness -- assets/test`; two runs are
byte-identical.

**Byte-compare result** (`s1_j_3_*` in `wld/mod.rs`, `player_file.rs`):
- The port decodes every section of the fixture (all eleven pointers land
  exactly; the app-side fix-ups keep 2 signs, 11 tile entities, 2 plates).
- Re-write is **byte-identical for sections 2..10** (tiles, chests, signs,
  NPCs, tile entities, pressure plates, town rooms, bestiary, creative powers)
  **and the footer**; the prologue framing + importance bitmap match with the
  pointer table zeroed.
- The header/flags block diverges in **exactly four unowned spots**, pinned
  field-by-field (`s1_j_3_the_header_flags_divergences_are_exactly_the_unowned_fields`):
  the banner kill/claimable counts (`killCount[1]`/`claimable[1]`, no `.wld`
  store), the tree-top variations (`treeTop[0]`, no store) and the world-gen
  manifest JSON (`manifest`, the port writes the empty string). These are
  documented divergences, not faked parity. **S1-J-3b closed the rest** (see
  the next subsection): `CreationTime`, the file-faithful `spawnTileY`, the
  seven ore tiers, the saved-NPC flags, the angler quest index, the
  cultist/Moon Lord/Queen Slime kills, the tower downeds/actives + apocalypse
  phase (with the load-time shield restore) and the party-girl/princess
  spawn unlocks.
- The `.plr` fixture exposed a real reader bug: `FILE_TYPE_PLAYER` was 1
  (`Map`) where `FileType.cs:8` says `Player = 3` вЂ” every real vanilla
  character was rejected with `WrongFileType`. Fixed (read parity); the `.plr`
  writer's own byte parity stays S1-J-5's.
- **S1-J-5c envelope fix**: the harness itself zero-padded the `.plr` with
  `PaddingMode.None` (mirroring the *read* path's `Player.cs:55074`); the
  vanilla *write* path uses the bare `RijndaelManaged`'s default **PKCS7**
  (`:54734-54742`). The harness now encrypts with `PaddingMode.PKCS7` and
  `golden.plr` was regenerated вЂ” same 3840 bytes, the last block now
  decrypts to 3 data bytes + 13 Г— 0x0D. `golden.wld` is unchanged
  (byte-identical regen). The port's writer is byte-identical to the
  regenerated fixture end-to-end (see "The `.plr` legacy-subset shim +
  default policy", increment 3).

## The worldgen parity proof (S1-A-7)

`ROADMAP` S1-A-7 asks for a comparison against a **C#-generated world**, not the
self-consistency replay (`generation_is_reproducible_for_a_seed`). The obstacle is
the deliberate stream divergence (research/35 #5): the port's worldgen draws
**xorshift64** per-pass streams (`Rng(seed ^ fnv(pass_name))`) where vanilla draws
one **Knuth subtractive `UnifiedRandom`** (`WorldGen.genRand => Main.rand`,
`WorldGen.cs:4445`, re-seeded `new UnifiedRandom(worldSeed)` per pass,
`WorldGenerator.cs:497`). A full generated world is therefore **not** byte-comparable
with a C# one by design вЂ” comparing them would only re-prove the known divergence.

**What is provable is the algorithm.** `tools/WorldGenParityHarness` extracts the
verbatim C# `WorldGen.TileRunner` (`WorldGen.cs:76770-77142`) + `PlaceWall`
(`:75125`) + `CanBeClearedDuringGeneration` (`:80168`) with **zero** substitutions
(`extract.py`), shims only the global statics, and runs them in two modes:

- **DIFF** вЂ” `genRand` replays the **port's** xorshift64 stream (state passed in).
  The verbatim C# walker then draws the same sequence as the port's `tile_runner`,
  so the two tile arrays are comparable. The Rust test
  `s1_a_7_the_tile_runner_matches_the_csharp_differential`
  (`worldgen/tile_runner.rs`) replays the same 6-call scenario on a 200Г—400
  all-stone world (ore placement over a protection zoo, a single-step ore disc,
  kind-59 mud with the stone draw + liquid clear, type -2 liquid fill, type -1
  carve, and the mud-wall lining) and compares **all 80 000 tiles field-by-field**
  (kind, wall, liquid, active, slope, half-brick, lava/honey/shimmer) **plus the
  final stream state** against the C# dump (`assets/test/parity_tiles.bin`). The
  initial state is pinned to `Xorshift64::from_seed(42).0` and the final state to
  the harness's `portState`, so a draw-order or algorithm divergence trips the test.
- **REAL** вЂ” `genRand` is the real Knuth `UnifiedRandom(42)`. The `.wld` it writes
  (`assets/test/parity_real.wld`) is a **genuine C#-generated world**. The test
  `s1_a_7_the_csharp_generated_world_decodes_and_rewrites_tiles` (`wld/mod.rs`)
  proves the port decodes every section and re-writes the **tile section
  byte-identical** (the tile codec is stream-independent вЂ” S1-J-3 proved the same
  for the golden fixture).

**Scope / divergences (documented, not faked):**
- The scenario uses only branches the port has ported. Excluded (the port's
  unported arms, `tile_runner.rs` module doc): the 367/368 shell wall placements
  (`WorldGen.cs:76914-76921`), the `case 53` underground-desert containment
  (`GenVars.UndergroundDesertLocation`, `:76934`), and the remix `oceanDepths` lava
  split (`:76899-76905`). The shim's empty `UndergroundDesertLocation` and
  `oceanDepths => false` match the port's deferral exactly.
- `SquareWallFrame` (`:80198`) is a **no-op on both sides** вЂ” a visual wall-framing
  pass the port defers (`place_wall` doc); wall frames are runtime-only and never
  serialized, so the comparison stays on saved fields.
- The **stream** divergence (xorshift64 vs Knuth) is factored out by the DIFF mode
  so the algorithm can be proven; the REAL world is the genuine C# output and is
  **not** claimed byte-equal to the port's generator. Full-world byte parity stays
  open and is A1-gated (it requires moving the passes onto the single Knuth
  `genRand` stream вЂ” S1-K-1's interleave half).

Regen: `python tools/WorldGenParityHarness/extract.py` then
`dotnet run --project tools/WorldGenParityHarness -- assets/test diff 13679457532755275413`
(the DIFF state) and `... real 42` (the REAL world). See the harness README.

## The pylon/trophy/void-lens passes (S1-G-1 wave D, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/pylons.rs` ports three of
`TileDrawing.PostDrawTiles(solidLayer: false)`'s deferred families
(`TileDrawing.cs:414-434`, draw order `:423-425`): `DrawTeleportationPylons`
(`:8639-8706`), `DrawMasterTrophies` (`:8597-8637`) and `DrawVoidLenses`
(`:8708-8736` + `VoidLensHelper.cs:11-105`). The collectors take the special
point's tile coords (the classification switch's gates, `:695-712`: pylon 597
`frameX % 54 == 0 && frameY == 0`, trophy 617 `frameX % 54 == 0 && frameY % 72
== 0`, lens 491 `frameX == 18 && frameY == 18`) and produce world-pixel sprite
records; the hook scans the view rect row-major and pushes them into the
always-rebuilt world-effect range. The colour math is XNA `Color` semantics вЂ”
every `Lerp`/`operator*` step truncates to bytes (`scale_bytes`/`lerp_bytes`),
including the alpha (`value3 * 0.7f` scales A 255 -> 178); the tests pin the
per-step truncation (`s1_g_1d_the_byte_math_truncates_per_step`). The lens's
`Lighting.AddLight(position, 0.4, 0.2, 0.9)` (`VoidLensHelper.cs:36`) lands in
the shared `EntityLights` pair behind `!Main.gamePaused`
(`TileDrawing.cs:8717-8720`), so the engine reads it one frame late like the
item/NPC feeds.

Deliberate deviations:

* **Z-order + range.** In the vanilla the three passes draw between the
  non-solid and solid tile layers (`Main.cs:63374` -> `PostDrawTiles`), inside
  the tile render targets. The port's fused tile pass has no layer seam, so
  the sprites ride the screen-space fx range (like the leaf gores) after the
  cached world range вЂ” the same documented z-order approximation the inline
  grass sway uses (`tiles.rs`). This keeps the G6 `WorldFrameKey` and the
  cached range untouched; the sprites animate per frame in the always-rebuilt
  range instead.
* **Dust rolls skipped.** `TeleportPylonsSystem.SpawnInWorldDust`
  (`TileDrawing.cs:8669-8673`, two `_rand.Next` draws) and
  `VoidLensHelper.SpawnVoidLensDust` (`VoidLensHelper.cs:40-75`, `Main.rand`)
  belong to the unported particle pass. Skipping them wholesale leaves both
  RNG streams untouched (the `entity_lights.rs` rule).
* **Frame counters.** `Main.tileFrameCounter[597]` wraps at 64 and `[491]` at
  40 (`Main.cs:19284-19287`/`:19227-19230`, `AnimateTiles`); the animator is
  unported (`drawdata.rs`'s `tile_frame в‰Ў 0`), so the pass stands them in with
  `game_update_count % 64` / `% 40` вЂ” same cadence and wrap, phase anchored at
  world load.
* **Smart cursor.** The selection-glow arms are ported
  (`Colors.GetSelectionGlowColor`, `Colors.cs:89-92`, integer halves/thirds;
  the pylon's column-2 mask and the lens's `Extra_93`), but
  `Main.InSmartCursorHighlightArea` is unported вЂ” the hook feeds
  `selection_mode = 0`.
* **Registry.** The `_specialPositions` deferred registry is not ported; the
  hook re-scans the view rect (the collection order is row-major, matching
  `Draw`'s loop). The pylon/trophy visibility gate reads the bottom-right cell
  `(x+1, y+1)` through `IsVisible` (`:1411-1432`) exactly, including the
  Echo-coating flag (`World::invisible_block`) and `TR_SHOW_INVISIBLE`.

Sheets: `Extra_181` (pylon, 14x8 frames), `Extra_198` (trophy, 1x28),
`Extra_93` (lens selection mask) join `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES`; `Projectile_734`
(the lens sprite, 1x8) is packed outside `spawnable_kinds`
(`VoidLensHelper.cs:79-80` loads it directly). Tests: 8 `s1_g_1d_*` per-pass
tests in `render/pylons.rs` (gates, bob/ring geometry, byte colours, flip,
lens frame cadence, light anchor, selection tints).

## The tile-crack overlay (S1-G-1 wave C, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/tile_cracks.rs` ports `Main.DrawTileCracks`
(`Main.cs:61533-61626`) 1:1: the book-type filter + the `<20` damage floor
(`:61543-61551`), `WorldGen.InWorld` fluff-0 (`WorldGen.cs:9688-9695`), the
active-block/wall visibility arms (`:61558-61566`), the door/solid/solid-top/
tree/glowing-mushroom shape classification (`:61571-61598`, the 22 px tree
frame windows verbatim), the slope/half-brick skip (`:61599`), the
20/40/60/80 damage ladder (`:61601-61617`), the `crackStyle*18` /
`(4+crackStyle/2)*18` source rects on the 18 px grid (`:61618-61622`) and the
`Lighting.GetColor` tint at `x*16-(int)screenPosition.X` (`:61623`). The draw
sites are `TileDrawing.cs:732-733` (`hitReplace` then `hitTile`, crack type 1)
and `WallDrawing.cs:203-204` (crack type 2). The `TileCracks` sheet joins the
static atlas loads (`assets.rs`, the `WiresNew`/`Actuator` seam) вЂ” one atlas,
one pipeline, unchanged.

Deviations (deliberate):
- **Single-accumulator projection.** The C# keeps 500-entry `hitTile` /
  `hitReplace` books with per-hit `AddDamage` steps and 60-tick TTL decay
  (`HitTile.cs`). The port's mining is one `mine_target` + `mine_timer`
  accumulator (`world_sim/editing.rs`); `mining_crack_record` maps it linearly
  onto the C# 0..100 damage (`mine_timer / mine_hardness * 100`, truncated
  like the int accumulator). At most one crack draws at a time; `hitReplace`
  draws nothing until replacement mining lands. The wall arm already emits
  `CRACK_WALL` records when the mined cell has no active block.
- **World-seeded crack style.** `HitTileObject.Clear` rolls
  `rand.Next(4)` re-rolled against the static `lastCrack` (`HitTile.cs:40-45`)
  from a `DateTime.Now.Ticks`-seeded stream. The port keeps the roll + the
  no-repeat loop verbatim but seeds `App.mine_crack_rng` with the world seed
  (the determinism rule, same deviation class as `NamedRngs::global`). The
  roll fires once per dig target (the C# rolls on slot reuse).
- **Invisible-block conjuncts vacuous.** `ShouldShowInvisibleBlocksAndWalls`
  (`Main.cs:58023-58030`) reads the echo monolith / `CanSeeInvisibleBlocks`;
  neither exists in the port and `Tile` carries no invisible bits, so the
  `(flag || !invisibleвЂ¦)` conjuncts are always true.
- **Draw site.** The C# draws inside the solid tile layer; the port hooks the
  per-frame world range right after the cached tile pass (`frame/draw.rs`) вЂ”
  the damage timer advances every frame, so the crack cannot ride the
  G6-cached range. The `WorldFrameKey` is untouched; the existing tile draw
  order and framing are unchanged.
- The C#'s `type == 72` arm (`:61591`) is kept verbatim but unreachable: 72 is
  in `TileID.Sets.IsATreeTrunk` (bits 71-77), so the tree arm claims it first.

Tests: `s1_g_1c_*` (7) вЂ” the damage ladder, the 18 px rects + tree column
shift, the shape classification (incl. every tree exclusion window), the
no-repeat style roll + seed determinism, the timerв†’damage projection, the
full per-record draw-gate walk (`crack_draw_plan`) and the hook's one-record
projection.

## The combat accessory dedupe/wiring (S1-C-12 wave E, 2026-11-19, code-only)

Wave B landed `accessory_combat.rs` UNWIRED while wave A's
`apply_equip_functional` carried verbatim INLINE arms for ten of the family's
kinds — naively calling the hook would DOUBLE-GRANT. Wave E dedupes to a
single grant path per row (code-only mode — no compiler invoked; tests
written, not run):

1. **Per-slot family**: `apply_equip_functional` now calls
   `accessory_combat::apply_combat_accessory(kind, self)` FIRST and returns
   when it claims the kind; the ten inline arms (489/490/491/2998/935/897/
   936/1343/1301/3015) are DELETED from the match. The C# rows are
   independent per-type `if`s (`Player.cs:14368-15450`), and the family
   kinds are disjoint from every remaining match arm, so claiming before
   the match is order-identical. The family gains what the inline arms
   missed: `kbGlove = true` on 897/936/1343 (`:15301/:15371/:15308`) and
   the two previously-absent kinds 3992 (Berserker's Glove, `:14411-14417`)
   and 3016 (Flesh Knuckles, aggro-only, `:14647-14650`).
2. **Wave-B parity fix found by the wave-E re-read**: the module's
   Berserker's Glove arm copied the Mechanical Glove's `meleeDamage +=
   0.12f` — the C# switch arm `:14411-14417` has NO meleeDamage row
   (kbGlove/autoReuseGlove/meleeScaleGlove/meleeSpeed/aggro only). Removed;
   the module test now pins `melee_damage == 1.0` for 3992.
3. **Sky-stone bundle**: the inline flag scan + stat fold in `player.rs`
   are replaced by `accessory_combat::set_sky_stone_flag` /
   `apply_sky_stone_effects` (ONE path). The fold now includes the C#
   `minionKB += 0.5f` (`:13002`) the inline copy omitted; its `lifeRegen
   += 2` half (`:12991`) keeps riding the existing `accessory_life_regen`
   fold. Flag timing is unchanged (scan before `update_equips`, fold at
   the same site).
4. **Per-tick clears the wired grants need** (without them the new rows
   would accumulate/stick): `minion_kb = 0.0` (`ResetEffects`
   `Player.cs:18347`) and `kb_glove = false` (`:18709`) added beside the
   crit-base resets in `player.rs`. `minion_kb` had NO reset before
   (only spawn-zeroed); no live producer existed until this wave — the
   field's consumer is the summon tooltip's knockback line
   (`ui/tooltip.rs:344`, `Main.cs:20749-20798`); `buff_effects_misc.rs`'s
   minion_kb is its own effect struct, not this field.
   `autoReuseGlove`/`meleeScaleGlove` (`:18710-18711`) still have no port
   fields.
5. **Naming fix**: the `player.rs` test comment calling 1301 "Necromantic
   Scroll" is corrected — 1301 is `ItemID.DestroyerEmblem`
   (`ItemID.cs:4285`); the Necromantic Scroll is 1845 (`:5373`).

Dedupe proof (tests-as-code): `player.rs::
each_combat_accessory_grants_exactly_once_through_the_wired_seam` pins the
FULL row set (4 damage classes, 3 crits, melee-speed bonus, kbGlove) for
each of the 12 family kinds through a real `Player::update` tick, re-ticks
(a second grant path would drift tick 2), unequips (the per-tick clears

not double). `the_sky_stone_bundle_grants_once_including_minion_knockback`

together, and the unequip decay. The module's 10 wave-B tests stay green

(the tooltip's melee-knockback line, `ui/tooltip.rs:330`), the bundle adds

standing documented-skipped halves are unchanged (aggro/autoReuseGlove/

roots are collected in draw-area row-major order, deduplicated like
`_vineRootsPositions`, and the strips draw right after the foliage pass - the
C# `PostDrawTiles` order `DrawTrees` -> `DrawVines` (`:428-429`). The strip
maths is term-for-term: the unclamped `Lerp(0.2, 1, |wind|/1.2)` factor, the
`-0.08*num3` rotation ladder (+0.0025 at num2>=2, +0.0075*num3 at num2>=5,
the wall probe incrementing num2 BEFORE the rotation), the remix-flipped
surface gate, the `GetWindGridPush(x, i, 20, 0.01)` subtract/-0.78-bounce
accumulator, the `(rot + PI/2).ToRotationVector2()*16` anchor walk, the
`(tileWidth/2, halfBrickHeight - tileTop)` origin and the case-638
`GlowMask[327]` glowmask (`Color.Lerp(White, tileLight, 0.75)`, `:6080-6084`,
sheet now packed). `_vineWindCounter` (`:375`) rides the sunflower's 60 Hz
step. The G6 key mixes the vine counter into the existing windy-anim slot and
adds the `WindGrid` clock ONLY when a vine thread is in the view rect (the
push decays on the grid clock even in calm air; vine-free worlds keep the
old cache behaviour bit-for-bit).

## The NPC aiStyle dispatch axis (S1-D-2, 2026-11-18)

The C# dispatches NPC AI on `aiStyle` first (`NPC.AI`, `NPC.cs:19819-41132`:
the `if (this.aiStyle == N)` chain of 128 arms), then on `this.type` inside
the family arm. The port dispatched on `NpcKind` alone (research/25 finding
9, research/39 rank 9) - a style could not be ported once for all its kinds.

**The seam.** `NpcKind::ai_style()` (`npc.rs`) is the first axis: a 199-row
table mapping every ported kind to its vanilla `SetDefaults` aiStyle, each
group cited to the `this.aiStyle = N;` lines (extracted mechanically from
the decompile - the compound `this.type` conditions evaluated per id, not
copied from the doc comments). `update_rng` now runs
`match self.kind.ai_style()`: a claimed style enters its family arm, every
other style falls through to `update_kind_ai` - the pre-axis `match
self.kind`, moved verbatim (no arm reordering, no body edits). The buff
block, `find_frame` and `contact` keep their exact positions around the
dispatch, so the fixed-step order and every RNG draw are unchanged.

**The first migrated family: aiStyle 5** (`AI_005_EaterOfSouls`,
`NPC.cs:20802-20806` -> `:50244-50700`). `ai_005_hover_family` carries the
four ported style-5 kinds - the Eater of Souls (6), the Hornet (42), the
Meteor Head (23) and the Servant of Cthulhu (5, its own type-5 branch from
S1-D-3k) - calling the same `update_hover`/servant machines with the same
params as the old kind arms. The old kind-match arms for these four are
`unreachable!` markers (the axis claims style 5 first); D-3 rounds shrink
`update_kind_ai` the same way, one family per round. No new arms ported.

**Proof.** `s1_d_2_tests::s1_d_2_the_style_axis_keeps_the_hover_behaviour`
runs all four kinds 300 ticks through the axis vs the verbatim pre-axis
arm bodies on cloned state with identical RNG seeds and asserts bit-equal
x/y/vx/vy/frame/frame_counter/rotation/sprite_dir/facing/on_ground and
player hp every tick.
`s1_d_2_the_ai_style_table_matches_the_csharp_set_defaults` pins 86
representative rows against the C# (the full 199-row table is cited
in-place). The world-hash pins and the existing NPC AI tests pass
unchanged (`cargo test --workspace -- --skip migrates_version_2_kinds_to_item_ids`).

**Known doc-vs-C# drift surfaced by the extraction** (the table follows the
C#, not the comments): the Retinazer's SetDefaults row is aiStyle 30
(`NPC.cs:10526`) and the Spazmatism's 31 (`:10543`) - the S1-D-3i work
labelled them 57/3; the port's machines are unchanged this round (behaviour
frozen), the style ids now carry the C#'s rows. Same for the Golem family
(the body 45 `:12167`, the attached head 46 `:12184`, the fists 47
`:12198`, the free head 48 `:12212`), the Wall of Flesh (27,
`:10347`) and the Moon Lord core/head (77/79, `:14127`/`:14089`).

## Plantera's Hook machine (aiStyle-52, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

**Source.** The C# has no `AI_052_*` method вЂ” the machine is the inline
`else if (this.aiStyle == 52)` block of `NPC.AI` (`NPC.cs:32076-32240`).
The family is ONE type: `NPCID.PlanterasHook` (263), the only
`this.aiStyle = 52;` row in `SetDefaults` (`NPC.cs:12402`; the row
`:12396-12409`: 40Г—40, noGravity/noTileCollide, dmg 60, def 24, lifeMax
4000, `dontTakeDamage = true`). The port has no hook `NpcKind` and the
Plantera v1 (`npc.rs::update_plantera`) spawns no hooks, so the machine
lands UNWIRED (`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style52.rs`, the Destroyer
precedent `be63c688`): pure fns over the NPC pool, type-parameterised via
`HookCtx::npc_type` + the caller's `type_of` kindв†’id closure (the
`:32129` same-type scan), activating unchanged when the kind lands.

**The port** (`planteras_hook_step`), in C# order: the orphan strike
(`:32080-32085` вЂ” `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999,0,0)` + netUpdate rides
`HookEvents::orphan_strike`; an absent/inactive boss slot reads as the
cleared `NPC.plantBoss` static, `NPC.cs:8393`/`:95175`); the dead /
non-jungle / above-surface / below-underworld retreat gates
(`:32086-32094` вЂ” the surface compare is the C#'s `(double)` form, the
underworld bound the f32 cast of the int `UnderworldLayer * 16`, strict
`>`); the client anchor latch (`:32095-32105` вЂ” BOTH slots copy
`Center.X / 16f`, the decompile's X/X quirk kept 1:1); the timer ladder
(`:32108-32124` вЂ” the unanchored reset, the в€’1 tick, the в€’2/в€’2 boss-life
accelerations on the INTEGER `lifeMax / 2` / `/ 4` strict thresholds, the
в€’6 retreat drain); the sibling re-arm (`:32125-32134`); the anchor search
(`:32135-32183`); the positive-anchor early return (`:32185-32188`); the
speed ladder (`:32189-32213` вЂ” 6/8/10, +1 expert, +1 expert-below-half,
Г—2 retreat, Г—2 dead, both multiplies stack); the anchor pull
(`:32214-32237` вЂ” the anchor centre `ai*16 в€’ 8`, the STRICT
`dist < 12 + speed` snap band keeps the raw delta, else the
`delta * (speed / dist)` normalise); the ftw thorn latch
(`:32220-32233` вЂ” `localAI[3]`, `SpawnPlanteraThorns`
(`WorldGen.cs:76113`) rides `HookEvents::spawn_thorns`); the rotation
(`:32238-32239` вЂ” `Atan2(x: bossDx, y: bossDy) в€’ 1.57f`, the named args
put dx first and 1.57f is the literal, not ПЂ/2).

**RNG argument** (every draw cited, all on the caller's `UnifiedRandom` =
the `Main.rand` stream under the `UpdateNpcs` swap):
1. `Next(60, 300)` (`:32131`) вЂ” once PER matching pool slot inside the
   `!flag59 && localAI[0] <= 0 && ai[0] != 0` gate: every other active
   same-type NPC with either velocity component non-zero re-arms the
   timer; the loop does NOT break, the last match's draw wins. Zero draws
   when the gate fails or no sibling moves.
2. `Next(300, 600)` (`:32137`) вЂ” on entering the search.
3. Per attempt (1..=1001 вЂ” `num778 <= 1000` with the pre-increment,
   `:32140-32142`): two `Next(-num781, num781 + 1)` jitters (`:32156`,
   `:32157`) ALWAYS drawn вЂ” even when the wall-target arm overwrites the
   aim вЂ” then `Next(6)` (`:32158`) ONLY below half boss life: the draw
   rides the left `&&` operand, so it is consumed even when `!= 0` (the
   gate-fail draw) and skipped entirely at full life.
4. Nothing else draws: `TargetClosest` (`:32160`) scans without
   `Main.rand`; the ladder/snap/rotation are pure maths.
The 13 witness tests (WRITTEN NOT RUN вЂ” code-only mode, no compiler
invoked) replay the stream draw-for-draw against a clone: the orphan
path consumes zero draws, the re-arm consumes exactly one draw per
moving sibling (and none for a stationary one), a full-life anchoring
attempt consumes exactly timer + 2 jitters, a below-half attempt adds
the failing `Next(6)`, the client latch consumes zero.

**Deliberate stand-ins (the unwired seams).** `HookCtx` carries the stock
flags (single-player netMode 0, classic, no getGoodWorld) plus
`boss_target_zone_jungle` (the port's `Player` has no `zone_jungle` field
вЂ” the wiring passes the scene-metrics flag per tick). The boss's target
slot absent from the player slice reads as the C# inactive-slot zeros
(dead false, ZoneJungle false, position (0,0)). The strike and the thorn
tile edits ride `HookEvents` (the port has no strike/thorn seam inside a
pure AI fn). The local `in_world`/`solid_tile` probes mirror
`WorldGen.InWorld` (`WorldGen.cs:9688-9695`) / `WorldGen.SolidTile`
(`:70111-70132`, the `tr_core::edit::solid_tile` shape вЂ” crate-private,
kept local like the Destroyer precedent's tile probes). The anchor
search's `try/catch` (`:32169-32181`) is the `InWorld` gate: an OOB index
can never anchor.

**Wiring follow-up.** When `NpcKind::PlanterasHook` (263) lands: the
`SetDefaults` row, the `ai_style()` table row (52), the style-axis claim
(`npc.rs`'s `match self.kind.ai_style()`), the Plantera hook spawn (the
`AI_051` machine's tentacle/hook burst), and the `HookCtx` feed
(`plant_boss` = the Plantera pool index, `type_of` = the kindв†’id table).
Until then the module is dormant вЂ” no sim path calls it, no RNG stream
changes (the UpdateNpcs stream is untouched by construction).

## The footstep sound wave (S1-E-21 wave D, 2026-11-18)

**Source correction:** vanilla 1.4.5.8 has NO per-tile-type player footstep
cues. The whole decompile carries no `footstep`/`StepSound` surface table and
no Snow/Stone step assets exist in `Content/Sounds` вЂ” the grass (`Grass`,
sound 6), stone (`Tink`, 21) and dig cues are the tile-break families
(`WorldGen.KillTile_PlaySounds`, wave C). The only footstep path is the
Hermes-boot fast run: `Player.SpawnFastRunParticles` (`Player.cs:20205-20216`)
plays `hermesStepSound` when `runSoundDelay == 0 && velocity.Y == 0`
(`:20212`) at `position` (the top-left, `:20214`) and re-arms
`runSoundDelay = IntendedCooldown` (`:20215`). The callers are
`HorizontalMovement`'s two 0.2x-acceleration arms past the
`(accRunSpeed + maxRunSpeed) / 2` threshold (`:19779`), grounded and
unmounted (`:19987-19990`, `:20017-20020`). `PlayerFrame` re-derives the cue
every frame: default `(SoundType 17, Style -1, Cooldown 9)`
(`:35947-35949`), the Moon Lord legs (`legs == 140`) override to
`(2, 24, 6)` (`:35959-35964`). `Player.Update` ticks the delay down
(`:24706-24708`).

The port: `Player::spawn_fast_run_particles` queues the play
(`pending_step_sound`), `update_frames` re-derives `hermes_step_sound`, the
decrement sits after `purge_immune_buffs` and before `update_frames` (the
C# order), and `world_sim/player.rs` drains the queue through
`Audio::play_step_sound` with the `UpdatePlayers` stream (`Player.Update`
runs under the `Main.cs:17754` swap). Case 17 (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:854-864`)
plays `Sounds/Run` and rolls `Main.rand.Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` for the pitch
(`:862`, `sound::Family::Run`) вЂ” the draw runs only AFTER the attenuation
gate passed (`:369-436` precedes the switch); the int overload
(`SoundEngine.cs:102-108`) draws no `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat. The Item-24
arm delegates to wave A's `play_use_sound` faГ§ade (the audio-only
`GetRandomPitch` + the case-2 pitch draw after the gate). `Run` and
`Item_24` join `SFX_CUES`.

Deviations: the `SpawnFastRunParticles` dust trails (`:20217-20300` вЂ” the
wings-3/rocket-6, sailDash and shoe-dye arms) are visual seams, unported;
the legs-140 override is coded but unreachable вЂ” the port's `legs_armor`
has no producer yet (the C#'s `:35767` effective-legSlot assignment is part
of the unported armor visuals); the `SoundInstanceRun` stop/re-create pool
is the standing D4 (a fresh source per play). Tests
`s1_e_21d_the_fast_run_queues_the_footstep_cue_and_cooldown`,
`s1_e_21d_the_footstep_pitch_draw_rides_the_passed_stream`.

## The read-only NPC snapshot seam (S1-D-8 partial, task/S1-D-8, 2026-11-18)

Stage-2 prerequisite (research/39 "Phase A"): the NPC pass scans `app.npcs.iter()`
per scanning NPC, re-borrowing the mutable store for read-only lookups. This round
introduces the seam for ONE scan family вЂ” the carrier-link scans in
`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s `update_npcs` pre-passes (the Moon Lord parts' core lookup
`NPC.cs:41642`/`:42098`, the unlinked part's family-core/head fallback find, and the
core's part-alive check `:41251-41269`):

- `crates/tr-app/src/world_sim/npc_snapshot.rs::NpcSnapshot` вЂ” a per-tick read-only
  view built once (`NpcSnapshot::build(&app.npcs)`) before the family, copying only
  the scan-visible fields (`uid`, `kind`, `hp`, the `Npc::center()` pair). The scans
  (`position_living_uid`, `first_living_kind_uid`, `any_living_uid`) take `&self`, so
  the compiler forbids them touching the mutable store; the family's writes land on
  the scanning NPC alone.
- The one intra-family mutation the live reads could observe вЂ” the pre-pass's own
  `hp = 0` kill of a part whose core died вЂ” is mirrored by the owning pass through
  `NpcSnapshot::kill(idx)`; later scans in the family see the death exactly as the
  live `hp > 0` reads did. Centres stay valid: the family never moves an NPC.
- Behaviour frozen: no predicate, order, constant or RNG change. Proof: the existing
  Moon-Lord NPC tests, the `worldgen/world_hash.rs` pins, and two seam-equivalence
  tests (`npc_snapshot::tests::the_snapshot_scans_match_the_live_slice_scans`,
  `the_kill_mirror_matches_the_live_hp_write`) that compare every snapshot query
  against the live-slice scan it replaces. Full workspace green.
- **Left (not this round)**: the other scan families (saucer/scutlix/dutchman carrier
  scans, the projectile pool's `npcs.iter()` sites, the separation/target-selection
  families) and the spatial hash вЂ” the ROADMAP S1-D-8 row stays рџџЎ until then. No
  spatial hash was introduced; the scan count is unchanged (the seam only changes
  what the scans borrow, not how many there are).

## The NPC spatial hash + the carrier family migration (S1-D-8b, task/S1-D-8b-spatial, 2026-11-18)

The spatial slice of S1-D-8, building on the seam above:

- `crates/tr-app/src/npc_spatial.rs::NpcSpatial` вЂ” a cell-bucketed index over the
  per-tick `NpcSnapshot`: each slot buckets by its centre into a 1600 px grid
  (`CELL_PX` вЂ” an index granularity ONLY, it never enters a predicate). `near()`
  visits the conservative cell window (`k = ceil(radius / CELL_PX)` cells past the
  query cell per axis вЂ” a superset of the disc) and yields candidates in ASCENDING
  SLOT ORDER, the exact order the linear `npcs.iter()` scan visited. `hp` is not
  indexed, so the seam's kill mirror (`NpcSnapshot::kill`) stays visible without a
  rebuild.
- ONE more scan family migrated: `world_sim/npcs.rs::carrier_link_pre_pass` вЂ” the
  saucer/scutlix/dutchman carrier pre-pass (the `AI_075` type-390 nearest-carrier
  lookup, the `AI_093` Dutchman crew count, the saucer mounts' turret/cannon crew
  counts). Its 4 radius scans now read `NpcSpatial::nearest_living_kind` /
  `count_living_kind_within` over the same snapshot the Moon-Lord family uses; the
  predicates, the strict `< 1600.0` reach and the first-wins tie-break (`d < bd`)
  are verbatim. The pass mirrors its own fall-with-carrier `hp = 0` kills via
  `snap.kill`. The display inheritance stays a live write pass (it mutates other
  slots); the family runs at the same fixed-step position (extracted to a function,
  called where the inline loop stood).
- Behaviour frozen вЂ” proof: the A/B twin-seed equivalence tests.
  `npc_spatial::tests` (4 tests) compares the spatial candidate sequences against
  the linear scan slot-by-slot and distance-bit-by-bit over 4 seeds Г— 60 query
  centres Г— 8 kinds, plus exact cell-boundary/strict-reach cases (a centre exactly
  1600 px away is excluded, one at 1599.9 included), the kill-mirror visibility and
  empty/all-dead pools.
  `world_sim::npcs::tests::the_spatial_carrier_pass_matches_the_linear_scan_over_twin_seeds`
  runs the WHOLE migrated pass against the verbatim pre-migration linear scan
  (kept as the `#[cfg(test)]` reference `carrier_link_pre_pass_linear`) over
  byte-identical twin pools (4 seeds Г— 120 NPCs incl. linked/unlinked mounts, dead
  slots, cell-edge positions) and asserts every write-visible field
  (hp/carrier_x/y/timer/phase/rot/facing/crew counts) bit-for-bit equal вЂ” including
  the kill cascade. The world-hash pins stay green.
- **Left (deferred)**: the projectile pool's 18 `npcs.iter()` sites
  (`projectile.rs`), the separation/target-selection families
  (`npc.rs`/`npc_target.rs`), and the remaining `world_sim/npcs.rs` scans вЂ” the
  ROADMAP S1-D-8 row stays рџџЎ. No TR_BENCH A/B was taken this round (the slice's
  contract is the equivalence proof; the perf measurement rides the next slice).
## The join-bundle message ids (S1-I-1 wave A, 2026-11-18)

Wave A of the message-id remap ports the JOIN bundle's eleven missing ids as
wire bodies + `C2s`/`S2c` codecs in `crates/tr-app/src/net.rs` вЂ” the first
dependency tier of `SyncConnectedPlayer` (`NetMessage.cs:2806-2822`) /
`SyncOnePlayer` (`:2885-2960`) / `SendNPCHousesAndTravelShop` (`:2824-2852`) /
`SendAnglerQuest` (`:2653-2673`) /
`CreditsRollEvent.SendCreditsRollRemainingTimeToPlayer`
(`CreditsRollEvent.cs:27-33`) / `SendAllMarkersToPlayer`
(`CoinLossRevengeSystem.cs:498-507`):

- `30 TogglePVP` вЂ” `(byte)plr + hostile` (`NetMessage.cs:856-859`).
- `42 Unknown42` вЂ” the mana sync, `(byte)plr + (short)statMana + (short)statManaMax` (`:961-965`). Named `PLAYER_MANA` for readability; the C# name is `Unknown42` (`MessageID.cs:95`).
- `45 TeamChange` вЂ” `(byte)plr + (byte)team` (`:970-974`). `157 TeamChangeFromUI` shares the writer arm but its read side adds the team-based-spawn tail (`MessageBuffer.cs:2355-2363`); 157 is not a join-bundle id and stays unported.
- `60 Unknown60` вЂ” the NPC household banner, `(short)npc + (short)homeX + (short)homeY + (byte)status` (`:1067-1072`); the status is `WorldGen.TownManager.GetHouseholdStatus` (`:2845`). Named `NPC_HOUSE`.
- `72 TravelMerchantItems` вЂ” exactly `Main.TravelShopMaxSlots = 40` (`Main.cs:67029`) `(short)` item types, no count prefix (`:1134-1141`, reader `MessageBuffer.cs:3121-3124`).
- `74 AnglerQuest` вЂ” `(byte)Main.anglerQuest + anglerWhoFinishedToday.Contains(recipient name)` (`:1145-1148`); the wire's bool is per-recipient, the client stores it as `anglerQuestFinished` (`MessageBuffer.cs:3147-3153`).
- `126 SyncRevengeMarker` вЂ” `RevengeMarker.WriteSelfTo` (`CoinLossRevengeSystem.cs:275-286`): int uniqueID, Vector2 location, int npcNetID, float hpPercent, int npcType, int aiStyle, int coinsValue, float baseValue, bool spawnedFromStatue; the reader mirrors it field-for-field (`:321-324`).
- `135 DeadPlayer` вЂ” `(byte)plr` only (`:1569-1571`); sent when `statLife <= 0` (`:2897-2900`), the client raises `immuneAlpha` to 255 (`MessageBuffer.cs:4195-4203`).
- `140 SetMiscEventValues` вЂ” `(byte)kind + (int)value` (`:1591-1594`); the join bundle sends kind 0 only (the credits roll's remaining frames). Kinds 1/2 (the server-side slime transforms, `MessageBuffer.cs:4250-4260`) decode but have no port application.
- `142 SyncProjectileTrackers` вЂ” `(byte)plr` + two `TrackedProjectileReference` bodies, each `(int)Key + (short)type` (`TrackedProjectileReference.cs:22-26`/`:33-37`).
- `147 SyncLoadout` вЂ” `(byte)plr + (byte)CurrentLoadoutIndex` + the `hideVisibleAccessory` `bool[10]` (`Player.cs:1708`) packed into one `(ushort)` вЂ” bit `i` per slot (`WriteAccessoryVisibility`, `NetMessage.cs:1882-1893`; unpack `MessageBuffer.cs:4494-4501`).

Deliberate scope boundary: **bodies + codecs only**. The two `netglue`
dispatchers carry explicit parked arms for the new variants вЂ” nothing sends
them and the client/host apply-and-relay sites (`MessageBuffer.cs:1851-1867`,
`:2290-2306`, `:2325-2364`, `:2695-2739`, `:3118-3126`, `:3147-3153`,
`:4043-4048`, `:4195-4203`, `:4238-4249`, `:4282-4297`, `:4328-4343`) land with
the send-path pass (S1-I-4), so the live net message order is unchanged. The
per-id round-trip tests `net::tests::s1_i_1_*` (11) pin the frame's id byte,
the exact C# body bytes and the decode round trip; the travel shop test also
pins the fixed 40-slot length (a 39-slot body fails to decode).

## Frost Moon boss wiring (S1-F-13c, W1-1 resolved, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

`task/S1-F-13c-wire-bosses` wires the three Frost Moon bosses — **Everscream
(344, aiStyle 57)**, **IceQueen (345, aiStyle 60)** and **SantaNK1 (346,
aiStyle 61)** — onto their faithful named machines. The verifier finding
**W1-1** was that the live bosses still routed to the `update_hover`
stand-ins (`npc.rs`'s kind arms), so the slice-C machines
(`npc_ai_frost_boss.rs` 3ce99f36, `npc_ai_frost_boss_b.rs` 8e216a35) were
DEAD CODE: the bosses never attacked and the RNG stream desynced ~4-15
draws/tick. **Code-only mode**: no compiler invoked; the wiring witnesses
are WRITTEN, NOT RUN.

- **The style-axis claim** (`npc.rs::update_rng_dust`): the aiStyle match
  gains three kind-gated arms — `57 if kind == Everscream`, `60 if kind ==
  IceQueen`, `61 if kind == SantaNK1` — mirroring the MourningWood/Pumpking
  precedent (`57 if kind == MourningWood`). aiStyle 57 is SHARED (325/344),

  arm (`NPC.cs:32821-32825`) rolls `Main.rand` through the verbatim
  `DustPool::new_dust`, which needs the live `Main.dust` pool + the
  `SpawnCtx` statics. `update_rng` now delegates to `update_rng_dust` with a
  scratch pool + a permissive ctx (the tests' path — the AI-level draws
  still ride the caller's stream); the live sim
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs::update_npcs`) threads `app.dust` + the frame's
  `spawn_ctx()` into the tick closure on the SAME `UpdateNPCs` stream
  (`Main.cs:17767-17769`'s `SwapRandom("UpdateNPCs")` wraps `NPC.UpdateNPC`,
  dust included). The draw census is unchanged: `Next(5)` every phase-1
  tick, then on 0 the `NextVector2Square` pair + the pool's own rolls — all

- **The wrappers** (`npc_ai_frost_boss_b.rs::frost_boss_b_step`,

- A STRUCK bubble goes through `bubble_check_dead` (the `checkDead`

  ai[0]=1/ai[1]=4, life restored to lifeMax, dontTakeDamage, netUpdate
  — the strike starts the 4-tick countdown, it does not kill.
- The C# `alpha` is an int (`alpha -= 30` can go negative); the port's
  u8 saturates — moot, the unconditional `alpha = 50` (`:34902`)
  overwrites both paths every tick (the fade + clamp are dead code,
  ported dead with citations).
- `Vector2.Normalize` on a zero vector is NaN in XNA; the port uses
  `normalize_or_zero` (the established projectile.rs convention).
  Reachable only when the player centre exactly equals the bubble
  centre.
- FindFrame case 371 (`:72138-72142`) pins frame row 1
  (`npcFrameCount[371] = 2`, `Main.cs:67121`) — consts pin both; the
  wiring caller sets `frame = 1`.
- Difficulty: 371 is in `NeedsExpertScaling` AND `ProjectileNPC`
  (`NPCID.cs:10447-10448`) — `ScaleStats` runs but the lifeMax<6 bump
  is skipped (`:18160-18163`, the 1-HP life survives); the expert
  damage factor is 0.75 with lifeMax untouched (`:18417-18424`, the
  `type != 371` gate). The port is single-difficulty normal; the
  wiring wave carries the expert rows.
## The Sharkron pair (S1-D-3 aiStyle-71, code-only, 2026-11-19)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style71.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s
`else if (this.aiStyle == 71)` arm (`NPC.cs:34958-35079`) as a pure
module — CODE-ONLY MODE: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; the 13
witness tests are written, not run. The family is the Sharkron 372 /
Sharkron2 373 (`ID/NPCID.cs:11421`/`:11423`), Duke Fishron's
sharknados' sharks; the 371 DetonatingBubble beside them rides
aiStyle **70** (`NPC.cs:13723`) and is NOT this arm. The *projectile*
aiStyle 71 (the Razorblade Typhoon, `Projectile.cs:30355-30454`,
already `ai_typhoon`) is a different system, untouched.

**The machine, verbatim:** `noTileCollide = true` (`:34960`); the
unset/dead-target re-pick is `TargetClosest(faceTarget: false)` then
`direction = 1` + netUpdate (`:34962-34967`) — the forced right
facing AFTER the selection is load-bearing for the sway's sign.
Phase 0 (`:34968-35025`): `ai[1]++`, noGravity, dontTakeDamage,
`velocity.Y = ai[3]` EVERY tick — the plain Sharkron's spawner passes
no ai3 (0 → it hovers), the Sharkron2's passes −1.5 (it rises). The
373-only sway (`:34976-35003`): the π/30·localAI[1] cosine scaled by
`ai[2]` (the spawner's projectile width, `Projectile.cs:29514`), the
undo-then-advance-then-apply double position add across the
`localAI[1]++`, the |cos−0.5| > 0.25 spriteDirection write (cos−0.5
>= 0 → −1), the `vy·spriteDirection·0.1` rotation with the two
sequential ±0.2 clamps and the alpha −6 fade-in. The C# subtracts
0.5 in DOUBLE before the float cast and compares the DOUBLE in the
sprite gate — the port casts the f32 product up to f64 for the
cosine and keeps the double through the comparisons. At
`ai[1] >= 90` (`:35004-35024`): phase 1, `ai[1] = 0` bumped to 1 iff
the box is NOT in solid tiles, the roar (sound 4 style 19 — an
outcome flag), `TargetClosest()` (faceTarget true),
`spriteDirection = direction`, `velocity = Normalize(playerCenter −
Center)·16` (the port's house `normalize_or_zero`, the XNA
reciprocal-multiply form), `rotation = ToRotation()` (+π when
direction −1), netUpdate. Phase 1 (`:35026-35078`): any other phase
RETURNS; free air floors `ai[1]` at 1, embedded fades alpha −15 with
the 150 floor; once armed (`ai[1] >= 1`): alpha −60 floor 0,
dontTakeDamage = false, `ai[1]++`, and the SECOND solid check kills
(`life = 0`, HitEffect, `active = false`, return — no `checkDead`,
the vanilla deactivates directly). `ai[1] >= 60` returns gravity;
the rotation rides the live velocity every phase-1 tick.

**RNG by construction:** the arm contains no `Next`/`NextFloat`
(`NPC.cs:34958-35079`), and `TargetClosest`/`TryTrackingTarget`/
`SetTargetTrackingValues` (`:77652-77781`, the `npc_target.rs` port,
reused UNMODIFIED) draw nothing — so `ai_style71` takes no RNG
parameter and the `the_style71_arm_draws_no_rng` witness pins a
seeded `UnifiedRandom` across a full 200-tick lifecycle of both
kinds. The `HitEffect` arm (`:84207-84228` — the dmg/lifeMax·100
type-5 dust loop on hit, the flat 75 + the 583/577/578/579 gore
burst on death) draws only inside `Dust.NewDust`/`Gore.NewGore`;
the NPC dust/gore call sites are unported (S1-E-4's remainder), so
the arm is skipped wholesale (the `npc_lights.rs` precedent — the
stream stays untouched) and `sharkron_hit_dust_plan` ports the
branch structure/counts only. The sounds draw no `Main.rand`.

**Wiring deferred** (the `npc_ai_style50.rs` precedent, 613aac92):
the roster has no Sharkron kinds, so the aiStyle axis
(the `match self.kind.ai_style()` block in `npc.rs::update_rng`)
has no style-71 arm to claim; one-line `mod` seam
only. `Npc` has no `no_tile_collide`/`no_gravity` fields — the
per-tick writes ride `Style71Outcome` for the wiring caller's
movement step (`NPC.cs:90490-90498`); the tile kill sets `hp = 0`
and returns `died_in_tiles` (the caller owes the DeathSound, the
dust/gore plan and the deactivation). `FindFrame` case 371/372/373
(`:72138-72142`) pins `frame.Y = num` — the SECOND row forever
(`SHARKRON_FRAME_ROW = 1`); `npcFrameCount[372] = [373] = 2`
(`Main.cs:67121`, the 370-379 row of the `:67082` array). The
expert/master tweaks (`ScaleStats_ByDifficulty_Tweaks`,
`:18417-18424`: damage ×0.75 for 372/373, knockback ×0.75 for the
371/372/373 group) ride the difficulty system, not this arm — the
consts are the normal-mode `SetDefaults` rows. The spawner itself
(the sharknado projectile aiStyle-64 arm, `Projectile.cs:29419-
29533`: every 4th bolt — 2nd for the Greater Sharknado 386 — spawns
a shark with the projectile's velocity, the 386 alone seeding
`ai[2] = width` / `ai[3] = −1.5`) is the projectile family's wiring
wave; the module documents the seed contract.

(`NPC.cs:34880-34883`/`:34884`/`:34958`); the kind match keeps

## The aiStyle-3 velocity ladder (S1-D-3, code-only mode)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai3_speeds.rs::apply_ladder` ports `AI_003_Fighters`'
per-type velocity ladder (`NPC.cs:57403-58401`) arm-for-arm in the C#'s
if-else order. The C# runs it after the shared target/stuck core
(`:57120-57402`) and before the lighting block (`:58402+`) and the position
integration; the port wires it at the same position вЂ” `npc_ai.rs`'s
`walker_step_ladder` sets the facing/sprite (the target-core stand-in), runs
the ladder in place of the direct `vx = facing * speed` write, then
integrates (`walker_integrate`, extracted verbatim from `walker_step`);
`npc.rs::update_zombie` calls `run_ai3_ladder` at the same slot. Converted
sites: zombie, skeleton (the cave walkers, the goblin fighters, the martian
ground group, the pirates, the scarecrows and the Splinterling all ride it),
scutlix, solar drakomire, solar selenian, vortex headcrab, vortex rifleman,
goblin, solar spearman, vortex soldier. The gate is `kind.ai_style() == 3`
plus the ladder's own coverage вЂ” a declined kind (non-style-3, the frost
block, the shooter exclusions) falls back to the direct write, so every
other caller's behaviour is byte-identical.

**RNG: none.** The whole block draws no `Main.rand` value вЂ” every arm is
deterministic arithmetic on velocity/direction/scale/life/target-centre.
(The shooter block `:59069+` draws `Next(-40, 41)` per axis; it is out of
this module.) The 18 test fns pin each arm's constants to the C# literals;
they were **written, not run** вЂ” this task ran in code-only mode (no
cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test invocation, no compiler invoked).

  for every id in the range.

**Code-only mode.** This round ran with NO compiler invoked вЂ” no cargo,
rustc, rustfmt, dotnet or test runs; only file reads/writes and git. The
behaviour-frozen refactor proof is therefore a **mechanical byte-proof**, not
a test run: every moved line was extracted from the `origin/main` blob
(`git show origin/main:crates/tr-core/src/edit.rs`, LF-normalized; the
worktree copy is CRLF and content-identical, verified line-by-line before
the move) and string-compared against the new file. Build/test verification
(world-hash pins, `generation_is_reproducible_for_a_seed`, the workspace
suite) is **deferred to the merge gate** per the task contract.
**The move.** `edit.rs` 6 695 в†’ 2 027 lines; the kill family lands in
`edit/kill.rs` (4 703 lines): the event records (`ObjectDrop`, `PotEvent`,
`HerbEvent`, `PileLootEvent`, `TreeDropEvent`, `TileKill`), the ring-depth
cap + `SQUARE_FRAME_ORDER`, `kill_tile`/`kill_tile_cascading`,
`actuation_square_frame`/`square_tile_frame_gen`/`square_tile_frame_default`/
`square_tile_frame`, `tree_drop_record`, `destroy_object_guarded`,
`kill_plan_cells`, `solid_tile`/`solid_tile_allow_bottom_slope`/`solid_tile2`,

clock/bookcase/lantern/bed/candelabra/3x3/chandelier/doors/3x2/chair/bench/
chest/sunflower/pot/piles/on-table/alch), `any_lava`, `pot_break_sound`,
`SoundCue`/`KillSounds`/`kill_tile_sound`, `remove_tile`, `can_kill_tile`,
and 65 tests (the tree/BUG-16, `can_kill_tile` refusals, DW-3.x cascade,
DW-2.x herb/sunflower/pot/pile/clay-pot arms, the sound table and the orb
tests). Stays in the parent: `WALL_UNBREAKABLE`, `ALCH_SOILS` (shared with
`edit/place.rs`), `place_tile_sound`, the wire/actuator family, the

**The byte-proof (four checks, all passed).** The build script assembled
both files from the blob lines and aborted on any mismatch before writing:

   relocated `td` alias, plus the re-export block and exactly two seam
   lines;
4. kept-line count conservation (2 032 kept + 9 re-export lines).
An independent on-disk re-verification re-located all 15 ranges inside the
written `kill.rs` and re-compared them to the blob: identical.

## S1-G-1e special tiles (code-only mode, 2026-11-18)
`crates/tr-app/src/render/special_tiles.rs` ports the S1-G-1 special/chest/
platform slice: `DrawSpecialTilesLegacy` (`TileDrawing.cs:7893-8024`), the
chest frame offsets (`CacheSpecialDraws_Part2` `:4287-4330`) and the
platform slope side-fills (`DrawBasicTile` `:1515-1545`, glow arm
`:1367-1401`). **Code-only mode**: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs, no
graphify вЂ” the 18 unit tests are written as code, NOT run; verification is
the C# line-by-line citations plus the source-rect/offset maths pinned in
the tests. Deliberate deviations:
- **UNWIRED module**: the `render/tiles.rs::draw_tiles` +
  `tr_core::drawdata` seam is contested by the in-flight S1-G-1 siblings
  (G-1a vines, G-1b ropes, G-1c cracks, G-1d pylons), so the slice lands as
  pure draw/decision functions (the `drawdata_anim.rs` S1-F-9b pattern).
  Intended call sites are documented in the module header: the chest adjust
  after `draw_data` in `resolve_tile_frame` keyed on
  `chest::find_chest(chest_anchor(...))`; the side-fill BEFORE the generic
  `push_slope` column path (the C# returns early, `:1544`); the legacy arms
  in the non-solid-layer special pass fed by `CacheSpecialDraws_Part1`
  (`:4152-4255`).
- **Tile-entity arms deferred**: 395 (item frame), 520 (food platter) and
  471's entity lookup need the `TileEntity` store the port does not have;
  only the 334 weapon-rack DISPLAY decode (`frameX % 5000 - 100`, the
  5000-chunk style count, the right-neighbour prefix
  `< 25000 ? -10000 : -25000`, the 40 px clamp with the `width <= height`
  tie, the `num4 >= 3` flip) is ported. The 334 item-texture resolve
  (`netDefaults`/`Prefix`/`itemAnimations`) and the `item.color` second
  pass ride the wiring step.
- **Cage frame input**: the 620 arm reads
  `Main.butterflyCageFrame[8, GetWaterAnimalCageFrame(...)]` вЂ” animated by
  `AnimateTiles_CritterCages`, the S1-F-9b deferred animator half; the
  caller passes the frame row. `GetWaterAnimalCageFrame` itself is ported
  verbatim (C# truncating integer division, `% Main.cageFrames` = 25).
- **Two-step XNA truncations** (the G-3 verifier finding): the cage halo is
  `Color(127,127,127,0).MultiplyRGBA(hsl)` (per-channel `(a*b) >> 8`) THEN
  `*= 0.5f` (`(int)(byte * 0.5)`) вЂ” two separate byte quantisations, never
  one combined float multiply; the final overlay is
  `Color(255,255,255,0) * 0.1f` в†’ (25,25,25,0). `xna_multiply_rgba` /
  `xna_scale_color` are the reusable helpers.
- **invisibleBlock bit unported**: the side-fill gates read
  `Tile.invisibleBlock()` (`Tile.cs:528-531`, `bTileHeader3 & 0x20`); the
  port's `Tile` has no `bTileHeader3`, so `FillNeighbor.invisible` reads
  `false` (the vanilla default for non-echo-coated tiles). The
  `shouldShowInvisibleBlocks` flag is threaded through the decision fn.
- **Behind-tiles layer**: `SetLayer(Layer_BehindTiles, вЂ¦)` has no port
  analogue yet (the S1-G-13 target family is unwired);
  `PlatformSideFill.behind_tiles` records the decision and the push draws
  into the world range until the wiring step routes it.
- **Sun orb / weapon-rack draws**: the anchor/origin/scale maths are exact
  (integer `Width()/2` origins, `pos - origin*scale` top-left); the texture
  decodes (`TextureAssets.SunOrb`, the item sheets) and
  `Main.sunCircle`/`mouseTextColor` are caller inputs. The additive alpha-0
  tints ride the port's existing blend deviation (S1-G-3).
## The world-sounds wave (S1-E-21i, 2026-11-18)

**Code-only mode**: this wave was implemented without invoking any compiler вЂ”
no cargo/rustc/rustfmt, no test runs, no graphify refresh (the Lead's task
constraint). The seven `s1_e_21i_*` witness tests are WRITTEN, NOT RUN; the
branch `task/S1-E-21i-world-sounds` is pushed unmerged for a verification pass.

### Census (what this wave covers, what it skips)

The WorldGen/Wiring world-event `PlaySound` sites, after the landed waves
(item-use A, tile-place B, NPC-hit C, footsteps D, tile-break table S1-E-21c)
and the sibling-owned scopes (ambience E21e, player E21f, NPC E21g, projectile
E21h):

- **Wall break** вЂ” `WorldGen.KillWall_PlaySounds` (`WorldGen.cs:60423-60441`),
  played from `KillWall` (`:60385`) BEFORE the dust (`:60391-60394`) and the
  drop (`:60400`). The port's `break_wall` played a hardcoded `Dig_2` вЂ” replaced
  by `tr_core::edit::kill_wall_sound` + `Audio::play_wall_break_sound`.
- **Wiring switch clicks** вЂ” `Wiring.HitSwitch`'s seven
  `SoundEngine.PlaySound(28, ...)` sites (`Wiring.cs:267` the 135/314/423/428/
  442/476 family, `:272` the wide 440 at `i*16+16, j*16+16`, `:285` the lever
  136, `:310` the timer 144, `:323` the 441/468 flags/buttons at the clicked
  cell, `:339` the 467 gem lock ONLY when `frameX/36 == 4`, `:375` the 132/411
  else-arm). The mine (210) and the geyser (443) are silent (`:288-296` carry
  no play). The port's `hit_switch` had a D19 "unported" comment on the
  else-arm вЂ” now queued.
- **Doors** вЂ” `WorldGen.OpenDoor` (`WorldGen.cs:37727`, `PlaySound(8)`) and
  `CloseDoor` (`:31908`, `PlaySound(9)`), success-path only. The port already
  played `Door_Opened`/`Door_Closed` through the plain `play_at` (no pitch);
  upgraded to `Audio::play_door_sound`'s case-8/9 pitched path.
- **Skipped (already landed + wired)**: the liquid-change cues (S1-E-25),
  the chest/menu cues (`chest.rs`), the tile-break table (`kill_cue`,
  S1-E-21c вЂ” untouched, its D3 pin stands).

### The plays and their RNG streams

Every play gates attenuation FIRST (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436` precedes
the type switch) and only then draws; the draws ride the CALLER's `Main.rand`
stage stream, never the wiring stand-in `Wiring::rand` (that stream is the
device-effects substitute вЂ” cannons/traps/teleport rolls):

| Site | C# | Stream |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hammer wall break | `Player.PickWall` `Player.cs:45949` | `UpdatePlayers` (`Main.cs:17754`) |
| Player switch bridge / minecart trip / tile-use click | `Collision.SwitchTiles` (`Player.cs:28274`), `Minecart.HitTrackSwitch` (`Minecart.cs:1281-1288`), `Player.cs:32174-32178` | `UpdatePlayers` |
| Weighted pressure plates | `PressurePlateHelper.Update` (`Main.cs:17763-17765`) | `UpdatePressurePlates` |
| NPC switch bridge | `NPC.cs:90504` | `UpdateNPCs` (`Main.cs:17767`) |
| Wiring tick (timer expiries) + logic sensors | `Wiring.UpdateMech` (`WorldGen.cs:71509`) + `TileEntity.PerformUpdates` (`:71510`) inside `UpdateWorld` | `UpdateWorldGen` (`Main.cs:17802-17805`) |
| Net replays (`17` wall break `MessageBuffer.cs:1177`, `59` switch `:2682-2693`, the rigged chest `:1887-1893`) | message handlers run outside every swap (`Main.cs:16895` NpcStrike precedent) | `rngs.global()` (the bare stream) |

The case maths, per arm:

- **13 Shatter** (`:783-792`): NO draws, no pitch.
- **6 Grass** (`:706-716`): one `Next(-30, 31) * 0.01` (`:714`) вЂ”
  `sound::Family::Grass`.
- **3 style 25** (`SoundID.NPCHit25`, `SoundID.cs:1281`): wave C's style
  faГ§ade вЂ” the audio-only `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat (drawn even at variance
  0, `SoundEngine.cs:99`), the Г—0.5 volume arm and one `Next(-10, 11)` pitch
  draw (`:670`), delegated to `play_npc_hit_sound("NPC_Hit_25", вЂ¦)`.
- **0 Dig** (`:440-452`): wave B's case-0 path вЂ” the `Next(3)` variation pick
  + `Next(-10, 11) * 0.01`, delegated to `play_place_sound((0, 1), вЂ¦)`.
- **8/9 doors** (`:728-749`): one shared `Next(-20, 21) * 0.01`
  (`:736`/`:747`) вЂ” `sound::Family::Door`. The int overload
  (`SoundEngine.cs:102-108`) draws NO `GetRandomPitch`.
- **28 Mech** (`:997-1007`): the `SoundInstanceMech[0].State == Playing`
  guard (`:998-1001`) returns BEFORE the one `Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` (`:1005`)
  вЂ” `sound::mech_case28(playing_0, rng)`. The play overwrites the slot
  WITHOUT a Stop (`:1002`); the port models the slot as
  `mech_slots: [Option<Sink>; 1]` and detaches the old sink. `Mech_0` joins
  `SFX_CUES` (id 28; `SoundMech[0]` loads `Sounds/Mech_0`,
  `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:22`/`:176`).

The wiring queue is the `take_statue_spawns` event-queue seam:
`Wiring::switch_clicks: Vec<(i32, i32)>` fills in play order inside
`hit_switch` (world pixels; the queue itself draws NOTHING), and each app
drain site plays on its own stage's stream immediately after the triggering
pass вЂ” the C# draws mid-walk, the port drains at the pass tail (the same
deviation wave C recorded for the projectile strikes).

### Deliberate deviations / deferrals

- **The `KillWall` fail-path plays are missing.** The C# plays the sound table
  even when the break fails (`KillWall_CheckFailure` `:60410-60421`: the
  dungeon walls `{7,8,9,94-99}` before Skeletron, wall 87 before Golem вЂ”
  `Main.cs:10598-10606`; `Player.PickWall` calls `KillWall(fail: true)` on
  every sub-100 damage tick, `Player.cs:45957`). The port's `break_wall` has
  no fail parameter and no hit-tile damage model, so the cue rides the
  successful break only. The fail gating needs the `hitTile` damage
  accumulator + the progression flags вЂ” a follow-up, not this wave.
- **The explosion wall-walk plays are deferred (E21h-owned).**
  `Projectile.ExplodeTiles`' 3Г—3 wall walk calls `WorldGen.KillWall`
  (`Projectile.cs:78745`) under the `UpdateProjectiles` swap
  (`Main.cs:17775`); the port's walk (`projectile.rs` explode_bomb) calls
  `tr_core::edit::break_wall` directly with no sound. That file belongs to
  the projectile wave вЂ” recorded here, not touched.
- **The load-rig `TR_TOGGLES` path stays log-only** (`app/mod.rs`
  `apply_tr_toggles`): no player exists at load, the C# `gameMenu`/loading
  gate would refuse the positioned plays anyway.
- **The wiring arm order differs from the C#.** The port groups
  135/314/423/428/442/476 first and puts 210/443 before the 132/411 else-arm;
  the click pushes match each arm's C# position semantics regardless (441/468
  click at the clicked cell, NOT the derived trip corner; 467 only on the
  trigger variant).
- **The `kill_cue` D3 pin is untouched.** The landed tile-break wave's
  pinned/no-jitter mapping (`editing.rs::kill_cue`) stays as-is; the new
  wall/door/switch paths use the pitched RNG contract instead.
- **The case-28 playing guard is device-bound.** Headless (no output device)
  `emit` returns `None`, the slot stays empty and the guard never trips вЂ”
  every audible click draws, matching the fresh-instance behaviour. With a
  device, a live click refuses the next one draw-free (the C# semantics).
- **The door cue strings are unchanged** (`Door_Opened`/`Door_Closed`) вЂ” the
  existing `interaction_events` tests keep passing their shape; only the
  play path gained the pitch draw.
- **One borrow re-fetch in `world_sim/player.rs`**: the accessory buff-arms
  call re-fetches `stream(UpdatePlayers)` instead of reusing the tick's `rng`
  binding (the switch-click drains borrowed the pool in between) вЂ” the
  stream identity and the draw order are unchanged.

### Witness tests (written, NOT run)

- `tr-core/edit/wall.rs::s1_e_21i_kill_wall_sound_table_arms` вЂ” every arm's
  membership verbatim + the window boundaries (87/94 outside 88..93).
- `tr-core/wiring.rs::s1_e_21i_hit_switch_queues_the_mech_clicks_per_type` вЂ”

## Test temp-path isolation (fix/test-temp-path-isolation, 2026-11-18)
**The race.** Disk-writing tests joined CONSTANT names onto
`std::env::temp_dir()` (`tr-s1-j-4-validate.trwld`, `tr-flow-char-fav`,
`tr-persist-v3.trwld`, вЂ¦). `%TEMP%` is per-user, not per-worktree: two gates
running `cargo test` concurrently in sibling worktrees share every one of
those paths вЂ” one gate's `remove_file`/`remove_dir_all` wipes the other's
in-flight fixture, producing spurious "file not found"/parse failures that
vanish on a serial re-run. The fix is test-code-only: every scratch output
moves into a unique per-test directory
`temp_dir()/tr-test-<pid>-<name>` (pid separates concurrent binaries, the
test slug separates tests inside one binary), created empty and removed
best-effort at the test's end. Committed fixtures (`assets/test/golden.*`)
keep their paths вЂ” only scratch outputs moved.
**The shared helper.** `crates/tr-app/src/test_world_helpers.rs` (the
existing test-utils module) gains `test_scratch(name)` (wipe-stale +
`create_dir_all`) and `remove_scratch(dir)` (errors ignored). The local
`scratch`/`ach_scratch` (saveglue) and `temp_dir` (save_list) helpers now
delegate to it; `tr-core`'s `wld/mod.rs` scratch helper already keyed on
pid + name and stays local (tr-core cannot depend on tr-app).
**Census вЂ” fixed constant paths (all fixed, pre-fix file:line):**
- `crates/tr-app/src/achievements.rs:914` (`tr-ach-test.trdat`)
- `crates/tr-app/src/app/flow.rs:2040` (`terrustaria-delete-gate.trwld`),
  `:2481` (`tr-flow-char-fav`)
- `crates/tr-app/src/app/mod.rs:4955` (`tr-dw-1-6-pins.trwld`), `:5004`
  (`tr-dw-1-6-clear.trwld`)
- `crates/tr-app/src/app/saveglue.rs:955, 1192, 1242, 1289, 1328, 1373,
  1431, 1458, 1498, 1594, 1637` (the DW-2.x / S1-J-4 / S1-J-7 round-trip
  files)
- `crates/tr-app/src/persist.rs:163, 195, 211, 227, 242` (the sidecar
  version fixtures)
- `crates/tr-app/src/ui/save_list.rs:453-454` (the fixed-name `temp_dir`
  helper; callers `:526, 557, 582, 630, 645, 740, 797, 818, 972`), plus
  `:575` (`tr-savelist-nope`) and `:634` (`tr-savelist-noplayers`) вЂ” the
  two missing-dir probes now point at an absent child of a unique dir
- `crates/tr-app/src/ui/world_creation.rs:1501, 1532`;
  `crates/tr-app/src/ui/world_select.rs:1417`
**Census вЂ” already pid-unique (safe across gates, left as-is):**
`assets.rs:3115, 3140`; `app/worldgen_job.rs:265, 308`;
`app/mod.rs:4591, 4655, 4673`; `app/flow.rs:2988`; `map.rs:882`;
`ui/ingame_options.rs:2319`; `tr-core/src/wld/mod.rs:1151`; saveglue's
`scratch`/`ach_scratch` (`:417, :1666`, now delegating). `tools/` uses
Python `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`/`mkdtemp` (`GenItemData/gen.py:3035`,
`GenItemData/test_gen.py:20`, `GenSortData/gen.py:372`) вЂ” already unique.
No `%TEMP%` literals or hardcoded `Temp` paths exist in test code.
**Code-only note.** Written under the swarm's code-only directive: no
cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs, no compiler invoked; style matched by hand.
Concurrency verification is DEFERRED to the compile window вЂ” run the same
filter twice in parallel, once per worktree (PowerShell):
```powershell
Start-Job -Name gateA { Set-Location 'C:\Users\DreadLord\Desktop\TR-tmpfix';
    cargo test -p tr-app --bin terraria-rust saveglue 2>&1 }
Start-Job -Name gateB { Set-Location 'C:\Users\DreadLord\Desktop\<sibling-worktree>';
    cargo test -p tr-app --bin terraria-rust saveglue 2>&1 }
Receive-Job gateA -Wait; Receive-Job gateB -Wait
# both must print `test result: ok` (cargo may exit 1 on success here вЂ”
# judge only by the result lines). Repeat with the filters `persist`,
# `savelist`, `worldcreate`, `dw_1_6` and finally the full gate:
# cargo test --workspace -- --skip migrates_version_2_kinds_to_item_ids
```

## Projectile SendData cadence (S1-I-4 wave C)
`app/net_proj_sync.rs` ports the projectile sync's three cadences as pure
functions (`ProjSync`), disjoint from `netglue.rs` (wave A) and
`net_npc_sync.rs` (wave B):
- **Spawn** (`Projectile.cs:11096`): one `27` per `NewProjectile`, after
  `FinalizeProjectile` + the modifier; the only gate is `SendData`'s
  `netMode == 0` return (`NetMessage.cs:83-86`).
- **Kill** (`Projectile.cs:77254-77257`): one `29` when
  `owner == Main.myPlayer && netMode != 0`, carrying the **entry** position
  snapshot (`:70648`), not the death position.
- **Per-update** (`Projectile.cs:17210-17244`): the `netUpdate`/`netSpam`
  budget РІР‚вЂќ cost 5, cap 60, refill 1/tick РІР‚вЂќ runs **per sub-step** (inside the
  `while` at `:16676`, `1 + extraUpdates` times); the `netUpdate = false`
  tail (`:17244`) is outside the loop and the owner gate, so it clears every
  slot's flag every tick. A parked send (`netUpdate2`) promotes and retries
  next tick.
- **Section culling** (`NetMessage.cs:1774-1800`): flag3 (`type == 12 ||
  projPet || aiStyle == 11 || netImportant`, `:1777`) bypasses culling;
  skipped clients are remembered per slot and re-served by
  `RecheckSectionsForSkippedUpdates` (`Projectile.cs:17246-17256`, host
  only), the targeted send clearing the flag (`NetMessage.cs:1821-1823`).
**Deliberate deviations (until the wave merge):**
1. The engine is **dead-code parity** (the R-36-2 film-framework pattern):
   the live loop still runs `netglue.rs::projectile_sync_plan`'s 10 Hz diff.
   Wiring both would double-send; the swap is the merge follow-up.
2. The 337 C# `netUpdate = true` AI-arm producers are not wired РІР‚вЂќ the port's
   AI arms skip the writes today; `ProjSync::mark_dirty` is the seam.
3. `bannerIdToRespondTo` rides as 0 (no pool field; the banner response is
   unported) and `Main.projPet` is a `false` parameter (no port table yet).
4. The per-slot bookkeeping lives beside the pool (`ProjSync`) instead of on
   `Projectile` so `projectile.rs` stays untouched by this wave.
Verification: `cargo test -p tr-app net_proj_sync` РІР‚вЂќ 10 per-site tests green
(`test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed`).

(`test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed`). **Superseded by the wave-D swap below
