## The net sync swap (S1-I-4d, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

The wave-B (`net_npc_sync.rs`) and wave-C (`net_proj_sync.rs`) decision layers
landed INERT (zero callers). This wave SWAPS them into the live loop and DELETES
the old duplicate sends — wiring both would double-send, so the swap is atomic.

**What was removed (the old paths):**
- `netglue.rs::net_tick`'s whole-set 10 Hz `23 NPCInfo` broadcast (one message per
  live NPC every cadence tick) — replaced by the per-NPC `netSpam` cadence.
- `netglue.rs::projectile_sync_plan` (the 10 Hz `27` change-diff + the vanished-key
  `29` feed) and its `App.net_proj_last` / `net_proj_spam` maps — replaced by
  `ProjSync`'s faithful budget.
- The client's absence-from-the-stream despawn prune (`App.net_npc_seen`,
  `net_npcs_seen_at`, the `NPC_STALE` const) — the event-driven `23` stream has no
  "whole set" to diff against; despawns are explicit life-0 bodies now.

**What was wired (the new paths):**
- `App::npc_sync_cadence` (host-only, `NPC.cs:90590`) steps
  `net_npc_sync::update_network_code` per NPC per fixed step, in slot order
  (`Main.cs:17948-17952`). State is keyed by the stable `Npc.uid` (the port's Vec
  compacts on death, so the index is not stable). `App::flush_npc_outbox` drains
  the `NpcSend` outbox through `S2c::NpcInfo` / `NpcHouse` / `NpcBuffs`.
- `App::proj_sync_cadence` steps `net_proj_sync::ProjSync` per fixed step
  (`Projectile.cs:17210-17244`); spawn `27` (`:11096`), kill `29` with the entry
  position (`:77254-77257`, `:70648`), and the budget pass. `App::drain_proj_outbox`
  sends through `S2c::Projectile` / `ProjectileDead` (host) or `C2s` (client).
- Both cadences run on a 60 Hz accumulator (`App.net_sync_cadence_timer`) inside
  `net_tick`, so the real frame loop AND the net-only test pump drive them; the
  outboxes drain on the 10 Hz tick. The message-id table (S1-I-1) is UNCHANGED.

**Swap proof (no double-send):** each subsystem has exactly ONE producer now.
The NPC `23` comes only from `npc_sync_cadence` → `flush_npc_outbox` (the old
broadcast loop is gone); the projectile `27`/`29` only from `proj_sync_cadence` →
`drain_proj_outbox` (`projectile_sync_plan` is gone). Within the projectile
cadence the spawn site and the change-detect producer are disjoint (the `fresh`
set skips first-sight), so a spawn emits ONE `27`, not two. Witnesses:
`the_npc_cadence_sends_once_then_throttles_not_every_tick`,
`the_proj_cadence_spawn_sends_one_27_not_two`,
`the_npc_cadence_throttles_a_moving_npc_to_the_netSpam_rate` (cadence parity),
`the_npc_despawn_streams_one_life0_body_and_the_client_drops_it` (stream-order).

**Deliberate deviations / interim stand-ins (recorded, not silent):**
1. **Interim change-detect producers.** The C# `netUpdate = true` comes from ~337
   projectile AI sites + the NPC AI arms. The NPC arms already set
   `Npc.net_update`; one projectile producer is wired (the gem-staff retarget,
   `Projectile.cs:37891`, via the new `Projectile.net_update` field). Until the
   full census lands, a state change vs the last body ALSO arms the dirty flag
   (`npc_sync_cadence` / `proj_sync_cadence`), so moving entities still sync. The
   send BUDGET is the faithful C# gate, not the diff — the diff only decides
   *whether* to dirty, the `netSpam` throttle decides *when* to send.
2. **The despawn feed** is the uid gone-diff (a uid the cadence knew that left the
   live set emits one life-0 `23`), not the C#'s per-slot `active=false` — the
   port's Vec removes dead NPCs, so the cadence (not the removed slot) emits it.
   The client removes on life≤0 with a generation guard (`MessageBuffer.cs:1661`).
3. **Hostile shots (owner 255)** are out of the projectile budget sync (the owner
   gate matches `Projectile.cs:17210` and the old diff's scope). On the C# server
   `Main.myPlayer == 255` folds them in; the port's host keeps a local player
   (owner 0), so hostile-shot sync lands with the owner-model reconcile.
4. **`has_head_index`** rides `NpcKind::is_town_npc()` (the town roster) until the
   `TypeToDefaultHeadIndex` table lands (`NPC.cs:90621`).
5. **The event-site helpers** (`sync_now`, `recheck_sections`, `note_broadcast`,
   `despawn_mark_applies`) stay dead-code-parity until their simulation callers
   land; the cadence's section culling rides the decision layer's own fan-out.
Verification: code-only mode — no compiler/test run this wave; the decision
layers' landed per-site tests (`net_npc_sync` 20, `net_proj_sync` 10) plus the
four new wiring witnesses are the tests-as-code. C# cross-reads cited per block.

## The aiStyle-14 flyer family (S1-D-3 aiStyle-14 slice, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)
`npc_ai_style14.rs::bat_ai` ports `NPC.AI()`'s `if (this.aiStyle == 14)`

`SetDefaults` rows `:9378`/`:9409`/`:9543`/`:9629`; the C# arm serves

(user directive); verification = re-reading the C# arm line by line, the 14

the live dispatch still routes the four kinds through `update_cave_bat`'s

Faithful details worth pinning:
- **The generic approach runs twice** for the water-group types
  (`:23183`'s list): the second pass (`:23265-23331`) sits OUTSIDE the
  `base.wet` gate, so a dry bat accelerates at 0.2/tick X, not 0.1 вЂ” the

  The Hellbat (60) instead follows the first pass with its own arm
  (`:23198-23263`: X 0.07 double-add / 0.03 brake, Y 0.02 brake).
- **The bounce clamps are direction-aware** (`:22855-22862`): the В±2 X
  minimum applies only when the bounce pushes AGAINST `direction`; the
  В±1 Y minimum (`:22867-22874`) is unconditional on sign.
- **The drift reset gate** (`:23363`) needs `!player.wet` AND the
  entity-box `Collision.CanHit`; `Player.wet` is not on
  `TargetCandidate` (the target scan never reads it), so it rides the

  centre + the 0.2-normalised jittered velocity; `NewProjectile(44, 21,
  0f)` and the `timeLeft = 300` write (`:23449-23450`) belong to the

  convention). `spriteDirection` is not written by this arm вЂ” the C#
  `TargetClosest` writes `direction`/`directionY` only; the renderer
  sync lands with the wiring.
**RNG argument (by construction)**: the arm's only `Main.rand` sites on
the ported paths are the 62/66 shot arm's вЂ” `Next(-100, 101)` for the X
aim jitter then the Y (`:23446-23447`, in that order, only on
`ai[0] == 20/40/60/80` with `CanHit`), and `Next(300)` inside the
reset threshold `(float)(300 + Main.rand.Next(300))` (`:23453`), drawn

draws on a shot tick, one draw on an in-view reset tick, zero draws
out-of-view, zero draws on a blocked shot tick (the else-if is not
evaluated), and 600 draw-free ticks per bat kind incl. the wet arm.

## The bat/fish reconcile (S1-D-3 census W-10 slice, task/S1-D-3-reconcile-batfish, 2026-11-19, code-only mode)

brief labels it W-9) reconciled the landed-but-unwired faithful modules
against the live stand-in arms. **Code-only mode**: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/
tests/graphify invoked — reads/writes + git only; verification = re-reading
the C# arms line by line (the distrust-verbatim rule, the f1701eb0 defect
catalogue checklist: missing gates / f32 reciprocal order / int-vs-float
division / strict bounds / RNG draw order / short-circuit operators).
**Per-kind verdicts:**

  CLAIMED.** `npc.rs::update_cave_bat` now routes through
  `npc_ai_style14::bat_ai` (`NPC.cs:22849-23486`); the hash-jitter stand-in
  (research/25 finding 25-6: a positional hash + `flyer_step` instead of
  the C#'s velocity ramps, the VoodooDemon's sickle absent) is retired.
  Audit of the module against the C#: FAITHFUL — the ungated second
  generic pass (`:23265-23331`, dry bats accelerate 0.2/tick X), the
  Hellbat's own second arm (`:23198-23263`), the direction-aware bounce
  clamps (`:22852-22875`), the drift reset gate (`:23363`), the X-before-Y
  shot draws (`:23446-23447`) and the short-circuited `Next(300)`
  (`:23453`) all match; no defect found.
- **Goldfish 55 / Piranha 58 / Shark 65 (aiStyle 16): CLAIMED.**
  `npc.rs::update_swimmer` now routes through
  `npc_ai_style16::ai_016_step` (`NPC.cs:23492-24021`);
  `npc_ai::swim_step`/`SwimParams` are DELETED (the stand-in lacked the
  head `TargetClosest` `:23494-23497`, the integer feet-slope division
  `:23709-23736`, the collide-latch bounces `:23737-23761`, the
  beach-avoid `ai[0]` writes `:23932-23956`, and integrated inside the

  (`:23576-23577`), the flop triple order (`:23977-23979`), the Arapaima
  asymmetric 7/4 snap caps (`:23786-23797`) and the 157 damp exemption
  (`:23957`) all match; no defect found.
- **The aiStyle-8 casters (FireImp 24 / GoblinSorcerer 29 / DarkCaster 32
  / Tim 45 / DesertDjinn 533): EXCLUDED — census-confirmed WIRED.** The
  live `update_caster` already delegates to the faithful
  `npc_ai_bat::ai_style_8_step` (the census's style-8 row: WIRED-DELEGATE;

  and is ASYMMETRIC: the right edge is the head's centre, the left edge
  headCentre в€’ 250 (NOT the dock's в€’200В·side).
- The dock aim rotation (`atan2 + 1.57f`, `:28151`) OVERWRITES the chase
  aim rotation (`atan2 в€’ 1.57f`, `:28047`) at the end of the 0/3 block вЂ”
  both writes kept, in order; the literal `1.57f`, not `FRAC_PI_2`.
- The chase normalisers DIVIDE by the distance with no epsilon floor
  (`:28044`, `:28173`, `:28192`) вЂ” a zero distance yields the C#'s
  NaN/Inf verbatim (the live arm floors at 0.001).
- The three dead-store sqrt reads (`num501` `:28150`, `num504`'s first
  value `:28158`, `num507`'s reused value `:28237`) are kept and
  annotated вЂ” computed, never read, no observable effect.
- The arm does NOT integrate `position += velocity` вЂ” the saw is
  noTileCollide, so `UpdateNPC` integrates after `AI()`
  (`NPC.cs:90498`); the caller owns the step.

Documented stand-ins: `life = -1; HitEffect(); active = false`
(`:27966-27968`) rides the port's hp-0 death convention with an early
return (observationally identical вЂ” `ai[2]` is 10 or в‰Ґ 60, so no state
branch matches anyway); the `HitEffect()` call reaches the
type-128..131 gore arm (`NPC.cs:89433-89469`) whose four
`Main.rand.Next(61, 64)` picks (`:89452/:89456/:89460/:89464`) are
COSMETIC gore вЂ” the dust/gore skip precedent (S1-E-4's drop sites stay
a follow-up), so the port draws nothing there. `EncourageDespawn(10)`
(`:28026`) rides the existing `Npc::encourage_despawn`
(`NPC.cs:7249-7256` вЂ” only ever lowers the window). The head reads
(`active`/`aiStyle`/`position`/`width`/`ai[1]`) ride the
`Style33Context` seam вЂ” the port's `World.prime_*` write-through carries
only the position today; `Main.netMode` rides `ctx.net_mode` and the
`EverLastingTicker` stamp rides `ctx.ticker`.

**RNG by construction**: the C# arm (`NPC.cs:27943-28244`) draws no
`Main.rand.Next` вЂ” every counter is deterministic (`ai[3]` ticks, the
hp-free state gates) вЂ” and the `npc_target::target_closest` helper is
RNG-free too, so `style33_step` takes no RNG parameter and cannot
perturb any stream; the witness
`the_arm_is_deterministic_without_an_rng` pins identical inputs to
identical state over 50 ticks, and pins that the saw fires no shot
(`wants_hostile_shot` stays empty вЂ” the dash IS the attack).
## The aiStyle-51 census audit (S1-D-3, code-only mode)
**Code-only mode**: this task ran with NO compiler invoked вЂ” no cargo, no
rustc, no rustfmt, no tests run, no graphify refresh. Every claim below is
verified by reading the C# and the Rust side by side, not by execution.
**Census (the first check)**: `aiStyle = 51` appears exactly ONCE in the
NPC `SetDefaults` census вЂ” `NPC.cs:12384`, type **262 Plantera**
(`ID/NPCID.cs:11201`), row `:12379-12395` (86Г—86, dmg 50 / def 14 /
lifeMax 30000, kb 0, value `Item.buyPrice(0, 15)` = 150000
(`Item.cs:49417-49420`), noGravity + noTileCollide, boss, npcSlots 16).
No named-constant assignments (`aiStyle = NPCAIStyleID.*`) exist in
`NPC.cs`. The two other `aiStyle = 51` hits are **projectile** styles вЂ”
`Projectile.cs:3830` (type 293 `LostSoulHostile`) and `:3874` (type 297
`LostSoulFriendly`, `ID/ProjectileID.cs:1140`/`:1148`) вЂ” a different
machine, S1-D-4's territory, out of the NPC census. The satellites ride
OTHER styles: Hook 263 в†’ 52 (`NPC.cs:12402`), Tentacle 264 в†’ 53
(`:12414`), Spore 265 в†’ 50 (`:12427`); Brain of Cthulhu 266 в†’ 54
(`:12443`, S1-D-3e's census, untouched). **Verdict: Plantera only в†’ this
task is a docs-only census audit of the sibling's coverage; no new code.**
**The sibling under audit**: `ba8159fc` (`task/S1-D-3-plantera-audit`,
pushed, NOT in `origin/main` at audit time вЂ” `git merge-base
--is-ancestor ba8159fc origin/main` exits 1). It ports the machine to
`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_plantera.rs` (604 lines, 11 witness tests
WRITTEN NOT RUN) and wires the kind-262 seam. The distrust-verbatim
re-read of the whole arm (`NPC.cs:31717-32075`) against that module
confirms the bulk of the port (the tuning ladder `:31763-31808`, the
500-px leash + in-band hover quirk `:31799-31831`, the reversal-Г—2
approach `:31832-31863`, the phase stats 36/50 Г—2 and 10/70 defГ—4 dmgГ—2
`:31866-31875`/`:31973-31980`, the >80 seed cadence with the f64
0.9/0.8/0.7/0.6 bumps + enrage +3 `:31880-31917`, the 22/275 в†’
27/276 (`Next(4)`, в€’30) в†’ 31/277 (`Next(8)`, в€’120) volley with the
`<0.8`-gated else-if short-circuit `:31937-31957`, the Г—3 muzzle
`:31963-31964`, timeLeft 300 unless 277 `:31966-31969`, the one-shot
8-tentacle latch `:31983-31994`, the в‰Ґ350 spore cadence with the f64
0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 bumps `:32037-32054`, the X-first В±10 jitters
`:32058`/`:32060`) вЂ” but finds these gaps:
* **G1 вЂ” the rotation atan2 is SWAPPED (behavioural defect).**
  `NPC.cs:31865` is `Math.Atan2(x: playerCX в€’ cx, y: playerCY в€’ cy) +
  1.57f`. The NAMED arguments bind dx to `Atan2(double y, double x)`'s
  **x-parameter** and dy to its **y-parameter** вЂ” the value is the
  STANDARD `atan2(dy, dx)`, computed in double, cast to float BEFORE the
  `+1.57f`. The sibling (`npc_ai_plantera.rs:170-172`) reads the named
  args as positional and ports `dx.atan2(dy)`; its comment ("the
  arguments are SWAPPED vs the usual atan2(dy, dx); ported verbatim")
  and its witness test `the_rotation_uses_the_swapped_atan2` (`:530-537`)
  pin the WRONG value. Player directly right (dx=100, dy=0): C# в†’
  `atan2(0,100) = 0` в†’ rotation 1.57; sibling в†’ `atan2(100,0) = ПЂ/2` в†’
  в‰€3.14. The boss head's roll is wrong on every tick. Fix wave: swap to
  `dy.atan2(dx)` through f64 (`((dy as f64).atan2(dx as f64)) as f32 +
  1.57`) and repoint the witness.
* **G2 вЂ” the spore lift condition is INVERTED (behavioural defect).**
  `NPC.cs:32059-32065`: `num773 = |num772 * 0.2|`; `if (num774 > 0)
  num773 = 0;` then `num774 -= num773` вЂ” the upward lead is subtracted
  ONLY when the jittered dy в‰¤ 0 (target at/above the boss); a target
  below gets NO lift. The sibling (`:414-420`) computes the lead
  correctly but writes `if dy > 0.0 { dy -= lead; }` вЂ” the exact
  opposite gate (its own comment describes the C# correctly; the code
  contradicts it). No witness test covers the spore aim, so the 11
  tests do not catch it.
* **G3 вЂ” the gore burst consumes 6 of the C#'s 12 RNG draws (stream
  drift).** `NPC.cs:32028-32030` draws `Next(width)` then `Next(height)`
  per gore (the sibling ports these, `:394-401`), but `Gore.NewGore`
  itself then draws `Next(10, 31)` (the vy kick) and `Next(-20, 21)`
  (the vx kick) per gore (`Gore.cs:1327-1328`) вЂ” 6 more draws the
  sibling skips with the emit ("documented skip, Brain precedent").
  The ChildSafety re-roll (`Gore.cs:1334-1340`) never fires
  (`ChildSafety.Disabled = true`, `GameContent/ChildSafety.cs:33`), and
  the full-pool early-out that would skip the velocity draws
  (`Gore.cs:1317-1320`) is unreachable in practice (600 slots vs a
  3-gore burst). The shared `Main.rand` stream therefore drifts by 6
  draws at the one-shot shell-break tick (`localAI[2]` latch). The
  sibling's ANALYSIS row "RNG order preserved (2 draws per gore)" is
  inaccurate вЂ” the true order is 4 per gore. Fix wave: draw the two
  kicks per gore (or emit fully-rolled gore requests the wiring inserts
  without re-rolling).
* **G4 вЂ” the first-tick NaN claim is wrong (doc inaccuracy).** The
  sibling's ANALYSIS says the C# "would divide by a zero hook count on
  the very first tick before its own spawns resolve". `NPC.NewNPC`
  activates the slot synchronously (`NPC.cs:80767-80771`,
  `active = true`), and the three hook spawns (`:31739-31741`) run
  BEFORE the centroid scan (`:31747`) in the same `AI()` call вЂ” the
  first tick sees 3 hooks. The 0/0 NaN centroid (`:31761-31762`) arises
  only when ALL hooks are later dead (or the roster was full at init).
  The port's own-centre fallback remains a valid documented stand-in
  either way; only the justification is wrong.
* **G5 вЂ” minor precision seam.** The C#'s distance/aim norms are
  `(float)Math.Sqrt(f32 sum)` вЂ” double sqrt of the f32-promoted sum,
  cast back (`:31799`/`:31820`/`:31934`/`:32066`); the sibling uses f32
  `.sqrt()` throughout (в‰¤1-ulp divergence per call). Same class as
  G1's double-atan2 cast. Recorded for the fix wave, not a structural
  defect.
**Recorded skips confirmed acceptable** (the sibling documents them):
`TargetClosest` (`:31721`) rides the passed-player convention (the
S1-D-3p migration is its own catalog row); the `timeLeft` refresh
(`:31727-31734`, `NPC.activeTime = 750` `:95186`) and `NPC.plantBoss`
(`:31735`) have no port fields; the expert/getGoodWorld arms
(`:31780-31789`, `:31805-31808`, `:31901-31912`, `:31928-31931`,
`:31941-31945`, `:31987-31990`, `:31995-32024`) are constants-off
(single-difficulty classic вЂ” note the ftw wiring wave must also account
for `NewNPC`'s per-spawn `Next(3)` under `Main.getGoodWorld`,
`NPC.cs:80752`); the net-client early returns (`:31876`/`:32033`) fold
out at netMode 0; the stand-in's world-bottom despawn tail is kept as
the port's safety convention.
**Wiring verified on the sibling branch** (by `git show ba8159fc`, not
by execution): `main.rs` declares `mod npc_ai_plantera`; `npc.rs`'s
kind-262 dispatch passes the rng (`NpcKind::Plantera =>
self.update_plantera(world, player, rng)`), the three
`wants_plantera_hooks/_tentacles/_spore` request fields exist and are
initialized; `world_sim/npcs.rs` drains the requests each tick and the
timeLeft-300 list covers 275/276 (not 277); `projectile/data.rs` carries
the 275/276/277 rows (`Projectile.cs:3614-3637`); the stale 480-tick
cycle test is repointed; `anchors.txt` has the `pub fn step` canary row.
The 11 witness tests exist as claimed вЂ” but one pins G1's wrong value,
and there are NO witnesses for the spore aim (G2), the volley RNG order
or the gore draws (G3): the fix wave must add them.
**Follow-ups (the fix/wiring wave, NOT this task)**: G1/G2/G3 corrections

## The aiStyle-63 census (S1-D-3, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)
The 2026-11-18 aiStyle-63 round ran the escape-clause census before porting:
a whole-tree `aiStyle\s*=\s*63` grep over `decompiled/` finds **exactly
one NPC SetDefaults row** вЂ” Flocko, type 352 (`NPC.cs:13471-13487`, the
`aiStyle = 63` at `:13475`; `NPCID.cs:11381` `Flocko = 352`). The only
other hit is `Projectile.cs:4639` (projectile type 379) вЂ” the projectile
machine's own style space, out of NPC scope. There is no named `AI_063`
method: the arm is the inline `else if (this.aiStyle == 63)` block of
`NPC.AI` (`NPC.cs:33971-34018`), and it carries **no per-type branch** вЂ”
the whole family is one kind. The two other `type == 352` sites are
non-AI (the HitEffect dust burst `:84776-84783` and the GetAlpha
white-200 tint `:93593-93595`).
**Census verdict: Flocko only в†’ no non-frost kind to port, so no
`npc_ai_style63.rs` was created.** The round is the docs-only
distrust-verbatim audit of the sibling's coverage: `5ef9b24b`
(`task/S1-F-13c-mob-ai`, S1-F-13c slice D, in flight вЂ” NOT an ancestor of
main, verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 1) ports the arm as
`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_frost_mob.rs::flocko_ai`. The audit read the
whole arm against the sibling's fn line-for-line and found it
**faithful**:
* `:33973` `TargetClosest()` вЂ” the sibling documents it as the caller's
  job (the `FrostTarget` seam); the wiring runs
  `npc_target::target_closest` (S1-D-3p, already on main).
* `:33974-33981` вЂ” `num953 = 11f`; `vector120 = Center + (direction*20,
  +6)`; the aim deltas use the player's `position.X + width*0.5f` and
  `Center.Y` (the CENTER, unlike the ElfCopter's chase which uses
  position.Y); normalise by `11f/dist`. The sibling replays each op in
  the same order; `FrostMobState::center()` = `position + size*0.5`
  (`Entity.cs:50-55`'s float halves вЂ” identical for the even 54x54 /
  20x42 boxes).
* `:33982-33986` вЂ” the day reversal is the literal `0f - num954` /
  `0f - num955` (kept as `0.0 - x`, not `-x` вЂ” same IEEE result, same
  shape).
* `:33987-34004` вЂ” `ai[0]--` runs BEFORE the latch test; the latch
  `dist < 200 || ai[0] > 0` re-arms `ai[0] = 20` only inside 200px, sets
  `direction` from the velocity sign (`vx < 0 в†’ -1` else `+1` вЂ” zero
  goes `+1`), `rotation += direction * 0.3f` and RETURNS (velocity
  untouched). The sibling matches, early return included.
* `:34005-34016` вЂ” the three SEQUENTIAL lerp tiers, each re-reading the
  just-written velocity: 50/51 always, then 10/11 if `dist < 350`, then
  7/8 if `dist < 300` (so inside 300px all three fire in order вЂ” the
  sibling's witness `flocko_chases_with_the_three_lerp_tiers` replays
  exactly this chain in C# f32 ops).
* `:34017` вЂ” `rotation = velocity.X * 0.15f` (assignment, not `+=`).
Defaults check: `FrostMobState::new` seeds direction 1 (`Entity.cs:20`
`public int direction = 1`), ai/localAI zeroed, and the (54, 54, 1.0,
450) row matches `NPC.cs:13473-13478` (the 54x54 box, lifeMax 450; scale
unset = 1). The full stat row (dmg 75, def 8, kb 0.4, value 500,
noGravity + noTileCollide, npcSlots 2, coldDamage, `:13476-13486`)
belongs to workers A/B's SetDefaults tables вЂ” the sibling's module
header records that split.
**RNG argument (by construction):** the arm draws no `Main.rand.Next` вЂ”
every value is a deterministic aim/lerp/counter computation, and
`TargetClosest` is the deterministic Manhattan scan
(`NPC.cs:77652-77781`, ported as `npc_target.rs`). `flocko_ai` therefore
takes no RNG parameter and cannot perturb any stream; the sibling's
dispatch (`frost_mob_ai_step`) passes `rng` only to the ElfCopter's shot
arm (style 62, the six draws `:33960-33967`), never to 63.
**Main-side state (this round's grep):** the style axis (`npc.rs:3255`)
claims only 5; `npc/data.rs::ai_style` carries no 63 row and no
`NpcKind::Flocko` exists (the `BoundGoblin => 63` hit at
`npc/data.rs:347` is the internal `to_u16` save id, NOT aiStyle вЂ”
BoundGoblin's aiStyle is 0, `:1476`). So on main aiStyle 63 is MISSING;
the faithful coverage lands when the sibling branch merges with workers
A/B's kinds/defaults + the wiring (`npc_target::target_closest` at the
`:33973` call site, the noGravity/noTileCollide direct integration). The
Flocko `FindFrame` arm (`:72413+`) stays deferred with the sibling's
other animation arms. The sibling was NOT touched by this round
(byte-identical on its branch); no compiler was invoked вЂ” the audit is
read-only against `git show 5ef9b24b:...`.

## The roller family's aiStyle-39 arm (S1-D-3 aiStyle-39, 2026-11-19)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style39.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s
`else if (this.aiStyle == 39)` block (`NPC.cs:29145-29665`) вЂ” the
GiantTortoise 153, IceTortoise 154, GiantShelly/2 496/497 and SolarSroller
417 вЂ” as a pure `style39_step(npc, world, ctx, players, rng)` over the
`Style39Context`/`Style39Type` seam. **Code-only mode: no compiler
invoked; the 13 witness tests are written, not run.** The module is
UNWIRED вЂ” `update_rng`'s style axis and the live
`npc.rs::update_solar_sroller` are byte-identical; the dispatch claim is
the wiring follow-up (the same landing shape as the aiStyle-28 round).

**Verdict that forced the module**: the live `update_solar_sroller`
(`npc.rs:10451-10517`) is APPROXIMATE вЂ” it invents a `5 + ai[2]*0.6` roll
speed and a `60*ai[2]` tick exit, counts the shelly `+0.5` wind-up rate on
417 (the C# uses `++`, `:29403`), never changes the height (the C#
collapses 52в†’32 at `:29414-29416` and restores at `:29638-29640`, both
feet-planted), writes no damage/knockback, uses `vx*0.05` rotation
instead of the В±ПЂ/10-clamped `vx/10*direction` (`:29632`), and has no
CanHit launch/aim, cliff probe, step-up probe, justHit reset, wet gates or
bounce FX. The other four kinds are unported entirely.

**Faithful pieces** (each cited at its site in the module): the head
step-up probe (`:29161-29202`) is the arm's OWN six-tile column probe вЂ”
NOT `Collision.StepUp` (that writes stepSpeed 1/2, `:59938/:59942`; this
one writes 0.75/1.5, `:29193/:29197`), with the halfbrick В±8 surface
offsets and the f64 `<= 16.1` lift gate; the raw `Main.tileSolid`/
`tileSolidTop` table reads (no `inActive()` conjunct вЂ” unlike
`collision.rs::solid`), `Framing.GetTileSafely`'s fresh-tile fallback
(`Framing.cs:426-439`); the `justHit && type != 417` reset
(`:29203-29208`); the cliff probe's f64 FLOAT-half centre
(`:29288/:29293`) vs the step-up probe's INTEGER half (`:29163`); the
shelly `&` (non-short-circuit) aggro gates and the state-0 early return
(`:29341`); the difficulty helpers вЂ” `GetAttackDamage_LerpBetweenFinalValues`
(`:7047-7050`) is `(int)Utils.Remap(difficulty, 1, 2, normal, expert)`
with the clamped `GetLerpValue` (`Utils.cs:315-348`), and
`GetKnockbackMultiplier_ScaledByDifficulty` (`:7031-7034`) samples the
Classic(1)в†’1 / Master(3)в†’0.8 `LinearCurve` (`GameDifficultyData.cs:86`,
the `Sample` operation order `(value-key.input)*num2/num + key.output`
kept verbatim, `:35-54`); the lunge's double `ai[1]++` on the launch tick
(`:29439/:29446` вЂ” the first flight tick sees 2), the 0.3 spin seed
applied on BOTH the launch line and the shared tail (`:29445/:29505`),
the `ai[3]` vx latch with the в€’0.22 pull and the Г—0.8 over-player release
(`:29480-29493`); the ball's Г—0.9 release with NO latch (`:29614-29621`),
the `ai[2] == 0 || ai[1] >= 1200` exit (`:29622`), and the wet override
that runs AFTER the unroll's 30-tick exit and wins the same tick
(`:29659-29663`).

**RNG argument**: the arm DOES draw `Main.rand`, so the fn takes
`rng: &mut UnifiedRandom` and consumes every arm-level draw in C# order:
`Next(10) == 0` (`:29212`, the 154 head dust gate), `Next(2, 5)`
(`:29418`, the ball revolutions), `Next(3) < 2` (`:29424` the 154 lunge
gate, `:29537` the ball dust gate), and on the bounce FX layer
(`ai[3] > 0`): per gore Г—4 on `ai[3] == 1` the `Next(100)` Г—2 offsets +
`Next(61, 64)` type + `Next(-10, 11)` Г—2 nudges (`:29564-29567`, 20
draws), then `NextFloat()` Г—5 per FX tick (`:29573` вЂ” the draw runs even
when `NewDust` refuses the spawn, the C# reads the dust slot either way).
The witnesses `the_ball_fx_layer_consumes_the_cited_draws` and
`the_ice_tortoise_gates_consume_their_draws` clone the RNG and replay the
exact draw sequence. **Documented deviation**: the dust/gore SPAWNS are
unmodelled (the NPC dust call sites are the outstanding S1-E-1/E-4
caller coverage, "Dust & gore" above); their pool-internal draws
(`Dust.cs:116-206`, `Gore.cs:1327-1328`'s `Next(10, 31)` then
`Next(-20, 21)`) ride the pool's `DustRng` seam when the spawns land вЂ”
the arm-level gates/arguments above are NOT skipped.

**Documented stand-ins and no-ops**: `gfxOffY`/`stepSpeed`/
`knockBackResist` ride the context (the port's `Npc` has no such fields вЂ”
the same convention as style28); `justHit` rides `ctx.just_hit` (the
wiring maps `hurt_cd > 0` вЂ” a widening: the C# flag lasts one tick,
cleared at `:90516`); `this.type`/`defDamage`/`defDefense` ride
`Style39Type` (the `SetDefaults` rows `:10936-10937/:10951-10952/
:14682-14683/:15360-15361`); the `noGravity = false` write (`:29496`) is
a cited no-op (all five kinds default `noGravity = false` and no style
code arms it true); the `position В± netOffset` pairs around the dust
spawns cancel exactly and only offset the unmodelled spawn positions.

**Caller-owned (the wiring round)**: the position integration + gravity
(`:90459-90472`), the `gfxOffY` ease-down (`:90396-90419`), the
`Collision_MoveSolarSroller` bounce pass (`:92736-92757` вЂ” `ai[2]--`,
`ai[3] = 1`, the Г—0.9 `oldVelocity` reflection + direction flip while
`ai[2] > 0`; this is where the ball's revolutions are spent вЂ” the AI arm
only READS `ai[2] == 0`), and `FindFrame`'s style-39 tail (`:77292+`:
`type != 417` zeroes the rotation, `frameCounter += |vx| * 1.1`, the 6-px
frame bands). The four unported kinds (153/154/496/497) ride
`Style39Type` + `size_override` until their `NpcKind`s land.
## The aiStyle-26 tails (S1-F-13b2 slice B, 2026-11-19, code-only mode)

(`projectile/data.rs`) and its `mod` declaration.

Ported, each with its C# cite in the file:
- **FindFrame case 315** (`NPC.cs:74465-74497`): the В±1 turn dead-band

## The Plantera hook-centroid anchor (S1-D-3-plantera-minions, rescoped, code-only mode, 2026-11-18)

**Rescope (Lead coordination note):** the three minion machines were
already ported by sibling branches while this task ran вЂ” kind 263
PlanterasHook (aiStyle 52) in `npc_ai_style52.rs` (commit 61e1bd5c,
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle52`), kind 264 PlanterasTentacle (aiStyle 53) in
`npc_ai_style53.rs` (89a9b808, `task/S1-D-3-aistyle53`), kind 265 Spore
(+261 FungiSpore, aiStyle 50) in `npc_ai_style50.rs` (613aac92,
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle50`). The duplicated machines written here were
REMOVED; the only remaining gap was the boss's leash-anchor
computation вЂ” none of the four modules computes it (the boss core
`npc_ai_plantera.rs`, ba8159fc `task/S1-D-3-plantera-audit`, only
RECEIVES `hook_anchor: (f32, f32)`; its sim currently passes Plantera's
own centre). This task delivers exactly that seam.

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_plantera_anchor.rs` ports `NPC.cs:31743-31762`
(the anchor block inside the aiStyle-51 boss arm) as pure fns over the
NPC pool:

- `hook_centroid(npcs, type_of) -> Option<(f32, f32)>` вЂ” walk the slots
  in order (`:31747`), take the first three live aiStyle-52 hooks
  (`:31749`, the `num745 > 2` break `:31755-31758`), sum their
  `Npc::center()`s as f32 in slot order (`:31751-31752`), divide by the
  count (`:31761-31762`). aiStyle 52 has ONE member вЂ” 263
  (`ID/NPCID.cs:11203`, `SetDefaults :12402`) вЂ” so the filter rides the
  caller's `type_of` closure, the SAME convention `npc_ai_style52.rs`
  uses for its `:32129` same-type scan.
- `hook_anchor(npcs, type_of, boss) -> (f32, f32)` вЂ” the merge-union
  call site: the centroid when hooks live, the boss centre otherwise.

Faithful details: `Center` is `Entity.Center`'s FLOAT width/2
(`Entity.cs:50-55`, the port's `Npc::center()`) вЂ” NOT the tentacle
anchor's integer-width centre (`:32301-32302`); the sums accumulate in
slot order before the divide; `array2` (`:31743`/`:31753`) is a DEAD
store (written, never read anywhere in the arm вЂ” verified) and is not
ported; the block draws NO RNG.

Deliberate deviations:

- **`NPC.active` в†’ `hp > 0`** вЂ” the pool's live-slot convention, the
  same reading `npc_ai_style52.rs` uses for the boss slot
  (`:32080-32085`); absent slots do not exist in the dense pool.
- **Zero hooks в†’ `None` + boss-centre fallback**: the C# divides by a
  zero count в†’ NaN (`:31761-31762`) and the leash reads NaN; the port
  returns `None` and `hook_anchor` falls back to Plantera's own centre
  вЂ” the sibling boss module's documented stand-in until hooks spawn.
- **WIRED at the union (2026-11-19, merger P5)**: the sim's pre-pass
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs`, before the tick closure вЂ” the carrier pre-pass
  precedent) computes `hook_centroid(&app.npcs, type_of)` per live
  Plantera and stores it on the new `Npc::plantera_hook_anchor:
  Option<(f32, f32)>` field; `update_plantera` consumes it with
  `unwrap_or_else(|| self.center())`. `type_of` reads `kind.to_u16()`
  (no NpcKind maps to 263 yet), so the centroid stays `None` вЂ” the
  wiring is live, the boss-centre stand-in persists until the hook
  kind lands with `npc_ai_style52`. The module-level
  `#![allow(dead_code)]` is removed (`hook_centroid` is live; the
  `hook_anchor` convenience wrapper keeps a fn-level allow вЂ” the sim
  stores the Option, the fallback lives in `update_plantera`). The
  pre-pass scans the pool once per tick vs the C#'s inside-the-AI scan:
  same tick's positions either way (the boss's own movement integrates
  after the AI), recorded as the port's pre-pass convention.

**THE MERGE UNION (four modules, no file overlap).** At merge, the
sim's kind-262 dispatch replaces the centre fallback with
`hook_anchor(&app.npcs, type_of, boss)` and passes the result into
`npc_ai_plantera::step`'s `hook_anchor` parameter. No edit to any of the
four sibling modules (`npc_ai_plantera.rs`, `npc_ai_style52.rs`,
`npc_ai_style53.rs`, `npc_ai_style50.rs`) is needed вЂ” this module is
new and disjoint. The sibling branches are NOT merged to main yet
(verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for all four); the union rides
their merge order, and this branch touches none of their files.

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style41.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s
`else if (this.aiStyle == 41)` block (`NPC.cs:29899-30159`) as a pure
function (`style41_step`) over `Npc`, keyed on the C# type id. The
three kinds вЂ” the Herpling 174 (`SetDefaults` `NPC.cs:11194-11207`:
52x26, damage 65, defense 26, lifeMax 220, kb 0.3, value 450), the
Derpling 177 (`:11238-11251`: 58x44, damage 80, defense 26, lifeMax
300, kb 0.5, value 500) and the Chattering Teeth Bomb 378
(`:13825-13838`: 20x26, damage 120, defense 30, lifeMax 200, kb 0.5,
value 450; `ID/NPCID.cs:11025`/`:11031`/`:11433`) вЂ” have NO `NpcKind`
variants yet, so unlike the aiStyle-28 round there is no live arm to
make unreachable: the module lands unwired (the aiStyle-28 pattern)
and the kinds + the `update_rng` `41 =>` dispatch claim are the
follow-up. **Code-only mode**: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests were run;
the 14 witness tests are written, not executed. The only hot-file
touch is `Npc.ai_action` (`NPC.aiAction`, `NPC.cs:6449`, the int
default 0) вЂ” the arm's windup frame hint (`:30112`, `FindFrame`'s
frame-4 row `:66701-66704`) had no port field.

Faithfulness points the port keeps:

- `base.direction *= -base.direction` (`:29988`) is a SET TO -1
  (dir * -dir = -dirВІ = -1 for В±1), NOT a flip вЂ” kept literally.
- The explosion re-centring (`:29929-29934`) adds the OLD box's
  INTEGER half-extents (`base.width / 2` вЂ” 20/2 = 10, 26/2 = 13) then
  subtracts the NEW 160 box's halves (80): the net shift is
  (-70, -67) on the first explosion tick and (0, 0) afterwards.
- The windup bonus computes `400 / dist` FIRST then Г—10 (non-177) /
  Г—5 (177) (`:30039-30040` вЂ” the multiply order matters in f32), caps
  at 30 and truncates with the C# unchecked `(int)` cast (`:30045`):
  NaN/В±inf в†’ `int.MinValue` (the x86 `cvttss2si`), not Rust's
  saturating `as i32` (`csharp_int_cast`).
- The band bonus is STRICT on both ends (`num614 < 350f &&
  num614 > 200f`, `:30059`/`:30071`/`:30089`/`:30101`).
- The f64 deadbands are kept: В±0.1 on the grounded walk (`:30023`)
  and the airborne accel/damp gate (`:30137`/`:30149`).
- The 378 arming is an `if` and the wet bounce an `else if`
  (`:29974`/`:29984`) вЂ” an unarmed bomb NEVER runs the wet bounce;
  the Derpling (177) is excluded from it entirely.
- The wet floor bounce reads `oldVelocity.Y` (`:29994`, captured
  pre-resolve at `NPC.cs:92538`): rising в†’ 5, else в€’2 вЂ” then the
  buoyancy damps above 4 (Г—0.95), lifts 0.3 and caps at в€’4.
- The ai[3] stuck detector (`:30016-30020`) flips the direction and
  arms ai[2] = 300; the hop re-aim only runs while ai[2] == 1
  (`:30049-30052`), so the 300-tick cooldown keeps the flipped side.
- `aiAction = 1` (`:30112`) is never cleared inside the arm вЂ” the
  C# quirk is kept (`Npc.ai_action` latches).
- The AI/integration split: the C#'s three `return`s (`:29971`,
  `:29981`, `:30120`) exit `AI()` only вЂ” `UpdateNPC` still integrates
  afterwards. `style41_step` runs `ai_041_body` then the generic
  integration on EVERY path: gravity 0.3 / maxFallSpeed 10
  (`UpdateNPC_UpdateGravity`, `NPC.cs:90880-90881` вЂ” NOT the port's
  generic 0.4/8, a pre-existing deviation outside this task), the
  В±0.005 f64 X deadband (`:90473-90476`), the wet 0.5 slowdown
  (`Collision_MoveWhileWet`, `:92785-92804`, `waterMovementSpeed`
  `:6015`), the `oldVelocity` capture (`:92538`) and the
  `collideX`/`collideY` changed-axis latches (`:92597-92604`).

Documented stand-ins: `NPC.wet` rides the port's `is_wet` (any water
tile overlapping the body вЂ” the swimmer's stand-in; honey/lava/
shimmer wet unported); `Main.player[this.target]` reads the one
session player (the C# reads slot 255's inactive zero player before
the first pick вЂ” the airborne `target >= 255` return is kept
literally); `life = -1; HitEffect(); active = false` (`:29966-29968`)
rides the hp-0 death convention (the sim's retain drops it); the
tile resolve is the axis-separated `collides_rect` stand-in (the
frost-legion shape; slopes/platforms unported like every family arm);
the `netOffset` add/subtract pairs net to zero and are omitted; the
`EverLastingTicker` stamp passes 0 (the S1-D-3p stand-in).

**RNG by construction**: every `Main.rand` draw in the arm rides an
emission the port skips вЂ” (1) the 378 fuse trail gate `Next(3)`
(`:29916`) is the gate OF the dust spawn; (2) the `ai[2] > 7`
explosion burst's 8 + 32Г—2 `Dust.NewDust` rolls and the 2 gore
iterations' `Next(100)`Г—2 / `Next(61, 64)` / `Next(-10, 11)`Г—2
(`:29939-29958`); (3) the sounds (`:29961` Item14, `:30083` style
29/124 вЂ” the `LegacySoundPlayer` pitch jitter draws ride the audio
pass, `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:613-632`). Skipping the emissions skips
their draws (the S1-D-3e/f/9 dust precedent), so `style41_step`
takes no RNG parameter and cannot perturb any stream; the witness
`s1_d_3_s41_the_arm_is_deterministic_without_an_rng` pins 200 steps

  to a flat 300. The port restores the real draw вЂ” exactly ONE `Next(600)`
  per phase-1 tick (the C# evaluates the comparison's right-hand side

  `s1_d_3_s46_the_arm_draws_one_next_600_per_phase1_tick`.

## The Angry Nimbus' aiStyle-49 machine (S1-D-3, UNWIRED, code-only mode, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style49.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s
`else if (this.aiStyle == 49)` arm (`NPC.cs:31587-31650`) вЂ” the Angry
Nimbus (250, `NPCID.cs:11177`), the style's ONLY user (`SetDefaults`
case 250, `NPC.cs:12221-12233`). **Code-only mode**: no compiler invoked
(no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests); the 9 witness tests are WRITTEN NOT RUN.

**The machine, verbatim.** Every tick: `noGravity = true` (`:31589`),
`TargetClosest()` (`:31590`, through the shared `npc_target::target_closest`,
S1-D-3p вЂ” the inline slot-0 candidate, the `update_zombie` convention;
the `session_candidate` seam lives only on the unmerged style-42 branch),
then the aim at the player's centre with the y offset **в€’200f** (`:31595`
вЂ” the cloud hovers 200 px ABOVE the player), normalized to the 4f speed
(`:31591`/`:31604-31606`) unless the distance is strictly `< 20f`, in
which case the CURRENT velocity is the aim (`:31597-31601`). Each axis
approaches the aim by В±0.25f (`:31592`), with the extra В±0.5f while the
velocity still points the other way (`:31611-31613`/`:31619-31621` on x,
`:31627-31629`/`:31635-31637` on y) вЂ” all comparisons strict.

**The rain window** (`:31640-31648`): the cloud's box horizontally spans
the player's box, its bottom edge is strictly ABOVE the player's top,
`Collision.CanHit` (the port's Manhattan walk, `projectile::can_hit`,
`Collision.cs:381-479`) and `Main.netMode != 1` в†’ `ai[0]++`; at
`ai[0] > 8f` (strict вЂ” the 9th qualifying tick) reset to 0 and fire the
Rain projectile **264**: X = `(int)(position.X + 10f + Next(width - 20))`
(width 34 в†’ `Next(14)`, 0..=13), Y = `(int)(position.Y + height + 4f)`,
SpeedX 0, SpeedY 5, Damage 20, KnockBack 0. The shot rides the plain
`Npc::wants_hostile_shot` list (the C# call passes no `ai0`/`ai1`); the
drain (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) spawns it with knockback 0. The 264
`SetDefaults` row (`Projectile.cs:3491-3502`: 4Г—40, aiStyle 45, hostile,
penetrate в€’1, timeLeft 120, scale 1.1, extraUpdates 1, ignoreWater) and
the projectile aiStyle-45 arm itself are M4-PROJ work вЂ” the request
carries the cited kind/position/velocity/damage only.

**RNG order (by construction).** The arm's ONLY `Main.rand` draw is the
shot's x pick (`:31646`), drawn AFTER the `ai[0] = 0` reset and BEFORE
`Projectile.NewProjectile`. `TargetClosest` (`:77652-77781`) draws
nothing. So `angry_nimbus_ai` takes the caller's `UnifiedRandom` and
consumes exactly one `next_max(14)` per fired shot, zero otherwise вЂ”
witnessed by `s1_d_3_s49_the_stream_advances_once_per_shot` (two seeded
streams, 8 non-firing ticks draw-free, the firing tick's x equals the
control's `Next(14)`).

**The movement tail.** Type 250 has no special arm in
`ApplyTileCollision` (`:92612-92627`) в†’ `Collision_MoveNormal`
(`:92723-92726`, plain `Collision.TileCollision`) +
`Collision_MoveWhileDry` (`:92591-92607`: the `Collision.up` 0.01f
ceiling nudge, the `collideX`/`collideY` latches off `oldVelocity`, the
`oldPosition` stamp, `position += velocity`). The 250 defaults set
`noGravity` ONLY вЂ” `noTileCollide` stays false, so the cloud DOES
collide with tiles. `Collision_DecideFallThroughPlatforms` includes the
aiStyle-49 row (`:92952-92955`, `fall = true`): the cloud drops through
platforms. `nimbus_step` ports the dry, no-slope path on the stand-in
`collides_rect` walk (the zombie convention: a blocked axis zeroes its
velocity component instead of the C#'s pixel-snap вЂ” the snap lands with
the shared Collision port; the stand-in does not model platforms, so
the wiring passes `fall = true` into the shared `TileCollision`).

**The frame clock.** `FindFrame` case 250 (`NPC.cs:72884-72897`, shared
with the Rain 264 / Sharknado 268): `frameCounter++`, at `>= 6.0` advance
the frame row and reset; wrap at `num * Main.npcFrameCount[250]`.
`Main.npcFrameCount[250] = 4` вЂ” the initializer `Main.cs:67082`, ten
entries per row from `:67084` (ids 0-9), so `:67109` covers ids 250-259
(`4, 3, 5, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 4`) and index 250 is its first entry.
`nimbus_find_frame` is the pure twin over the frame INDEX (the port's
`Npc::frame` convention); the private `frame_counter` reset is the
wiring step inside `npc.rs::find_frame`.

**Deliberate stand-ins / skips.**
- `Main.netMode != 1` (`:31640`) folds to the host path (the port is
  single-player/host) вЂ” the rain gate always passes.
- The thunder ambient roll (`NPC.cs:90111-90113`: type 250,
  `Next(700) == 0` в†’ sound 29 style `Next(41, 44)`) is `UpdateNPC`'s
  sound layer вЂ” unported; when it lands it draws BEFORE the AI arm each
  tick (the RNG-order note for the wiring step).
- The `HitEffect` dust/gore rows (`:88959-88979`: the cloud puff 54
  burst, `dmg / lifeMax * 50` dusts while alive, 20 + the two gore 99s
  on death) are the dust-layer skip (the S1-D-3e/f precedent).
- The wet/slope/conveyor collision halves (`:92545-92562`,
  `:92574-92578`) are unported engine layers.
- The stat row (34Г—26, dmg 50, def 24, 300 HP, kb 0.3, value 300f =
  3 silver, HitSound NPCHit30 / DeathSound NPCDeath33) rides the
  `ANGRY_NIMBUS` cited `NimbusDefaults` const for the wiring step вЂ” no
  `NpcKind::AngryNimbus` exists yet and the kind tables are contested by
  the in-flight S1-D-3 sibling branches, so this slice is UNWIRED (the
  `npc_ai_style42.rs` precedent, `8ac80b4e`): `#![allow(dead_code)]`,
  the `mod npc_ai_style49;` registration, the kind-table rows + the
  `49 =>` dispatch arm are the family's merge step.
## The spore pair (S1-D-3 aiStyle-50, code-only)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style50.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s

so the style axis (`npc.rs:3255`) has no arm to claim; only the one-line

- **Seams**: `Npc` has no `no_tile_collide` field вЂ” the arm's per-tick
  write (false for 261, true for 265) is returned in `Style50Outcome`;
  the FungiSpore's contact death (`:31657-31662`) sets `hp = 0` and
  returns `died_on_contact` (the caller owes `HitEffect(0, 100.0)` +

  `despawnEncouraged` flag (`:7255`) has no port field вЂ” the established
  `encourage_despawn` seam. `Main.expertMode` is a parameter (the port is
  single-difficulty normal, `world.rs:727`); the expert double-damp

- **Not this system**: the *projectile* aiStyle 50 (the spore cloud,

**RNG by construction** вЂ” the arm's only `Main.rand` draws:
1. the ftw reflect re-roll `Next(10)` (`:32245`) вЂ” EVERY getGoodWorld
   tick, drawn BEFORE the `NPC.plantBoss < 0` early return: an orphan

Nothing else draws; the classic orphan path and every steering tick are

**Wiring deferred** (the `npc_ai_style16.rs` fish precedent, 8754ef9f):

- `Main.netMode != 1` в†’ true (single-player port): the rearm block

- `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999, 0f, 0)` (`:32256`) в†’ an

- The boss/anchor slots resolve through `Ai53Ctx` (`Ai53NpcView`): the
  C# reads `Main.npc[NPC.plantBoss]` for the hp bands and

**Faithfulness details pinned by the witnesses** (the W66 defect
classes): the anchor centre halves are INTEGER divisions
(`(float)(width / 2)`, `:32301-32302`); the orbit vector keeps the C#'s
add-then-subtract round-trip (`(centre + ai) - centre`, `:32304-32307` вЂ”
NOT simplified to `ai`, f32 rounding differs at large centres);
`Math.Sqrt` is f64 on the f32 sum with the result cast back BEFORE the
divide (`:32308`) and there is NO zero guard вЂ” at `ai == (0, 0)` the C#
produces NaN and every steering/rotation compare fails, leaving the
state untouched (Rust IEEE reproduces it; a guard would be an
invention); the boss hp bands are DOUBLE compares on `NPC.plantBoss`
(exclusive `<`) while the expert radius term reads the TENTACLE's own
hp in f32 (`:32289`); the steering compares ride `base.position`, not
Center; the X and Y steer pairs are separate if/else-ifs (both axes
steer per tick); the rotation tail is two separate ifs (at
`num797 == 0` neither fires) and the left fold adds the LITERAL `3.14f`,
not PI (`:32367`).
## The legacy minimap light export (S1-E-19 wave B, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode**: this wave was finished under a user directive of file
reads/writes + git only - NO cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs, no dotnet, no
graphify. The tests below are **tests-as-code: written, NOT run**; the wave-A
legacy goldens and the full-suite verification are deferred to the next
build-capable pass. No compiler was invoked.

`crates/tr-core/src/lighting/legacy.rs` gains `try_updating_map_with_light`
(`TryUpdatingMapWithLight`, `LegacyLighting.cs:371-433`) and the `ProcessArea`
gate block (`:341-358`) runs INLINE in `process_area` - before `PreRenderPhase`
resets the count, so the `renderCount == 3` gate sees the C# value. The export
is split along the C#'s own seam:

- `MapLightExport<'a>` borrows the `Main.Map` tile array (`WorldMap._tiles`),
  the `Main.mapTime` counter (`Main.cs:803`), `mapTimeMax` (`Main.cs:801`) and
  the `Main.mapEnabled` gate (`Main.cs:813`). The app's `WorldMap` hands it out
  through `legacy_light_export` (`tr-app/src/map.rs`); the frame driver
  (`app/frame/draw.rs`) attaches it only while a legacy mode is active and
  pushes the returned `changed` list into the map texture's dirty queue
  (`push_dirty`, the `MapRenderer.QueueChange` analog).
- The gate order is verbatim (`:340-358`): `ShiftUnProcessedDataOver` -> the
  `Netplay.Connection.StatusMax > 0` poke `mapTime = 1` (`:341-344`, wired
  from `App.net_status_max`) -> the `mapDelay` countdown (`:345-348`) -> the
  `mapTime == 0 && mapEnabled && renderCount == 3` gate (`:349`). `mapDelay`
  lives ON THE ENGINE (`Main.mapDelay`, `Main.cs:229`, static ctor `= 2` at
  `:66504`, world-load re-arm `WorldGen.cs:6947`); `enter_loaded_world` calls
  `reset_map_delay` (`app/mod.rs`).
- The export body (`:373-432`): the re-arm `mapTime = mapTimeMax` happens
  FIRST (`:373`); the window is the camera's SCALED view
  (`Camera.ScaledPosition/ScaledSize`, `Camera.cs:12-14` - the
  `GameViewMatrix.Translation` offset, `SpriteViewMatrix.cs:149-153`'s
  `Utils.Round` banker's rounding, computed in the driver from `world_zoom`)
  intersected with the requested rect, both clamped with the C#'s max-first
  `Utils.Clamp` (`Utils.cs:223-234`, the shared `wind::cs_clamp`). The walk is
  x-outer/y-inner over the PRESENTED `R/G/B`: max channel, White's 1.5x
  brighten (`IsColorOrWhiteMode`, `Mode < 2`, `:204`/`:416-419`), the
  `(byte)Math.Min(255f, num4 * 255f)` truncation (`:420`), the sky-air 22
  ambient (`:421-424`), the revealed-floor 22 (`:425-428`), then
  `Main.Map.UpdateLighting` (the shared `crate::map::update_map_lighting`,
  `WorldMap.cs:49-63`). `Main.updateMap` (`:432`) rides the seam's
  `update_map` field.
- The C# `try/catch` (`:351-357`) becomes abort-on-out-of-bounds early
  returns: the re-arm at `:373` happens first either way, tiles written
  before the abort persist and `updateMap` stays untouched. The state COLUMN
  is bounds-checked once per `i` BEFORE the inner loop (`:398` reads
  `_states[...]` before the `j` loop) - an out-of-range column aborts even
  when the y range is empty.

Map-side split (`tr-app`): while a legacy mode is active the frame's map
phase runs only the per-frame `Main.mapTime` countdown
(`WorldMap::tick_map_time`, `Main.cs:61818-61821`); the modern
`ExportToMiniMap` countdown/reveal stays inside `WorldMap::update` for Color
mode. The legacy engine owns the export itself - exactly the C# split
(`LightingEngine.ExportToMiniMap` vs `LegacyLighting.TryUpdatingMapWithLight`).

**RNG streams are untouched by construction**: `TryUpdatingMapWithLight`
draws NO random numbers (the whole `:371-433` body is reads, clamps, byte
maths and map writes). The swipe stream keeps its exact order - `NextSeed()`
after every swipe pass (`:1082`), `WithModifier((ulong)(i*1000+j))` +
`Next(98,100)` per wet decay draw (`:1250-1251`) - and the scanner stream
keeps its one `NextSeed()` per `PreRenderPhase` (`:723`). The export runs
between the shift and the sky reseed inside `process_area`, adding no draws
before, between or after them. The witness test
`map_export_keeps_the_rng_streams` drives 20 frames with wet cells beside
the torch (real swipe draws) and asserts byte-identical presented light plus
identical `swipe_rng`/`scanner_rng` seeds against a seam-less run.

Deliberate deviations / deferred callers:
- `Main.updateMap`'s CONSUMER (`Main.cs:61886-61894`, `MapRenderer.DrawToMap`
  of the rect) is not separately ported: the port's texture upload rides the
  per-tile dirty list (`push_dirty` -> `prepare`), which covers the same
  changed tiles. The rect itself is carried on the seam for parity.
- `BlackFadeCameraTeleport`'s `mapTime < 5 -> 5` poke (`Main.cs:62552-62555`)
  has no port caller (the teleport fade is unported); the seam's `map_time`
  borrow is where it will land.
- The `gameMenu` re-arm `mapTime = mapTimeMax` (`Main.cs:61822-61825`) is a
  menu-state concern outside this wave; the in-game countdown is exact.

Tests-as-code (written, NOT run - code-only mode): 7 new
`legacy::tests::map_export_*` (the RNG-stream witness, the delay/count/
renderCount gate schedule, the disabled gate, the netplay pin, White's
1.5x + floor-22 + byte truncation + changed-list order, Retro's raw byte,
the sky-air 22 arm with a wet-cell counterexample) + 1 `tr-app`
`s1_e_19b_the_legacy_light_export_seam_borrows_tiles_and_counter` (the seam
borrows, the countdown floor, the re-arm and tile-write persistence). The
12 wave-A goldens are untouched and must stay green when later run.
## The Creeper family (S1-D-3 aiStyle-55, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style55.rs` ports `NPC.AI`'s whole
`else if (this.aiStyle == 55)` block (`NPC.cs:32657-32741`) as a PURE
velocity machine. **Family identity verified from the C#**: the only
`this.aiStyle = 55;` row in `SetDefaults` is the **Creeper**, type 267
(`NPC.cs:12456-12469`, `NPCID.cs:11211`). The Brain of Cthulhu (266) is
aiStyle **54** (`:12443`) вЂ” style 55 is not a Brain phase-2 arm; it is the
orbiting swarm's own machine, reading the Brain's centre through the static
`NPC.crimsonBoss` slot (set at `:32372` by the Brain's AI head, cleared
at `:8397`/`:95176`). The port's `npc/data.rs` style table already
carried the correct row (`Creeper => 55`, `:1567`).

The arm carries every branch: the brainless despawn (`:32659-32664`),
the orbit state's `ai[1]` reset, the strict `> 90f` ring with the
8-px homeward drift through the 15/16 blend and its early return, the
strict `< 8f` Manhattan amplify (Y then X), the lunge roll
(`:32686`), the `TargetClosest` + reciprocal-first unguarded 8-px aim
(`:32688-32694`), the expert homing steer (the unguarded `Normalize`,
the ftw 12f/49-50 row and the expert 9f/99-100 row, `:32700-32714`), the
strict `> 700f` leash reset (`:32715-32721`), and the `justHit`
recoil with the `knockBackResist == 0f` six-hit counter (`ai[1] > 5f`,
`:32724-32739`).

**RNG by construction** (the `npc_ai_style16` precedent): the arm's only
draws are the lunge roll at `:32686`,
`Main.netMode != 1 && ((Main.expertMode && Main.rand.Next(100) == 0) || Main.rand.Next(200) == 0)`.
Classic: the `&&` short-circuits before `Next(100)` (never drawn);
`Next(200)` is drawn EVERY in-ring state-0 tick, even when the roll
fails. Expert: `Next(100)` every in-ring tick; `Next(200)` only when
the first roll is non-zero (the `||` short-circuits on a zero вЂ” one
draw, not two). The far-orbit return and the whole state-1 tail draw
nothing. The witnesses mirror the cited draws on a cloned
`UnifiedRandom` and compare the full stream state (`PartialEq`),
including a ten-tick replay; a drifted draw count/order fails by
construction once executed.

**Code-only mode**: no cargo/rustc/tests were run on this branch вЂ” the 14
witness tests in the module are WRITTEN, NOT RUN.

**WIRED (S1-D-3 W-2, 2026-11-19, code-only mode вЂ” no compiler invoked):**
the aiStyle axis claims `55 =>` (`npc.rs::ai_055_creeper_family` ->
`ai_055_step`) and the `update_creeper` stand-in is RETIRED (the kind arm
is the axis-unreachable marker, the style-5/9 precedent). The seam feeds
`Ai55Ctx`: `brain_anchor` over the sim's `world.brain_*` write-through,
`npc_target::session_candidate` as the slot-0 candidate,
`player.buffs.expert_mode` (the retaliate convention,
`world_sim/npcs.rs`), `SeedFlags::FOR_THE_WORTHY` for `getGoodWorld` (the
`npc_ai_bat` convention), and the new one-tick `Npc::just_hit` field
(`NPC.cs:6453`) вЂ” armed by the strike paths (`hurt`,
`hurt_from_projectile`, `strike_pooled` вЂ” `strike_melee`/
`strike_projectile` delegate there; `NPC.cs:81274`), read by the arm,
cleared once per `update_rng` after the AI (`NPC.cs:90516`; the clear
sits BEFORE the port's folded-in `contact` pass so a thorns reflect
survives to the next tick's AI like the C#'s player-update strike).
`ticker` stays 0 (the zombie's `target_closest` precedent). The
`Ai55Effects::deactivate` request drains via `EncourageDespawn(0)` вЂ” the
same-tick pool removal (`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s `despawn_expired` retain),
the port's `active = false` shape without the death effects `hp = 0`
would trigger; the sim's `update_brain_state` retain
(`world_sim/npcs.rs:1040`) is the backstop.

**RNG parity of the swap (classic worlds):** the stand-in drew exactly
one `Next(200)` per in-ring state-0 tick and nothing elsewhere; the
faithful arm draws the identical census вЂ” the expert `Next(100)` half
short-circuits BEFORE drawing on classic (`ctx.expert_mode == false`),
the far-orbit return precedes the roll, the state-1 tail draws nothing,
and `TargetClosest`/the aim/`netUpdate` writes are RNG-free. The shared
`UpdateNpcs` stream therefore stays in step on classic worlds (witness
`s1_d_3_w2_the_wired_classic_draw_census_matches_the_mirror`). Expert
worlds gain the C#'s real draw shape (a faithful fix, not a regression).

The wiring witnesses (`npc.rs`, WRITTEN NOT RUN): the repointed
`the_creeper_orbits_brain_and_lunges` (now through the axis arm, plus the
one-tick-flag lifecycle: strike-tick recoil, update-tail clear, the
cooldown tail no longer recoils),
`s1_d_3_w2_the_700_leash_is_live_through_the_axis`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_lunge_retargets_and_syncs_through_the_axis`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_wired_classic_draw_census_matches_the_mirror`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_brainless_creeper_despawns_same_tick`.

The line-by-line audit of the stand-in against the C# block (the W66
defect classes) found these real deviations, all fixed in the module
(and now LIVE via the wiring):
- **Missing 700-px leash** (`:32715-32721`): the stand-in's lunging
  Creepers never drop back to the orbit on distance вЂ” they lunge forever.
- **Missing `TargetClosest`** (`:32688`): the stand-in aims at the
  session player directly, never updating `target`/`targetRect`/
  `direction`/`directionY`/`targetSetFrame`.
- **Invented `.max(1.0)` distance floor**: the C#'s `8f / sqrt` at
  `:32692` is unguarded (a coincident centre gives `inf`/`NaN`);
  the stand-in floors the distance at 1.
- **f32 operation order**: the stand-in computes `dx / d * 8.0`
  (divide-then-multiply); the C# computes `num829 = 8f / d` then
  `dx * num829` (reciprocal-first) вЂ” different rounding (the (15, 20)
  witness fixture discriminates them: 4.7999997 vs 4.8000002).
- **`hurt_cd` vs `justHit`**: the stand-in reads the ~11-tick damage
  cooldown as the recoil gate; the C# reads the ONE-TICK `justHit`
  flag, so a struck Creeper should recoil on the strike tick only.
- **Missing gates/branches**: the `netUpdate` writes (`:32662`,
  `:32696`), the expert/ftw homing steer (`:32700-32714`) and the
  `knockBackResist == 0f` six-hit counter (`:32728-32735`, dead for
  the vanilla Creeper's 0.8f row but part of the arm).

Deliberate folds, all cited in the module:
- `Main.netMode != 1` в†’ true (single-player port) вЂ” on a client the C#
  draws nothing at the roll.
- `NPC.crimsonBoss` в†’ `Ai55Ctx::crimson_boss_center` (`None` = the
  `< 0` despawn), fed by `brain_anchor` over the sim's
  `world.brain_present`/`brain_x`/`brain_y` anchor
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs:993-995`).
- `active = false` leaves as `Ai55Effects::deactivate` (the port's
  `Npc` has no `active` field; the sim's pass retains the Creepers
  away when the Brain dies).
- `NPC.justHit` в†’ the port's `Npc::just_hit` one-tick field (the W-2
  wiring landed it: armed `NPC.cs:81274`, cleared `:90516`; the
  `Ai55Ctx::just_hit` seam carries it into the pure arm вЂ” the
  `Ai16Ctx::just_hit` precedent).
- `Math.Sqrt` keeps the C#'s f32-sum в†’ f64-root в†’ f32-cast shape
  (provably bit-identical to a direct f32 sqrt for this input shape, but
  transcribed literally); `Vector2.Normalize()` is XNA's
  reciprocal-multiply, unguarded.
- Position integration stays OUT of the arm (the C# AI ends before
  `UpdateCollision`).

## The Martian Saucer core audit (S1-D-3 aiStyle-76, code-only)

`NPC.AI()`'s `else if (this.aiStyle == 76)` arm (`NPC.cs:36071-36519`)
was ALREADY ported on main — `npc.rs::update_saucer_core` (M4-EVENT-4e,
2026-11-08), the sole kind being the MartianSaucerCore 395 (the census of
`this.aiStyle = 76;` across `NPC.cs` returns exactly one hit, `:14052`,
the `type == 395` SetDefaults row `:14045-14062`). No new module was
created (the no-parallel-implementations rule); this round is the
distrust-verbatim audit of the live arm against the whole C# block, with
surgical fixes. CODE-ONLY MODE: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; the
11 witness tests (`npc.rs::s1_d_3_s76_audit_tests`) are WRITTEN NOT RUN,
verified by C# re-reading + hand-arithmetic.

The defects found and fixed (each cited to the C# line):

- **The despawn ride was nested under the far gate.** The C#'s
  `if (ai[0] == -1 || ai[0] == -2)` (`:36130`) is its OWN if/else-if
  chain — a core that entered -1/-2 while the player was far keeps
  climbing after the player returns inside the 5600-px window. The v1
  ran the ride only while `far`, freezing the negative phases near the
  player. Fixed: the ride chains off the phase, not the distance.
- **The living-player restore reset -1 to 0.** The C# restores only
  -2 → 2 (`:36137-36140`); the `if (ai[0] == 0) ai[0] = 0;` at
  `:36141-36144` is DEAD code (the phase is -1 or -2 there). The v1's
  `if -2 { 2 } else { 0 }` killed the -1 climb on the first restore
  tick. Fixed: -1 stays -1, the counters still zero (`:36145-36147`).
- **The despawn timers were missing.** `EncourageDespawn(10)`
  (`:36133`, the only-lowering `:7249-7256` write) and the DIRECT
  `timeLeft = 300` (`:36136`, not an EncourageDespawn) now run; the
  dead-player branch takes neither (the `!player19.dead` gate).
- **The vulnerable wobble never dropped the shield.** The C# sets
  `dontTakeDamage = false` at `:36383` (the SetDefaults `true` row
  `:14060` holds until then). The port now models the SetDefaults
  shield at construction (`Npc::new`) and drops it in the wobble —
  the core is unkillable by damage until the crew-dead bridge hands
  it the vulnerable phase (the bridge itself stays the documented
  M4-EVENT-4f follow-up).
- **The gun's 447 dropped its owner payload.** `NewProjectile(..., 447,
  80, 0f, myPlayer, whoAmI + 1)` (`:36437`) — the deathray arm
  (`Projectile.cs:30818`) reads `ai0 - 1` to find its owner. The v1
  pushed the plain shot tuple; the shot now rides
  `wants_hostile_shot_ai` with `ai0 = slot + 1` (the shell's entry
  shot already did, `update_saucer_mount`).
- **The side picks used Rust `signum`.** The band-0 approach's -600
  offset (`:36229`) and the band-2 approach's +300 (`:36285`) multiply
  `Math.Sign`, which returns **0 on the exact tie** — Rust's
  `f32::signum` returns +1 on +0.0, sending the core 600 px the wrong
  way when it sits exactly above the player. The new `math_sign`
  helper carries the C# tie. The band-CHANGE writes (`:36217`,
  `:36433`) use the `Sign(...) == 1 ? 1 : -1` ternary instead — the
  tie folds to -1 there; both forms are pinned by witnesses.
- **The clearance probe dropped `!tileSolidTop`.** The C# predicate is
  `nactive() && tileSolid[type] && !tileSolidTop[type]`
  (`:36247`/`:36256` and the three replicas) — platforms do NOT stop
  the scan. `ground_clearance` now carries the term (the Dutchman's
  `:38908`/`:38917` probe shares the helper, same predicate), and the
  row-0 landing keeps the C#'s literal `count--` shape (the v1 clamped
  it to 0). The probe columns are the C#'s cast-then-divide
  (`(int)Center.X / 16`, `(int)(position.Y + height) / 16`,
  `:36244-36245`), not divide-then-cast.
- **The dive/park/dash Y targets were inverted at low clearance.** The
  C# eases toward -4 but caps the steepness at the clearance
  (`0f - num1111 > num1110` → `-clearance`, `:36266-36270`,
  `:36347-36351`, `:36481-36485`): a 0-px clearance eases toward 0,
  not -4. The v1's `-(clear.max(-4.0))` ran -0/-4 backwards. Fixed in
  all three arms.
- **The wobble rotation ran f32 cos of 6.283.** `RotatedBy` takes a
  DOUBLE and computes `(float)Math.Cos(radians)` (`Utils.cs:1675-1684`)
  on the promoted f32 angle; the angle literal is
  `(float)Math.PI * 2f` = TAU, not 6.283. The three cosine bands now
  promote to f64 and use TAU; the 120+ raw-angle band uses TAU too.
- **The gun chase had an invented zero guard.** The C#'s
  `vector154.Normalize()` (`:36454`) has NO `.max(0.001)` floor — the
  port's guard is gone (the approach arms' <50/<70 gates make their
  zero vectors unreachable; the chase's exact-coincidence NaN is the
  C#'s own behaviour, carried verbatim).
- **The netUpdate writes were missing** (`:36116`, `:36128`, `:36148`,
  `:36223`, `:36392`, `:36441`, `:36449`, `:36517`) — all landed.

RNG by construction: the whole arm draws NO `Main.rand` — no
`Next`/`NextFloat` anywhere in `:36071-36519`; `NewNPC`'s only draw is
the getGoodWorld gate (`:80752`, constants-off in the port);
`TargetClosest` (`:77652-77781`) is the deterministic Manhattan scan
(now riding `npc_target::target_closest`, style 76, the S1-D-3p
helper); `EncourageDespawn` and the 9999 instant-kill
`StrikeNPCNoInteraction` path (`:81237`'s `Damage >= 9999 &&
owner == 255` flag — no loot/dust/combat-text draws) draw nothing. The
`rng` parameter stays for the dispatch signature, untouched; the
witness `s1_d_3_s76_audit_the_arm_draws_no_rng` pins a `UnifiedRandom`
state across all six scan bands, the wobble, the gun and both rides.

Documented folds (unchanged from M4-EVENT-4e): the off-world
`active = false` (`:36516`) folds to hp=0 through the death pass; the
classic-only constants (no expert difficulty flags in the arm itself —
the 80 damage is the literal `num1126`); the crew spawn's
`localAI[0..3]` sibling slots ride the pre-pass write-through (the
port's link model). The shell's missile battery + the classic/expert
phase bridge remain the M4-EVENT-4f follow-ups — with the shield now
modelled, the core is damage-immune until that bridge lands (the C#
behaviour; the v1 let the player kill the shielded core outright).

### Faithfulness traps kept (the W66/W94 catalogue)

- **Draw-before-early-return**: `spriteDirection = -(int)this.ai[0]`
  (the TRUNCATED int negation) is the FIRST write in all three arms
  (`:28247/:28524/:28759`), BEFORE the head-gone despawn gate вЂ” the
  port writes `sprite_dir` first too (witness tests pin it on the
  despawn tick).
- **Two different centres**: the band comparisons use INTEGER
  half-widths (`(float)(width / 2)` on both entities) while the
  dock/aim vectors use the FLOAT centre (`width * 0.5f`) вЂ” kept
  distinct (`half_w` vs `dock_vector`).
- **f64-on-f32**: `Math.Sqrt`/`Math.Atan2` are DOUBLE calls on f32
  operands вЂ” the port computes `((x*x + y*y) as f64).sqrt() as f32`
  and `(y as f64).atan2(x as f64) as f32` (`cs_sqrt`/`cs_atan2`);
  the sums/products stay f32 and the `speed / (float)Math.Sqrt(...)`
  divisions are f32 divides of an f64-rounded sqrt. The literal
  `1.57f`, not FRAC_PI_2.
- **Strict bounds**: the hysteresis >800/<400, the snap |vx|+|vy|<2,
  the rise gate y<head.Yв€’280, the В±500 centre gate, the state-5
  playerCentreв€’100 condition, and ALL four shot cadences (>140, >40,
  >200, >80 вЂ” the ++ runs first, so equality holds) are STRICT, pinned
  by boundary witness tests.
- **Dead stores annotated**: the vice's `num516` (`:28432`),
  `num519`'s first value (`:28444`, the name is reused for the dash
  scale at `:28460`), `num522`'s first value (`:28487`, reused at
  `:28502`), and the cannon's `num531` head-Y read (`:28693`,
  overwritten at `:28694`) вЂ” kept verbatim, no observable effect. The
  cannon's `num525`/`num532` and the laser's `num539`/`num546`
  ARE read (the shot normalisers) вЂ” not dead.
- **No epsilon floor**: the normalisers divide by the distance
  verbatim вЂ” a zero distance yields the C#'s NaN/Inf (the live arm
  floors at 0.001; the port does not). The cannon's reversed vector is
  `(0f в€’ num) * scale` verbatim (`-0.0` preserved).
- **No integration**: all three are noTileCollide, so `UpdateNPC`
  integrates `position += velocity` after `AI()`
  (`NPC.cs:90498`); the step fns do not move the limb.
- **Despawn fall-through = early return**: `ai[2] += 10` per tick,

  tick); after the kill `ai[2]` is 10 or в‰Ґ60 so no state branch

### RNG by construction

The vice arm draws NO `Main.rand` вЂ” every counter is deterministic;
`style34_step` takes no RNG parameter and the dispatcher witness
pins the stream bit-identical after a vice tick. The cannon and laser
each draw exactly TWO `Main.rand.Next(-40, 41)` values (X then Y) per
FIRED shot вЂ” the reversed-dock bomb `:28669-28670`, the player bomb
`:28748-28749`, the hover volley `:28904-28905`, the flank volley
`:28982-28983` вЂ” and nothing else. Both draws sit INSIDE
`Main.netMode != 1` AND the STRICT `localAI[0] >` threshold, so a
client or a non-firing tick draws ZERO; `UnifiedRandom::next_range`
is the exact `Next(min, maxExclusive)` stream
(`Utilities/UnifiedRandom.cs:120-132`). The stream-clone witness
tests pin the exact draw count and order per firing tick and the
zero-draw gates. The despawn's `HitEffect()` reaches the
type-128..131 gore arm (`NPC.cs:89433-89469`) whose four
`Main.rand.Next(61, 64)` picks (`:89452/:89456/:89460/:89464`) are
COSMETIC gore вЂ” the dust/gore skip precedent (S1-D-3e/f/g and the saw
sibling), so the despawn draws nothing. `npc_target::target_closest`
is RNG-free. The shots ride `Npc::wants_hostile_shot` (the style-28
seam); the C#'s knockback `0f` and `Main.myPlayer` owner are the
tuple's documented non-carried fields.

`localAI[0]` threshold вЂ” a non-firing tick draws nothing. The wiring
witnesses assert the stream state through `update_rng` (clone-before
/ replay-two-draws), so the retirement cannot silently shift the
shared stream. The despawn's HitEffect gore stays the cosmetic skip.

## The atlas skyline packer (S1-G-12b, 2026-11-19, code-only)

**The bound.** The renderer draws ONE atlas through one instanced sprite
pipeline (AGENTS.md rendering invariant; research/41 D-3 вЂ” the C# itself is
per-texture, `TileBatch.cs:485-536`, so the packing algorithm is
port-infrastructure, not game logic). The atlas is 8192 px wide and must stay
в‰¤ 8192 px tall (the strict-GPU max 2D dimension). The landed best-fit
decreasing-height shelf packer (S1-F-13c slice B) held the main sheet set at
~8121 px вЂ” 71 px of headroom. Two branches were SKIP-blocked on it:
`task/S1-E-4b-gore-draw` adds ~1400 `Gore_<id>` sheets
(`AssetInitializer.cs:135-137`, the `Main.DrawGore` source
`Main.cs:21873-21907`) and `task/S1-L-8b-mount-data` adds 25
`STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` rows (the Drill glow strips, the mount GlowMasks
283/284/285/370, the corrected minecart file names, the S1-L-9 land-mount
sheets).

**Measured heights** (`tools/atlas_sim.js` вЂ” reads the REAL sheet dims out
of the retail `.xnb` files through an LZX decoder ported from
`crates/tr-content/src/lzx.rs`, mirrors the `assets.rs` enumeration
including `proj_data`'s range arms and the two branches' additions; no
compiler invoked). The sim's best-fit shelf height on the main set is
8117 px vs the recorded 8121 вЂ” a 4 px census residual (a handful of sheets
whose decode the sim skips), immaterial to the bound decision:

| sheet set | best-fit shelves (main) | first-fit shelves (E-4b) | skyline waste | skyline span | maxrects BAF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (test world, 7826 sheets) | 8117 | 8117 | **7289** | 7251 | 7070 |
| main + gore (9228 sheets) | 8493 OVERFLOW | 8493 OVERFLOW | **7680** | 7643 | 7462 |
| main + gore + mount + font (9254 sheets) | 8664 OVERFLOW | 8664 OVERFLOW | **7932** | 8091 | 7601 |

**The choice: skyline bottom-left, waste tie-break** (option 1 of the task
brief). Each rect tries every skyline node's left edge; the placement y is
the max skyline height over the span; the winner minimises `(y, waste, x)`
вЂ” bottom-left first, then the least area buried under the rect, then
leftmost. All keys are integers and the scan order is fixed, so the layout
is a pure function of the input list (the world-swap `build_ref` contract).
The skyline backfills the width tails the shelf pass strands per row вЂ” the
exact failure mode the ~1400 same-band gore sheets exposed. The span
tie-break was evaluated and rejected: it wins on the smaller sets but packs
the critical combined set at 8091 px (only 101 px headroom) vs the waste
tie-break's 7932 px (260 px headroom). Maxrects best-area-fit packs tighter
still (7601 px) but is more code (free-rect split + containment prune) for
headroom the port does not need yet; it stays the documented next step if a
future sheet wave eats the 260 px. A two-atlas split (option 4) was not
needed and would break the one-atlas/one-pipeline invariant.

**Name dedup** (option 3): the census found 41 duplicate decodes in the full
set вЂ” 48 `Projectile_*` names ride both `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` and the
`proj_data` loop (minus the ones whose file is absent). The `sheets`
HashMap keeps one rect per name, so the later copy's pixels were dead weight.
`build_ref` now keeps the FIRST occurrence of each name вЂ” UV-neutral for
every lookup (they already resolved to one rect), and it removes the dead
pixels. No sheet a draw references was removed.

**Implementation.** `crates/tr-render/src/atlas.rs`: `skyline_pack`
(the pure packer over PAD-inflated rects in a `max_width - PAD` bin) +
`build_ref`'s dedup/sort/skyline pass. The PAD geometry is unchanged:
every sheet keeps the 2 px border and в‰Ґ 2 px separation (the rects are
inflated by PAD before packing and offset by PAD after). `build` delegates
to `build_ref` exactly as before, so the owned and borrowed paths stay
bit-identical. `font_atlas.rs`'s independent shelf packer is untouched.

**Tests (WRITTEN, NOT RUN вЂ” code-only mode, no compiler invoked).**
`tr-render/src/atlas.rs`: `skyline_layout_is_deterministic_across_runs`
(two runs, identical pixels + rects), `skyline_copies_every_sheet_to_its_rect`
(UV correctness: every sheet's pixels at its rect, rect in-bounds with the
PAD border), `skyline_sheets_never_overlap_including_padding` (pairwise
on the inflated rects), `skyline_backfills_the_tall_sheets_tail`
(hand-computed 3-sheet witness, height 84 vs the shelf pass's 96),
`duplicate_names_pack_once_first_wins`, `skyline_fits_the_gore_shaped_stress_set`
(1400 small sheets + a tall band under 8192). The pre-existing
`build_ref_matches_build_bit_for_bit` still pins the owned/borrowed
contract. `tr-app/src/assets.rs`:
`the_full_gore_and_mount_sheet_set_fits_the_strict_gpu_bound` decodes the
real content, appends the simulated E-4b gore enumeration (910/911 excluded)
and the L-8b additions, and asserts height в‰¤ 8192 + every sampled gore sheet
addressable.

**Consequence for the goldens.** Like the E-4b branch's own packer change,
the skyline moves every sheet's atlas position: all UVs shift, so the golden
screenshot SHA256s change by construction and must be re-taken when a build
is next allowed (no pixel-behaviour change вЂ” the same texels, new addresses).
The E-4b and L-8b branches can now un-skip: their sheet sets fit.

## The vines keep their background walls (fix/vines-destroy-walls)

**User report.** Spawned vines destroy background-wall tiles: in mini-caves
with a destructible `dirt_wall`, the wall disappears and a vine stands in
its place.

**Root cause вЂ” the worldgen Vines pass, not the growth tick or the draw.**
`worldgen/biome_detail.rs::pass_vines` planted each vine segment by
REPLACING the whole `Tile` struct:

```rust
world.tiles[i] = Tile { kind: vine, frame_x: 0, ..Default::default() };
world.tiles[i].flags |= FLAG_ACTIVE;
```

`Tile::default()` zeroes `wall`, `wall_frame`, `liquid`, `meta` (paint) вЂ”
so every generated vine erased the cell's background wall. The C# Vines
pass writes fields only (`WorldGen.cs:20210-20216` for the 52 arm,
`:20246-20251` for the jungle 62 arm, `:20390-20395` for the corrupt 636
arm): `active(true)`, `type = <vine>`, `ClearSlope()` вЂ” `tile.wall` and
`wallFrame` are never touched. Jungle-grass overhangs above mini-cave
pockets carrying the natural dirt wall grew vines straight through the
wall field, which is exactly the reported symptom.

The two other suspects were re-verified faithful and left unchanged:

- The runtime growth arm (`growth.rs::grow_vine_arm`,
  `WorldGen.cs:73311-73341` + the four sibling families `:73343-73499`)
  writes `kind`/`flags`/`liquid` only; `wall` is a separate `Tile` field
  (`tile.rs:19`) it never touches. (Its `SquareTileFrame` /
  `CopyPaintAndCoating` calls remain the documented M7-GROWTH omissions.)
- The draw layer: walls draw in their own pass BEFORE tiles
  (`render/tiles.rs`, `Main.DrawWalls` shape), gated only by
  `wall_visible` + `tile_hides_wall` вЂ” the frame-opacity proxy for
  `WallDrawing.FullTile` (`WallDrawing.cs:91`, `:241-442`), which returns
  false for every non-solid kind. Vine frames are transparent, so the
  wall draws under vine cells; the deferred `DrawVines` strip pass
  (`render/vines.rs`, S1-G-1) draws only vine sprites and never touches
  the wall layer.

**Fix.** `pass_vines` now writes the C#'s fields in place: `FLAG_ACTIVE`,
`kind = vine`, `set_slope(0)` + clear `FLAG_HALF_BRICK`
(`Tile.ClearSlope`, `Tile.cs:130-134`), `frame_x = 0` (the port's existing
framing convention for vine segments). Wall, wall frame, liquid and paint
survive. The RNG draw order is unchanged вЂ” the write itself draws nothing
вЂ” so `generation_is_reproducible_for_a_seed` (a == b) stays green; the two
pinned world-hash VALUES (`world_hash.rs` `SEED42_512` / `DEFAULT_WORLD`)
are stale by design (vine cells now carry their walls) and must be
re-measured at the merge gate.

**Tests-as-code (written, not run вЂ” code-only mode, no compiler invoked).**

- `biome_detail::tests::vines_grow_without_erasing_the_background_wall` вЂ”
  a jungle-grass overhang above a dirt-walled pocket: every grown vine
  cell keeps wall 2, its (5,2) autotile frame, the paint and the liquid;
  `ClearSlope` ran.
- `biome_detail::tests::forest_vines_keep_the_wall_and_clear_the_slope` вЂ”
  the 52 arm keeps the wall and wipes a leftover slope + half-brick.
- `growth::tests::the_vine_arm_preserves_the_wall_and_wall_frame` вЂ” the
  runtime arm over 599 seeds: grown vines keep wall + wall_frame.
- `render::tiles::tests::walls_draw_under_vine_cells` вЂ” the wall-pass gate
  (`tile_hides_wall`) does not cull a vine cell's wall; an opaque dirt
  block does (the `FullTile` control), slopes/half-bricks never do.

**Out of scope (pre-existing, unchanged).** The compact `pass_vines`
model itself (per-family length caps 12/20 vs the C#'s `Next(1,10)`
counter runs, the missing 382/636/205/638 arms and the leaf-192 arm) is
the documented M1.4-WGEN-3 approximation; this fix changes only the cell
write, not the pass shape or its stream.
