  `num`, `+num` at the DOUBLE `lifeMax/1.25` and `/1.5`, then the INTEGER
  `/2`/`/3`/`/4`/`/5`/`/6` вЂ” `free_head_barrage_step` splits them correctly
  (f32 divisions for the first two, raw `i32` divisions for the last five);
  the World carries the raw `golem_hp`/`golem_max_hp` ints
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs:2861-2862`/`:3794-3795`), so the integer tiers are
  reproducible (a ratio could not). flag54 (the BODY's blocked line,
  `:31497-31501`, via `world.golem_x/y` = the body's centre) adds `num*10`.
- *The restored RNG triggers*: `ai[2] > 100 + Main.rand.Next(4800)`
  (`:31506`) вЂ” ONE draw per tick, every tick, strict `>`; the blocked-line
  lead `NextFloat()` X THEN Y, two draws PER BEAM, only while flag54
  (`:31555-31556`) вЂ” `free_head_blocked_lead` keeps the order; the tier
  escalation `(int)(dmg*1.5)` / `speed*2.5` (`:31553-31554`).
- *The beams* (`:31509-31569`): two at `+-14` from `cy - 50`, base 24 dmg /
  11 speed, +1/+0.25 at each BODY 50/40/30/20/10 % tier (`:31521-31548`),
  the normalized aim, the 3-tick spawn lead (`:31563-31564`), the
  `timeLeft = 300` override in the shot drain (`world_sim/npcs.rs:3897-3900`,
  `:31568`).
- *The shield*: `dontTakeDamage = true` from `SetDefaults` (`:12219`) never
  clears вЂ” the sim's spawn writes it (`world_sim/npcs.rs:3434`); the
  `golemBoss < 0` orphan guard (`:31372-31376`) rides `!world.golem_present`
  -> `hp = 0` (the family's documented direct-write stand-in for
  `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999, 0f, 0)` вЂ” the C#'s `owner == 255` +
  `Damage >= 9999` bypass flag `:81237` pierces the shield, so the kill
  itself is behaviourally right; the death-chain gore/sound fold with it).
- *The `TargetClosest` calls* (`:31377`, `:31451`) fold into the port's
  single-player target seam (the family-wide documented fold).

**Gaps found (for the follow-up вЂ” NOT fixed this round, the golem module is
the sibling's).**

- **G1 вЂ” the `noTileCollide` phase machine is UNPORTED** (`:31363-31371`).
  The C# free head defaults `noTileCollide = false` (case 249 sets no such
  line) and PHASES it per tick: its own blocked line sets it true (with
  flag53), and `noTileCollide && Collision.SolidTiles(position, w, h)`
  re-collides it. The port's arm integrates RAW every tick
  (`npc.rs:14556-14557`, `x += vx; y += vy`) вЂ” the head flies through temple
  walls even on clear-line ticks where the C# collides. `local_ai[0]` is
  taken by the mouth flag; the discarded TR-D3s48 partial had added a
  dedicated `Npc::no_tile_collide` field for exactly this. The fix needs the
  field (or a free local slot) + the two-probe phase + the seam's
  `player::collides_rect` pass gated on it. Behavioural, the largest gap.
- **G2 вЂ” the f32-vs-DOUBLE tier boundaries + the accumulation order** (the
  f1701eb0 catalogue class). The C# casts `(double)life < (double)lifeMax *
  0.8` etc. (`:31420`/`:31424`/`:31428`/`:31432`, `:31469`/`:31473`,
  `:31524-31544`); `free_head_fireball_step`/`free_head_beam_tier` compare in
  f32 (`npc_ai_golem.rs:279-291`/`:343-349`). At non-exact products the
  boundary flips: e.g. lifeMax 21000 at the 30 % beam tier вЂ”
  `21000.0f32 * 0.3f32` rounds ABOVE 6300.0, so `life == 6300` takes the tier
  in the port but not in the C# (`6300 < 6300.0` is false in double). The
  sibling's OWN attached-head core uses f64 for the same class
  (`head_fireball_step`, `npc_ai_golem.rs:367-371`) вЂ” the free-head cores
  should match. Second residual: the C# adds each tier to `ai[1]`/`ai[2]`
  SEQUENTIALLY (five/eight rounded f32 adds, `:31419-31434`/`:31468-31504`);
  the port pre-sums the ladder in f32 and does ONE `+=` (`npc.rs:14489`/
  `:14522`) вЂ” a different rounding path that can drift the 300-cadence /
  the trigger crossing by a tick over long fights. Both are ulp-class;
  fix = f64 compares + per-tier sequential adds (or a stream-witnessed
  proof of equivalence, which does not hold in general).
- **G3 вЂ” the facing write is a stand-in**: the port writes
  `facing`/`sprite_dir` from the velocity sign (`npc.rs:14554-14555`); the
  C# arm writes NO direction вЂ” it rides `TargetClosest`'s
  `SetTargetTrackingValues` target-face (`:77744-77755`). Diverges while the
  head drifts away from the player; folds with the family's TargetClosest
  seam but was not cited there.
- **G4 вЂ” the dust tail's stream offset, quantified**: the skipped 228-dust
  tail (`:31572-31585`, the standing cosmetic-skip) draws **SEVEN**
  `Main.rand` values EVERY tick while the head lives вЂ” `Next(2)` `:31575`,
  `NextFloatDirection()` + `NextFloat()` `:31576`, `NextFloatDirection()` +
  `NextFloat()` + `NextFloat()` `:31579`, `NextFloat()` `:31581`. Unlike the
  event-gated dust skips elsewhere in the family, this is a CONSTANT 7-draw
  per-tick offset on the shared `UpdateNpcs` stream вЂ” every downstream
  vanilla-synced roll drifts while the free head is alive. The gameplay
  draws (the trigger + the leads) are restored in the C#'s order, so the
  port's own stream is self-consistent; the offset matters only for
  vanilla-stream parity (the standing deviation, now counted).
- **G5 вЂ” FindFrame reads the POST-pin cadence**: the C# case 249
  (`:72963-72976`) reads `localAI[0] == 1` вЂ” the PRE-pin mouth flag; the port
  RECOMPUTES `ai[1] < 20 || > 280` (`npc.rs:6296`) AFTER the flag53 pin
  `ai[1] = 20`. On a blocked-line tick whose pre-pin `ai[1]` was in the
  window (e.g. 285 -> flag53 pins 20), the C# shows the mouth OPEN (the
  stored flag 1) and the port shows it CLOSED (20 fails both tests). Fix =
  read `local_ai[0]` (the arm already stores it). The dropped
  `frameCounter` 16-wrap (`:72972-72975`) is cited dead (no reader for this
  type) вЂ” accepted.

**Verdict.** Style 48 is COVERED by the landed golem-audit arm вЂ” the census
finds no missing kind and no competing port needed. The cores are faithful
in structure, constants, tier SPLIT (DOUBLE vs INTEGER) and RNG order; the
five gaps above (G1 behavioural, G2 ulp-class x2, G3/G5 small, G4 the
quantified standing skip) are the follow-up's scope. The three-way reconcile
is already recorded (ANALYSIS "The Golem family (S1-D-3)" вЂ” axis 47
delegates, style46/47 stay unwired references); the discarded TR-D3s48
partial adds nothing the landed arm lacks except the G1 field sketch.
Docs-only round — **no compiler invoked**.

  skip, the stream divergence starts only at a tick where the original
  NPC is already gone).

### Deviations (deliberate, recorded)

- The pool-pass placement: the C# interleaves the 52/53 arms in the
  200-slot order INSIDE `UpdateNPC`; the port runs them after the
  per-NPC step (the worm precedent) — freshly spawned minions take
  their first AI tick one frame late, and the hook/tentacle draws land
  after the other kinds' draws of the same tick instead of in slot
  order. The per-machine draw ORDER is unchanged.
- The hook's orphan strike lands as `hp = 0` directly (the port's
  convention) instead of routing `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999, 0, 0)`
  through the damage path — the C#'s `flag` instant-kill
  (`NPC.cs:81237`) skips the damage tracker anyway; the death-sound +
  bestiary-credit passes own the rest.
- `Main.mouseTextColor` (the FungiSpore light's pulse term) has no
  port field — the light helper takes it as a parameter (255 steady)
  for the light-pass wave.
- The tentacle's `reflects_projectiles` effect has no `Npc` field —
  `None` on every classic tick (the wiring may add the field with the
  ftw wave).
- The bestiary portraits rest the `SetDefaults` boxes (the
  pumpkin/frost precedent — the four `UI/Bestiary/NPCs/NPC_26x` sheets
  are not packed).

- The far/near normalize is f64 `Math.Sqrt` over an INT sum, cast to f32
  BEFORE the divide (`:34052`/`:34062`); NO zero guard — the C# NaN/Inf
  passes through into `ai[0]`/`ai[1]`. Kept.
- `Entity.DirectionFrom` (`Entity.cs:210-213`) is XNA `Normalize(Center
  - Source)` — a zero vector yields NaN, carried by the f32 threat sum

  zeroes at the 8-cap. Kept.
- `Hitbox.Distance(Center)` is `Utils.cs:1507-1542`'s rect-to-point
  distance over the INT-truncated Hitbox (`Entity.cs:171-183`): the

  bands, the corner `Vector2.Distance`. The threat scan reads ONLY

  cleared after generation (`WorldGen.cs:15714`, the
  `collision.rs::solid_kind` precedent). Platforms (`tileSolidTop`) do

## The snail wall-crawler family (aiStyle-67)

S1-D-3 (aiStyle-67), code-only mode, 2026-11-19.
`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style67.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s
`else if (this.aiStyle == 67)` inline arm (`NPC.cs:34348-34622`; the family
has NO `AI_067_*` method) as pure functions over a single `Npc`.
**NPC aiStyle 67 is NOT projectile aiStyle 67** (the pirate shots,
`AI_067_FreakingPirates`, siblings S1-D-4b7/12) — a different dispatch in
`Projectile.cs`, untouched here.

**Census.** The only three `this.aiStyle = 67;` rows in `SetDefaults`:
Snail 359 (`NPC.cs:13573-13586`, `NPCID.cs:11395`, 12×12, dmg 0 / def 0 /
lifeMax 5, npcSlots 0.5, noGravity, catchItem 2006), GlowingSnail 360
(`:13587-13600`, `NPCID.cs:11397`, 14×14, catchItem 2007) and MagmaSnail 655
(`:17280-17294`, `NPCID.cs:11987`, 14×14 + lavaImmune, catchItem 4849).
None has an `NpcKind` — the module is UNWIRED (`#![allow(dead_code)]`); the
machine is type-parameterised (`SnailCtx::npc_type`) and activates
unchanged when the kinds land.

**Fidelity notes (the quirks kept 1:1).**
- The shimmer probe's clamp upper is `Main.maxTilesX`/`maxTilesY`
  INCLUSIVE (`:34352-34353`) — an edge index reads a null tile and skips;
  the port's `World::tile` returns `None` out of bounds. The cast is
  `(int)(Center.X / 16f)` (AFTER the divide) here, but
  `(int)Center.X / 16` (BEFORE) for the lights (`:34387`/`:34391`) — both
  orders preserved.
- The 359 resize reads the OLD box once before either axis resizes
  (`:34368-34377`), uses the INTEGER `width / 2` half and the `-2f` X
  quirk; Y uses the FULL old height. `size_override` carries
  `base.width/height`. The scale roll runs AFTER the resize block, so the
  roll tick never resizes (the witness pins it).
- `GetShimmered` (`NPC.cs:91548-91565`): the statue arm despawns
  (`SpawnedFromStatue`), else all three types `Transform(677 Shimmerfly)`
  (`NPCID.cs:10470`'s `359,677`/`360,677`/`655,677` rows, `NPCID.cs:12031`).
  The 677 kind is unported, so both arms ride `SnailEvents` intents; the
  early return writes no `noGravity` (`None`). The `liquid > 30` gate is
  strict (30 does not shimmer).
- The fall roll `Next(7200)` rides the RIGHT `&&` operand (`:34411`):
  drawn only while `ai[2] == 0`, a gate-FAIL draw is still consumed.
- The fall block's ground probe is
  `(int)(Center.X + width/2 * -direction) / 16` — integer half-width,
  cast AFTER the add (`:34446-34453`); a non-topSlope tile + collideY
  decrements the timer, a bottomSlope ahead flips direction.
- The flag70 wall latch (`:34458-34464`) skips the whole rotation ease;
  the stuck detector (`:34465-34482`) forces direction +1 after 11 ticks
  at the same X (`localAI[2] > 10`).
- The rotation ease captures the target, restores the current rotation
  (`:34577-34578`), wraps at the strict `> 6.28` / `< 0` with the
  `(double)` compare kept as an f64 promotion, then runs TWO separate
  `if`s (not else-if) with the `> 3.14` long-way branch and the
  clamp-to-target.
- `Collision_MoveSnailOnSlopes` (`:92704-92721`, dispatched at
  `:92568-92571` in place of the normal slope pass) keeps the vanilla
  `direction *= -direction` quirk (`:92711`) — for ±1 that is always −1.
  The C#'s `NPC.gravity` argument to `Collision.SlopeCollision` is UNUSED
  in the body (`Collision.cs:1791-2031`; only `WalkDownSlope` reads it,
  `:1688`), so the port's gravity-free `slope_collision` signature is
  faithful.
- `snail_find_frame` is the pure twin
  `(vx, vy, frame, counter) -> (frame, counter)` (the
  `npc_ai_style49.rs::nimbus_find_frame` convention —
  `Npc::frame_counter` is private to `npc.rs`); the wiring drives both
  fields from `find_frame`. Fall rows 4/5 at the 6-tick phase (reset at
  `6*2-1 = 11`), walk rows 0/1/2/3/2/1 at the 10-tick phases (reset at
  `10*6-1 = 59`), zero velocity freezes both (`:72258-72261`).

**RNG by construction.** Exactly TWO `Main.rand` sites in the arm, in
source order, both on the caller's `UnifiedRandom` (the exact `Main.rand`
stream):
1. `Next(80, 111)` (`:34381`) — type 359 ONLY, once, when `ai[3] == 0`
   AND `netMode != 1`; zero draws once `ai[3]` is set (the resize never
   re-rolls).
2. `Next(7200)` (`:34411`) — when `ai[2] == 0` AND `netMode != 1`,

Nothing else draws: the lights, speed split, tile probes, state machine,
rotation ease and velocity tail are RNG-free; `TargetClosest`
(`NPC.cs:77652-77781`) and `SlopeCollision` (`Collision.cs:1791-2031`)
were re-read — no `Main.rand` in either body. The witness tests replay
the stream draw-for-draw against a clone (`assert_eq!(rng, witness)`);
the client path (`netMode == 1`) draws nothing at all.

**Seams.** `SnailEvents::no_gravity` (the arm's `noGravity` writes, last
write wins — `Npc` carries no gravity flag), `SnailEvents::light`
(`(tile_x, tile_y, [r,g,b])` for the `EntityLights` feed,
`npc_lights.rs`'s vocabulary), `shimmer_statue_despawn` /

### The RNG argument

Every gameplay draw rides the C#'s named stream at the site's own
position in the update order:

- The player-tick queues (hurt/death/jump/Fart/splash/drown/flap) drain
  at the `update_player` pass tail on `UpdatePlayers` — `Player.Update`
  runs under the `Main.cs:17754` swap, and `GrabItems` (`:27428`) runs
  INSIDE it, so the world-pickup chime's C# stream is `UpdatePlayers`
  even though the port's pickup lives in the items pass (the drain
  point differs, the named stream is the source's — the E21h
  queue→drain precedent).
- The revenge ping draws on `UpdateItems` (`WorldItem.UpdateItem` under
  the `Main.cs:17779` swap), right after the share draws in the same
  arm — the draw ORDER inside the arm is the source's.
- The chest transfers run from the click handlers OUTSIDE every swap —
  the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in (`rngs.global()`, the wave-C net-strike
  precedent), snapshotted across the field borrows.
- The grapple fire runs in the player pass before `Player.Update` —
  `UpdatePlayers`, after the gate.
- The attenuation gate precedes EVERY gameplay draw
  (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436` before the switch); a muted or
  out-of-range play consumes nothing. The style façade's GetRandomPitch
  NextFloat rides the audio-only `sound_style_random` (never a gameplay
  stream). The int overload (`SoundEngine.cs:102-108`) draws NO
  GetRandomPitch — the wave's int-id plays consume only their case
  draws.

### Deviations

1. **The wing-flap frame machine is the default arm's stand-in.** The
   hover wings' (22/28/30/...) own frame tables (`:29552-30445`) and the
   wings-43/48/49 constants are visual seams — their flap arms read
   frames 4/5 the default machine never produces, so they stay silent
   (the exclusion list already silences most). The wings-29 dust arm's
   `Next(5)`/`Next(10)` draws (`:30504-30517`) are NOT consumed — they
   are dust-visual rolls inside the unported table; when the visual

### The worm sim-pass RNG + placement (W-A2-1, code-only mode)

Audit `docs/research/55-audit-worms.md` (branch `origin/docs/audit-worms`)
finding W-A2-1 — the shared `AI_006_Worms` mechanics in
`world_sim/npcs.rs` (`update_worms_in` + `worm_head_step`), fixed in
place on `fix/worm-rng-placement`. The C# was re-read whole at every
cited window before each edit.

**The fixes (per audit finding):**

- **T1c budget draws (`NPC.cs:51303-51342`).** Every head in the
  `:51303` list rolls `ai[2] = Next(8, 13)` FIRST (`:51310`); type 10
  (GiantWorm) rolls again `Next(4, 7)` (`:51313`), type 117 (Leech)
  again `Next(3, 6)` (`:51341`), type 13 (EoW) overrides with
  `GetEaterOfWorldsSegmentsCount()` (`:51317`) but the first draw was
  still consumed. The pre-fix port drew once per family — a stream
  shift for every later `UpdateNpcs` consumer on every worm spawn.
  Now: draw-then-override, the discarded result kept advancing the
  stream. The Destroyer (`AI_037`'s own roll) and the crawltipede
  (the fixed 30-link spawn, `:51369-51392`) are OUTSIDE the list and
  draw nothing — their spawn routing stays byte-identical (R55 boundary).
- **T1g flag3 scan (`NPC.cs:51525-51597`).** The margins are
  `(int)(x/16)-1 .. (int)((x+w)/16)+2` exclusive-high, clamped; a tile
  counts when `nactive && (tileSolid || (tileSolidTop && frameY==0))`
  OR `liquid > 64` (liquid on INACTIVE tiles too), and only when its
  16-px box actually overlaps the NPC rect (`:51586`). Each
  overlapping tile draws `Main.rand.Next(100)` (`:51590`) — the draw
  sits BEFORE the `type != 117 && nactive && tileSolid` guards in the
  C# `&&` chain, so Leech heads and liquid-only tiles consume it too;
  on 0 the effect-only `KillTile(fail:true, effectOnly:true)` fires
  (dust only — the dust effect rides the unwired dust seam, the DRAW
  cannot be skipped). The pre-fix scan had no margins, no overlap
  test, no solidTop arm, liquid gated on active, and no draw at all —
  a per-digging-tick stream divergence. The always-fly presets
  (`:51548-51567`) skip the scan entirely (`!flag3 | flag2` is false);
  of the ported kinds only the crawltipede 412-414 (`:51560-51563`) —
  ported so its stream stays draw-free.
- **T1a head rotation (`NPC.cs:52201`).** `rotation = Atan2(vy, vx) +
  Math.PI/2` at the tail of the no-leader `else` — every head, every
  tick. The pre-fix `worm_head_step` never wrote rotation (heads drew
  frame-up while digging sideways). The heads use PI/2
  (`FRAC_PI_2`), the followers keep the `1.57f` literal (`:51878`) —
  the two constants stay distinct.
- **T2b child placement (`NPC.cs:51347` + `NewNPC:80770` +
  `Entity.cs:128-131`).** `NewNPC` sets `Bottom = (X, Y)`:
  `child.pos = (X - width/2, Y - height)` with
  `X = (int)(pos.X + (float)(width/2))` — the width is an INT, so
  `width/2` is integer division — and `Y = (int)(pos.Y + height)`.
  The child's BOTTOM sits at the parent's bottom; the pre-fix port
  put the child's TOP there, one child-height low per link, and did
  not int-truncate. Fixed.
- **T2c pass order.** C# runs `AI_006` inside each NPC's `Update` in
  slot order; `NewNPC`'s `Start = whoAmI` gives every child a higher
  slot, so the head moves first and each follower snaps to the
  leader's SAME-TICK centre. The pre-fix pass ran followers before
  heads — a one-tick lag along the chain. Now heads first, then the
  follower trail in ascending slot order (= ascending `seg_index`).
- **T1d surface gate (`NPC.cs:51110-51148`).** `flag = true` for
  types 10/39/95/117/510 (ported: GiantWorm, Leech); target dead OR
  (flag && player above `worldSurface*16`) → `EncourageDespawn(300)`
  (the existing `despawn_timer` seam) + `velocity.Y += 0.2` while
  gated. The dead-target arm runs for every segment (family-wide).
  The `TargetClosest()` retarget has no single-player seam (the
  target IS the one player) — documented. The 513/510/621 rows ride
  their kind waves.
- **T1e corruption escape (`NPC.cs:52004-52050`).** INSIDE the dig
  branch after the aim scale: Devourer/EoW whose target is outside
  Corrupt/Crimson or dead → flag6; no living player in ZoneCorrupt
  (flag7 — Corrupt only, NOT Crimson) → below
  `(rockLayer + maxTilesY)/2` the head deactivates and walks the
  `ai[0]` chain dead (the port kills the head + every DOWNSTREAM
  `seg_index` of its `worm_id` — an EoW split fragment ahead keeps
  its own life, as the C# walk never reaches it), and the aim
  overrides to straight down (`num48 = 0, num49 = num45`).
- **T1f 1000-px override (`NPC.cs:51598-51615`).** A listed head
  (ported: Devourer/GiantWorm/EoW/Leech) with no player inside the
  ±1000-px box around its rect forces flag3 (one rectangle test,
  strict inequalities, int-truncated positions).

**The RNG argument (stream-position parity).** `UnifiedRandom` is the
exact .NET subtractive stream (`next_range`/`next_max` = one
`Sample()` each). Per head kind, at chain start: Devourer 1 draw
(`Next(8,13)` kept), GiantWorm 2 (`Next(8,13)` discarded +
`Next(4,7)`), Leech 2 (discarded + `Next(3,6)`), EoW 1 (discarded,
constant 65), Destroyer 0, crawltipede 0. Per digging tick: one
`Next(100)` per overlapping candidate tile in X-outer/Y-inner scan
order, for every listed head including the Leech; the always-fly
crawltipede draws none. The witness tests replay each ledger on a
twin oracle stream and assert the NEXT raw draw after the pass is
equal — pre/post stream-position parity per head kind, plus the
two-tick crumble ledger. The tests are WRITTEN, NOT RUN (code-only
mode, no compiler invoked).

### Structure decisions

- The four aiStyle-1 kinds ride the slice-A/B module shape
  (`projectile_ai_frostmoon::step` + `finish_flight`, the verbatim
  `ai_style1_flight` tail replication) — the C# block order preserved:
  hook group → flag3 counter → below-counter hooks → the gravity else-if
  chain → the shared tail. 345 counts (not on the flag3 list) and pins at
  50 in its own arm; 348/349/350 rest (`:55985-55987`) so the generic
  `ai[0] >= 15` gravity never opens for them — they fly straight (the
  349's +0.2 is its own hook's, applied every tick).
- The aiStyle-14 pair are HEADS only: the dispatch runs `ornament` /
  `spike_pulse` and then the SAME generic `ai_spear` tail — no parallel
  flight copy. The 346 burst's five spawns ride back to the pool
  (`ShrapnelSpawn`, the nebula request shape) and drain through
  `spawn_with_data_ai_owned` with the ornament's owner, Damage 40 / KB 0
  (`:24894`), `ai1 = ornament.ai[1]` (the frame payload), the box centred
  (`NewProjectile` `:10876-10877` — the spawn site subtracts the 6x6
  half-box). The spawned shrapnel is flipped `friendly = false` (the
  `spawn_hostile` convention — the row's stock friendly is false, the
  pool's slot default true).
- The style-58 arm is inline in the module (`present`) and gated to 351
  in the dispatch — the style's only rowed kind, so no other kind's
  behaviour changes. The C#'s two consecutive `if`s (`:28913`/`:28926`)
  are kept: the tick that flips ai[0] to 1 runs BOTH blocks (frame 1, the
  second +0.1, the drag) in the same tick — the witness pins it.
- The 346 burst's `owner == Main.myPlayer` gate (`:24883`) folds to the
  pool's `simulated` gate: the port models hostile shots as owner 255
  (`spawn_hostile`) while the C# spawns with `Owner: Main.myPlayer`
  (`NPC.cs:32885`); the arm only runs on locally-simulated slots
  (`projectile.rs:12961-12965`), which IS the owner test in the
  single-player port (the saucer precedent).

### RNG by construction

- **Zero-draw arms**: 345 (`:57116-57128` — the latch is sound-only), 348
  (`:56246-56273` — sound-only latch), 349 (`:56221-56245`), 352
  (`:24848-24866`), 351 (`:28906-28937`) contain no `Main.rand` call at
  all. Their ports cannot drift any stream.
- **350's dust window** (`:55138-55157`): `Next(3)` (+ inner `Next(10)`),
  `Next(4)` (+ inner `Next(5)`) — every draw feeds `Main.dust` alone, no
  observable state. The window is SKIPPED whole with its draws (the
  aiStyle-1 pool's zero-RNG convention, the slice-A/B precedent — the
  same documented stream-position deviation those slices carry). No
  trajectory can change; the deviation is the convention, recorded here.
- **346's burst** (`:24885-24894`): the draws FEED observable state (the
  five shrapnel velocities) and are KEPT on the pass's threaded stream in
  the C#'s exact order — per fragment `Next(-20,21)` → `Next(-20,0)` →
  `Next(-30,31)` (SpeedX's jitter, named-argument evaluation order) →
  `Next(-30,31)` (SpeedY's). The Y draw's range tops at −1, so the
  `10/sqrt(dx²+dy²)` normalise never divides by zero. The recording-stream
  witness (`the_ornament_bursts_five_shrapnel_in_draw_order`) pins the
  20-draw sequence. The burst fires once per ornament (timeLeft == 1),
  so the stream cost is deterministic per spawn.
- The spawn-site draws (`NPC.cs:32838`'s `Next(0,31)` ai0 payload,
  `:32885`'s `Next(2)` frame pick, `:33607`'s `Next(5)`, the velocity
  jitters) belong to the NPC-side machines (the S1-F-13c frost-boss
  slices own them — `npc_ai_frost_boss.rs`/`_b.rs` already carry them);
  this round adds no spawn site, so no UpdateNPCs-stream position moves.

### RNG argument (zero draws by construction)

The module takes NO rng parameter. Every C# `Main.rand` draw in the ported
blocks is dust-only — its result feeds nothing but a dust count/velocity/
scale, never state: the 638 proximity burst `Next(15,31)` (`:55889`), the
640 dust gates `Next(extraUpdates)`/`Next(2|6)`/`Next(2)`/`NextDouble`/
`Next(10)` (`:55453-55470`) and the numUpdates==1 trail dust
(`:55473-55481`), the Kill() dust counts `Next(5,10)` (`:73433`) and
`Next(2,5)` (`:76123`). Skipping them with the dust layer therefore keeps
every state-bearing decision identical (the ai001_a/b dust-skip
convention). The ported arms draw nothing, so the pass's UpdateProjectiles
stream is untouched for every OTHER kind — byte-identical by construction.
The `damage_pve` decay is pure arithmetic (no variance draw added).

### The stream argument (why the drain is safe)

`Main.UpdateProjectiles` runs under the `Main.rand` swap
(`Main.cs:17775-17777`): every `PlaySound` inside the projectile walk —
the AI arms AND the `Kill()` tail — draws its case-2 pitch from the
`UpdateProjectiles` stream. The port queues each play as a
`(id, style, x, y, pitchOffset)` intent (`Projectile.wants_sound`, the
`wants_mark_spawn` pattern; the pool forwards it into
`pending_proj_sounds` right after the dispatch) and drains at the pass
tail in `world_sim/projectiles.rs` — AFTER the wave-C NPC-hit drain, on
the same named stream. `Audio::play_proj_sound` gates attenuation BEFORE
any draw (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436` precedes the case switch), the
E21e precedent; the `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat rides the audio-only
`sound_style_random`. The C# plays mid-walk; the port's batch drain moves
the draw to the pass tail — the same recorded deviation as wave C's
strike plays (relative order among the tick's sound draws is preserved;
the interleaving with gameplay draws is not). The witness tests pin the
contract: muted/out-of-range plays draw NOTHING, an audible play draws
exactly one `Next(-6, 7)` on `UpdateProjectiles`, every other stage
stream stays pristine.

### Deviations (deliberate, recorded)

- **The Light's Bane post-gate volume scale** (`:42237`,
  `Volume *= 0.15f * ai[0]` on the returned instance) is DEFERRED — the
  queue→drain batch plays at the style's own volume. The cue, position
  (Center) and −1 latch are ported.
- **The bomb cue fires at the detonation latch** (`timeLeft <= 3`), not
  inside `explode_bomb`: the position is the PRE-`PrepareBombToBlow`
  `base.position` the C# reads (`:78331` precedes the `Resize`), and the
  fuse-instance Stop (`:70675`) has no pool (the standing D4 deviation).
  Gated to the five kinds `explode_bomb` accepts.
- **The 301 Stacked Discs' −0.33-pitch whoosh arm** (`:38879`) has no
  ported row — deferred; the generic 8-tick arm covers the ported
  boomerangs. The Phaseblade family and 383 exclusions (`:38868`) name
  unported kinds — the port's gate is unconditional over its own rows.
- **The slice-A latch order**: the C# plays before the `ai[1]` latch on
  81/180/248 and after it on the rest; the queue payload is identical
  either way (the drain runs at the pass tail), so one helper keeps the

### B-6d-1 — the apocalypse slot table (FIXED)

`WorldGen.UpdateLunarApocalypse` (`WorldGen.cs:86693-86748`) sets one
flag per tower TYPE (517 solar / 422 vortex / 507 nebula / 493 stardust,
`:86708-86725`). The port's match had `NebulaTower => 2` AND
`NebulaTower => 3` — the second arm unreachable, slot 2 (vortex) never
set, so `tower_active_vortex` cleared on the first update after any
tower death and `:86744`'s all-four doom gate could fire with the Vortex
pillar standing. Fixed to `VortexTower => 2` / `NebulaTower => 3` — the
slot order keeps the flag writes (`lunar.rs:147-150`) consistent (the
audit's alternative "VortexTower => 3" would have crossed the
vortex/nebula flags). Witnesses: all four towers counted once each, the
vortex-only death never arms the doom, all-down arms it, a living core
(398) holds it.

### B-6d-2 — the 629 bolt's shield spend (FIXED, three counts)

C# `Projectile.Kill()`'s type-629 block (`Projectile.cs:72944-72979`,
read whole):
1. the spend is `Clamp(ShieldStrengthTower<Kind> - 1, 0,
   ShieldStrengthTowerMax)` (`:72953` etc.) — ONE per bolt, regardless
   of damage (the 629 spawns with damage 0, `NPC.cs:79290`); the port
   drained `slot.damage`;
2. the shield is picked by `Main.npc[(int)ai[0]].type` (`:72946`) —
   `ai[0]` is the HOST NPC INDEX, not a tower ordinal; the port matched
   `ai[0] as usize` 0/1/2/3 against the four shields, so with the
   compacted vec the spend hit an arbitrary shield;
3. the host's `ai[3] = 1f` shield-flash (`:72951` etc.) fires only while
   the shield is non-zero — the port never set it.
All three fixed in the aiStyle-122 dispatch arm; the switch's missing
default is kept (a non-tower host spends nothing); the clamp max rides
`tower_shield_max` (`NPC.cs:6795-6806`, halved post-Moon-Lord). The
`:72977-72978` netUpdate/SendData(101) tail stays unmodelled
(single-player). The spend is still only reachable once B-6b wires the
spawn sites — no live code spawns 629 yet (R72 owns that loop).

`Projectile.cs:33844-33856` (`AI_108`'s 579 arm at `ai[0] == 90`):

### B-6d-4 — the DD2 lane fade window (AUDIT FALSE POSITIVE, no change)

Audit 53 §4.1 defect 1 claimed `npc.rs:10769` ramps 500→550 while C#
ramps 500→600, and that the port's scale at death is 0.05 vs C#'s 0.525.
Re-verified against source — the claim miscomputes its own cite:
- C# `NPC.cs:41028`: `scale = Lerp(1, 0.05, GetLerpValue(500, 600,
  ai[0], clamped: true))`.
- `Utils.GetLerpValue` (`Utils.cs:315-343`) with clamped=true returns
  0 below 500, 1 above 600, else `(t - from) / (to - from)` =
  `(ai[0] - 500) / (600 - 500)` = `(ai[0] - 500) / 100`.
- The port: `let t = ((self.ai[0] - 500.0) / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  self.scale = 1.0 + (0.05 - 1.0) * t;` — algebraically IDENTICAL.
- At the death tick `ai[0] == 550` (`NPC.cs:41038`): t = 0.5, scale =
  1 − 0.95·0.5 = 0.525 in BOTH. The gate dies mid-fade in vanilla too;
  the 600 endpoint is never reached. The audit's "port finishes at 550"
  reading treated the `/100` divisor as a 100-tick window ending at the
  death tick — but the divisor is the C#'s own `to - from`.
No code change (the golden rule forbids "fixing" faithful code). A
witness test pins the window at 500 (scale 1), 525 (0.7625) and the 550
death (0.525, hp 0, unshielded) so no future pass narrows it.

(`DD2Event.cs:1075-1095`): the Dark Mage's `if` (`:1078-1081`) runs its
`NewNPC`, and the chain after it (`:1082-1093`) runs its OWN `NewNPC` —
`num4` is only the net-sync handle (`:1100-1103`), re-assigning it does
not un-spawn the mage. The port returned `chain.or(boss)` — one body,
the mage dropped whenever the chain fired. Fixed to
`LaneSpawn { first: boss, second: chain }`; the resolver
(`spawn_dd2_from_gate`) already iterates `[first, second]` in order, so
the mage spawns first, the chain body second — the C#'s statement order.
Witnesses: mage+wyvern, mage+javeliner, mage+goblin, the right-lane
`Next(2)` miss (chain alone), and the live-mage `AnyNPCs(564)` gate.

### B-6e — the DD2 wave-6 spawn drop (FIXED, branch fix/dd2-wave6-spawn-drop)

The new finding handed to the Lead by B-6d, resolved on
`fix/dd2-wave6-spawn-drop` (based on `fix/lunar-dd2-small-wrongs`
6e3d201e — the chain lands both). Code-only wave: no compiler invoked,
witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN; verification = whole-block C# re-reads +
hand-traced draw sequences.

C# `DD2Event.Difficulty_3_SpawnMonsterFromGate` case 6
(`DD2Event.cs:1691-1728`, read whole): TWO independent `if` chains.
The first (`:1692-1707`) rolls `Next(20)`/`Next(20)`/`Next(12)`/`Next(25)`
for the balista 577 / sapper 565 / mystic 571 / drake 569 and runs its
`NewNPC`. The second (`:1708-1727`) is a SEPARATE statement — its
`Next(7)` glider 578, `Next(7)`+`Next(3)` mystic/frost-mage, `Next(5)`
javeliner 563, or the squire arm: `Next(3)` spawns the 557 into `num8`
(`:1724`) and the 554 ALWAYS spawns into `num9` (`:1726`). `num8`/`num9`
are only net-sync handles (`:1755-1762`); re-assigning `num8` does not
un-spawn the first chain's body. Up to THREE bodies per pass.

The port returned `second.first.or(first)` — the first chain's body was
dropped whenever the second fired, and the squire's unconditional 554
rode the optional `second` slot. Fixed: `LaneSpawn` gains a `third`
field (only this arm fills it — the always-spawned 554), the wave-6 pick
is `{ first, second: second.first, third: second.third }`, and the
resolver (`spawn_dd2_from_gate`) iterates `[first, second, third]` in
the C#'s spawn order (first chain, then 557-on-roll, then 554). RNG is
unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION: every roll and its order is untouched — the
bug was purely the post-roll body selection.

## The pillar shield loop (B-6b, 2026-11-19, code-only mode)

Audit research/53 (`docs/audit-pillars-dd2lanes`, rows 1c/2b) found the
pillar shield STATE faithful but unwired: `tower_shield_absorb` /
`update_tower_shields` had test-only callers, the towers never read
`tower_shield_*`, and no live code spawned the 629 TowerDamageBolt —
pillars were killable by direct damage from tick 1 and no mob kill ever
chipped a shield. This round wires the loop
(`task/S1-D-3-pillar-shield-loop`).

**The C# machine (read whole).**

- **Spawn sites** — `NPC.cs:79279-79320`, inside `checkDead`'s
  pre-death type switch: solar mobs 412-419+518 spawn a 629 while
  `ShieldStrengthTowerSolar > 0` with `ai0 = FindFirstNPC(517)`;
  vortex 425/426/427/429 → host 422; nebula 420/421/423/424 → host 507;
  stardust 402/405/407/409/411 → host 493. Each call is
  `NewProjectile(source, Center.X, Center.Y, 0f, 0f, 629, 0, 0f,
  Main.myPlayer, FindFirstNPC(host))` — damage 0, velocity 0, knockback
  0. `FindFirstNPC` (`NPC.cs:89885-89895`) returns the first active
  slot of the type, **-1** on miss. NOT in the sets: 428
  (VortexHeadcrab), 406 (StardustCellSmall), 410 (StardustSpiderSmall).
  The `checkDead` carrier guard (`NPC.cs:78042`: `realLife >= 0 &&
  realLife != whoAmI`) skips linked segments — the crawltipede
  bodies/tails ride the carrier's death events.
- **The spend** — `Projectile.cs:72944-72979` (the 629's `Kill` arm,
  `netMode != 1`): switch on `Main.npc[(int)ai[0]].type` (the HOST
  NPC's type — `ai[0]` is an NPC index, not a tower ordinal); if the
  matching shield `!= 0` set the host's `ai[3] = 1` (the flash
  trigger), then `Shield = (int)MathHelper.Clamp(Shield - 1, 0,
  ShieldStrengthTowerMax)` — **−1 per bolt regardless of damage**.
- **The gate** — `NPC.cs:39101-39115` (aiStyle 94, every tick):
  `dontTakeDamage = ShieldStrengthTower<Kind> != 0` per type. While
  the shield stands the tower refuses every hit; the shield falls ONLY
  through 629 contacts. `downedTower*`/`TowerActive*` are written by
  the tower's DEATH (`NPC.cs:79321-79345`), never by shield
  exhaustion. The ai[3] flash cycle (`:39069-39100`: NPCDeath58 on
  the shield-state flip, NPCDeath3 at ai[3]==1, the 120-wrap) reads the
  trigger the spend writes.

**The wiring (Rust).**

| C# | Rust | position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NPC.cs:79279-79320` spawn cases | `world_sim/npcs.rs::spawn_tower_damage_bolts` | `update_npcs` death path, BEFORE the tower death arms (the C# switch's mob cases precede the pillar cases) |
| `NPC.cs:89885-89895` FindFirstNPC | the `app.npcs.iter().position(kind && hp>0)` scan, -1.0 on miss | inside the spawn loop; the port's compacted vec index is the sim's current whoAmI (the saucer-deathray seam precedent) |
| `NPC.cs:39101-39115` dontTakeDamage gate | `world_sim/npcs.rs::apply_tower_shield_gates` | `update_npcs` death-path tail (after the death arms, so cultist-spawned towers are gated the same tick) |
| `Projectile.cs:72953` etc. −1 spend | `world_sim/npcs.rs::tower_shield_absorb` (RESHAPED: −1 clamp 0..max, returns the pre-spend `!= 0`) | the fn seam; the live 629 arm call site is R71's |
| `NPC.cs:95247-95251` all-dead reset | `world_sim/npcs.rs::update_tower_shields` (was test-only) | `update_npcs` death-path tail |
| the hurt/strike/PVE refusals | pre-existing gates: `npc.rs` hurt's `dont_take_damage` check, the strike gate, `projectile.rs` PVE walk's `!nPC.dontTakeDamage` (`Projectile.cs:12583`) | unchanged — the gate pass now feeds them live |

The spawn rides `spawn_hostile_ai` (the `HostileShotAi` seam): kind
629, the mob's CENTRE (the port's seam carries centres; the C#
`NewProjectile` subtracts half the extent at `Projectile.cs:10876-
10877` and the port's `ai_tower_damage_bolt` reads `pos` as the
centre — the recorded arm deviation, research/53 §3.1), velocity 0,
damage 0, knockback 0, `ai0` = host index, `ai1` = 0. The row's
`SetDefaults` (`Projectile.cs:6754-6766`: 8×8, aiStyle 122, hostile,
timeLeft 3600, penetrate −1, extraUpdates 2) already rides
`projectile/data.rs`'s 629 row.

**The absorb reshape (audit §2.2's fix spec).** The old
`tower_shield_absorb(world, tower, dmg)` drained `dmg` per hit and
flipped `downed_tower_*`/`tower_active_*` at zero — both wrong
models. The new `tower_shield_absorb(world, tower) -> bool` chips −1
(clamped `0..tower_shield_max`) and returns whether the shield stood
(the C#'s `!= 0` gate on the ai[3] flash). The downed/active writes
are RETIRED from the fn — the death arms (`npcs.rs`'s
`NpcKind::SolarTower` etc.) already own them. The old test
(`the_absorb_drains_and_flags_the_down`) is repointed to the faithful
model (`the_absorb_chips_one_per_bolt_and_never_downs`).

**RNG argument (by construction).** The spawn loop draws NOTHING: the
C# cases contain no `Main.rand` call, and `NewProjectile` for type
629 draws nothing either — aiStyle 122 is not the aiStyle-1 velocity
damp (`Projectile.cs:10895-10902`), 629 is absent from the owner-rand
spawn arms (`:10907-10919`: 206/335/358/406), the golf-ball and
CD-copy sets (`ProjectileID.cs:191`), the timeLeft overrides and
`FinalizeProjectile`'s 93/113/gem arms (`:22043-22061`). The gate
pass and the reset are pure state writes. The all-streams census
witness (`the_spawn_loop_draws_nothing`) pins every named stream
byte-identical across a two-kill loop.

**Boundaries / deliberate folds.**

- **The 629 arm's spend call site** (`projectile.rs:13502-13521`:
  drains `slot.damage`, selects by `ai[0] as usize` ordinal, never
  sets ai[3]) is **R71** (`fix/lunar-dd2-small-wrongs`) — this branch
  wires the SPAWN loop only and hands R71 the reshaped spend fn; the
  merger reconciles (host-kind selection `Main.npc[ai[0]].type` +
  the ai[3]=1 write + the −1 call).
- **The pillar AI machine re-port is B-6a (queued)** — the stand-in
  `update_ancient_cultist`'s 180-tick self-kill (ai[2] misused as a
  timer; the C# ai[2] is the dissolve FLAG set by `checkDead`
  `:78080-78086`) STAYS until B-6a. Consequence documented: a pillar

  NPCDeath58/NPCDeath3 cues ride B-6a too (they read R71's ai[3]

- **Gate/reset position fold**: the C# runs the gate inside the pillar

  (once per NPC pass). Same-tick semantics for the shielded→bare

- **`lunar.rs:136`** (the duplicate NebulaTower slot arm) is R71's

- **R71 handoff resolutions** (LEAD-R71-HANDOFF, consumed): (1) the
  580 bolt's `ai1 = Next(80)` (`Projectile.cs:33841`) spawns from the
  578 ritual marker's OWN aiStyle-108 arm (`:33838-33842`,

**Verification.** Code-only: the C# blocks re-read whole (the spawn

## The small-kinds wiring wave (S1-D-3-wire-smallkinds, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

Four landed-UNWIRED NPC-AI modules from the entity-ai-census §2b worklist
are now WIRED: the Blazing Wheel (aiStyle 21, type 72), the Angry Nimbus
(aiStyle 49, type 250), the Dungeon Spirit (aiStyle 56, type 288) and the
Force Bubble (aiStyle 72, type 384). Each was a pure module with no
`NpcKind`, no dispatch arm, no anchors/PORT_MAP row on main. This wave
adds the four kinds + their `SetDefaults` rows + the dispatch claims +
the minimal Ctx seams, retiring the stand-in routing with `unreachable!`
markers (the aiStyle-5/9 precedent). The modules' own witness tests stay
as the audit cross-check; three new wiring tests per kind are WRITTEN,
NOT RUN — **no compiler invoked**.

**The kinds + protocol ids.** `NpcKind::{BlazingWheel, AngryNimbus,
DungeonSpirit, ForceBubble}` (`npc.rs`). The protocol ids (`to_u16` /
`from_u16`, `npc/data.rs`): AngryNimbus 250, DungeonSpirit 288,
ForceBubble 384 keep their vanilla ids (all free); BlazingWheel takes the
port-local **353** because the vanilla 72 slot is the MartianWalker's
(`to_u16`'s bijection guard). `cs_id()` returns the vanilla `NPC.type`
(72/250/288/384) for the AI arms' type gates. Every exhaustive `NpcKind`
match gained arms (scripted scan): `to_u16`, `ai_style`, `size`,
`max_hp`, `contact_damage`, `defense`, `value`, `render_key`,
`update_kind_ai`, `find_frame`, `debuff_immune_ids`, the netglue
`npc_seed`, the bestiary portrait table, the draw match. The `SetDefaults`
rows are verbatim (`NPC.cs:9714-9731` / `:12221-12233` / `:12738-12752` /
`:13882-13894`): the wheel's alpha 100 / behindTiles / dontTakeDamage /
scale 1.2 land in `Npc::new`; the bubble's kb 1 (the head default,
`:8533`) and dmg 0 (`:8563`) are explicit rows.

**The dispatch split (the Ctx seams).** `Npc::update_rng`'s aiStyle axis
(`npc.rs`) claims 21/49/56/72:
- **21 (BlazingWheel)** — the arm runs inline: `ai_style21` (the
  ricochet machine, RNG-free) + `collision_move_blazing_wheel` (the
  12×12 `noSlopeCollision` centre box + the dry-move latch). The
  `mouseTextColor`-pulsed centre light (`NPC.cs:24664`) is fed

  returned light triple from the AI call is discarded. `blazing_wheel_frame`

- **49 (AngryNimbus)** — `nimbus_step` (the AI + the dry no-slope move

- **56 (DungeonSpirit)** — the arm needs the shared `Main.dust` pool +
  its `SpawnCtx` (App fields the `&mut self` update cannot carry), so
  `style56_step` runs in the world-sim tick closure
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) at the spirit's slot turn, filling a
  `Style56Env` from `app.dust` / `app.spawn_ctx()` / the `UpdateNPCs`

  `NPC.cs:32755`) ride the pool in slot order. The axis' 56 arm owns

  (`NPC.cs:90494-90498`, the dead-band X snap + the stamps).
- **72 (ForceBubble)** — the arm reads the SIBLING NPC slots
  (`Main.npc[(int)ai[0]]`), so `ai_style72` runs in a world-sim host

**The officer's bubble lifecycle (aiStyle 3, NOT the bubble's arm).**
The Martian Officer's spawn/shield block (`AI_003_Fighters`,
`NPC.cs:56222-56251`) is wired through `Npc::martian_officer_bubble`
(called after the officer's walker step in `update_kind_ai`): the spawn

**Order deviation (documented).** The C# runs the bubble's aiStyle-72
arm at the bubble's own slot turn; the port runs it in a pre-pass at

immutably before the per-NPC `&mut` loop). The snap therefore reads the
officer's PREVIOUS-tick centre when the officer's slot is later — the

Scutlix) already carries. The arm is RNG-free, so the placement does not

own sheets (`NPC_72` 34×144, `NPC_250` 48×168, `NPC_288` 28×102,
`NPC_384` 48×52 — decoded via the prebuilt `tr-content` `dims` example,

## The saucer wiring (S1-D-3-wire-saucer, code-only)

`task/S1-D-3-wire-saucer` wires R34's faithful `npc_ai_style75.rs` module
into the live sim, closing the **P0 event-progression blocker** the R58b
audit flagged as M3: the live `update_saucer_mount` had NO phase bridge,
so killing the Martian saucer crew (392 shell / 393 turrets / 394 cannons)
NEVER opened the core 395 and the invasion fight could not progress. The
old witness `the_dead_crew_opening_the_core_kills_it` asserted
`core.is_some() || invasion_type == 0` — a tautology that admitted the gap.

**Base.** The work is based on R34's module branch
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle75` (tip `ac1f45a2`), merged onto `origin/main`
(`c7fe175d`) in the `TR-wire16` worktree — the chain lands both the module
and the wiring. CODE-ONLY MODE: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; the
new witnesses are written, not run.

**What the wiring does.**
- **Axis claim.** `npc.rs::update_rng`'s aiStyle axis gains
  `75 => self.update_rng_style75_solo(...)`; the six kinds' kind-match arms
  (`ScutlixRider`, `MartianSaucer`/`Turret`/`Cannon`, `FlyingDutchmanCannon`,
  `SolarDrakomireRider`) become `unreachable!` markers and the three
  stand-in functions are deleted. The duplicate dead saucer arm
  (`npc.rs:4036-4038` in the audit) is marked unreachable too.
- **Pooled sim path.** The family machine is a POOL step (the host/crew
  slot links read `App::npcs` live), so `world_sim/npcs.rs`'s tick closure
  runs `style75_step(npcs, i, ...)` in slot order on the `UpdateNPCs`
  stream for every aiStyle-75 NPC — ahead of the solo `update_rng` axis
  (which only sees a one-slot pool). The shared `NPC.Update` preamble is
  extracted to `Npc::update_preamble`; the pooled arm runs
  preamble → `style75_step` → `find_frame` → `contact`, matching
  `update_rng`. The solo wrapper (`update_rng_style75_solo`) keeps bare
  `update_rng` test callers faithful over a one-slot pool.
- **Slot-aligned links.** `carrier_link_pre_pass` (+ its linear A/B twin)
  now writes the slot-aligned `ai[0]` host link (the module's
  `npcs[ai[0]]` read) and the 392 shell's `local_ai[0..3]` crew slots (the
  C#'s `localAI` links, `NPC.cs:36095-36102`), adds the 416 DrakomireRider,
  and NO LONGER kills orphaned mounts — the module owns the orphan-death
  (`:36064-36069`) and the riders' `Transform(382/518)` fallbacks
  (`:36056-36063`). A hostless mount gets `ai[0] = -1`.
- **Seam drains.** `Style75Out.shots` → `wants_hostile_shot` /
  `wants_hostile_shot_ai` (the sim's shot drain resolves them);
  `spawn_carrier` → `wants_mount_carrier` (a resolve pass spawns the 391/415
  Bottom-placed, `NPC.cs:80770`, `timeLeft = 750`); `transform` →
  `wants_transform` (a resolve pass runs `Npc::transform_to_kind`, the
  `NPC.Transform` maths `:81084-81114`); `sounds` → `Audio::play_use_sound`
  drained at the C# call position on the `UpdateNPCs` stream (the case-2
  `Next(-6,7)` pitch draw, `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:632`); `died` → hp already
  0, the death pass owns HitEffect + deactivation. Dust spawns through the
  REAL `DustPool::new_dust` on `app.dust` with `app.spawn_ctx()`.

**M1–M4 resolution (the audit's mount defects).**
- **M1 (seats unrotated/unscaled)** — RESOLVED by activation: the module's
  ride offsets do `offset *= core.scale` THEN `RotatedBy(core.rotation)`
  (`NPC.cs:35547-35551` shell, `:35623-35627` turret, `:35637-35641`
  cannon, `:35652-35656` Dutchman), exactly the C# order. The wiring feeds
  the live core's `scale`/`rotation` through the slot-aligned pool.
- **M2 (grouped one-emitter battery)** — RESOLVED by activation: the module
  draws ONE `Next(maxValue4/5)` gate per LIVE-flag emitter in the order
  turret-left, turret-right, cannon-left, cannon-right, each hit drawing
  its own NextDouble/NextDouble/Next/Next chain (`NPC.cs:35978-36025`).
  The wiring runs that exact code on the `UpdateNPCs` stream.
- **M3 (phase bridge absent)** — RESOLVED: the module's 392 arm implements
  the bridge (`NPC.cs:35552-35613`, read whole): flag80 = core in [0,1) AND
  no crew lives; the %200 crew netUpdate marks; crew all dead → core
  `ai[0] = 3` (classic) / `1` (expert) + zero ai[1..3] + netUpdate. The
  wiring drains it through the sim (the module writes the core slot
  directly in the pooled step). The tautology witness is replaced by
  `the_dead_crew_open_the_core_and_the_fight_progresses`: live crew blocks
  the bridge, dead crew opens the core (ai[0]=3, ai[1..3]=0), the core's
  death ride (`NPC.cs:36104-36107`) kills it next tick.
- **M4 (despawn-ride restore inverted)** — the −1→0 / −2→2 restore lives in
  the CORE's aiStyle-76 machine (`update_saucer_core`, `NPC.cs:36130-36149`),
  which is R35's branch territory (89b65c54, in-place fixes). This wiring
  does NOT touch `update_saucer_core`; the bridge writes core `ai[0]` only.
  The module's mount-side M4 concern (the riders' despawn mirrors) is
  carried by `DiscourageDespawn(60)` + the `timeLeft` mirrors.

**RNG argument.** The wiring adds NO draws of its own: the sim calls the
SAME `style75_step` on the SAME `UpdateNPCs` stream the module's 16
witnesses pin (per-slot battery gates + hit chains + dust gates, the real
`DustPool::new_dust` internals, the sentinel velocity writes). The only
new stream consumers are the Item12/Item39 sound drains, which the module
already accounts for via `Style75Out::sounds` (the audio seam owns the one
`Next(-6,7)` pitch draw per audible play, at the C# call position). The
carrier-spawn/Transform resolves draw nothing (`NewNPC`/`Transform`/
`TargetClosest` are RNG-free). The `the_wired_style75_path_is_rng_parity_deterministic`
witness pins two identical apps to byte-identical NPC state + the
`UpdateNPCs` stream at the same position.

**Boundary.** Core 395 rides aiStyle 76 = R35's branch (`89b65c54`,
in-place fixes). `update_saucer_core` is UNTOUCHED; the bridge writes the
core's `ai[0]` (and zeroes ai[1..3]) only, exactly as the C# shell arm does.

**Verification.** Code-only: every seam call site checked against the
actual signatures by read/grep (`style75_step`'s 8-arg shape,
`Style75Ctx`/`Style75Out` fields, `play_use_sound`'s 6-arg shape,
`transform_to_kind`'s kind-table swap, `DustPool::new_dust`'s 12-arg shape,
`session_candidate`/`target_closest`). The C# bridge (`NPC.cs:35540-35619`)
and Transform (`:81084-81148`) and NewNPC Bottom placement (`:80755-80784`)
were re-read whole. The progression/retirement/RNG-parity witnesses are
WRITTEN, NOT RUN — **no compiler invoked**.

## The zombie fighter audit (S1-D-3z, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

Branch `fix/zombie-fighter-audit-defects` on the chain base `aab09419`
(S1-D-3p walker migration batch 1). Scope: distrust-verbatim audit of the
port's zombie fighter (`npc.rs::update_zombie`, the `AI_003_Fighters`
family, `NPC.cs:55856-60339`) + the missing small zombie variant kinds.
**Code-only mode — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; every test below
is WRITTEN, NOT RUN.**

### The three verified defects (fixed)

**A — the invented daylight burn.** The port accumulated `burn += 1/60`
in daylight and dealt `hp -= 6` per second ("the vanilla burn", the old
M4-first-pass note at ANALYSIS "NPCs and combat" — now corrected in
place). The C# `AI_003_Fighters` has NO daylight damage anywhere in
`:55856-60339`: the discouraged arm's daytime block is
`if (Main.IsItDay() && (double)(position.Y / 16f) < Main.worldSurface
&& type != 624 && type != 631) EncourageDespawn(10)` (`NPC.cs:57377-57380`)
— a 10-tick `timeLeft` flee-despawn window (`EncourageDespawn`
`:7249-7256`, the per-tick decrement + cull `:77986-77996`, mirrored by
the port's `despawn_timer`/`tick_despawn` in `world_sim/npcs.rs`). Fix:
the burn block is removed; the discouraged arm now calls
`encourage_despawn(10)` under the C#'s gate. NOTE the two boundaries are
different compares: the despawn gate is `<` on the TILE coordinate
(`position.Y / 16 < worldSurface`), the chase-discouragement gate is `>`
on PIXELS (`position.Y > worldSurface * 16`, `:60302`). The `burn` field
stays in `Npc` for struct-layout stability but is RETIRED — no machine
reads or writes it. The old test
`zombie_walks_to_the_player_and_burns_at_dawn` is repointed to
`zombie_walks_to_the_player_and_despawns_at_dawn` (no hp loss + the
10-tick window armed + expired).

**B — the blocked-path jump constant.** The port jumped `-6.2` at a
blocked path; `-6.2` exists NOWHERE in the C# arm. The one-tile-wall
step-up arm is `base.velocity.Y = -6f` (`NPC.cs:60125`, inside the
obstacle scan's `SolidTileNoPlatforms(num198, num199 - 1)` branch
`:60111-60128`; the taller walls jump `-8f`/`-7f` `:60102`/`:60107`, the
slope arm `-5f` `:60131`). Fix: `update_zombie`'s jump → `-6.0`;
`npc_ai.rs::WalkerParams::ZOMBIE`/`WANDER` jump → `-6.0` and the false
`-6.2` cite corrected to `NPC.cs:60125`. The port keeps its
collision-jump STAND-IN (jump whenever the horizontal move is blocked
and grounded) — the full door-bash / step-up scan (`:59831-60088`) is
the documented remainder below.

**C — the chase gate's missing idle term.** C# `NPC.cs:57336` is
`if (this.ai[3] < (float)num57 && NPC.DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged(...))`;
`num57` is 60 for the zombie family (the 180 override is the type-120
row, `:57035-57038`, unreachable for these kinds). The port's inline
fold tested only `!discouraged`, so a zombie whose idle counter reached
60 kept chasing instead of wandering. Fix: `self.ai[3] < 60.0 &&
!discouraged`. `ai[3]` is the fighter idle counter that
`world_sim/npcs.rs` ticks via `ambient_sound::fighter_idle_counter`
(`NPC.cs:57034-57149`) BEFORE `update_rng` (the S1-E-21 wave E wiring —
unchanged by this task). The batch-1 `walker_step_fighter`
(`npc_ai.rs`) already carried this term; the zombie's own fold had
dropped it. The discouraged arm itself was also wrong (`vx *= 0.9`
decay): it now ports the C#'s else-if body (`NPC.cs:57375-57401`) — for
the zombie family `CanBeBusyWithAction` is false (none of the listed
types, `:60332-60339`), so the arm always runs when the gate fails: the
daytime despawn (defect A), then the wander-flip (grounded + stopped →
`ai[0]++`, flip `direction`/`spriteDirection` every 2 ticks; any
horizontal motion resets `ai[0]`; `:57381-57397`), then the zero-direction
snap to +1 (`:57398-57401`).

## The obstacle scan + the blood-moon pair (S1-D-3z round 2, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

Same branch `fix/zombie-fighter-audit-defects`, same chain base
`aab09419`. This round closes the first round's documented remainder
(the door-bash / step-up scan) and adds the two blood-moon kinds the
audit named (489 BloodZombie / 490 Drippler). **Code-only mode — no
cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; every test below is WRITTEN, NOT RUN.**

### The obstacle scan (the remainder, now ported)

`npc_ai_fighter_scan.rs::fighter_obstacle_scan` ports `AI_003_Fighters`'
obstacle-scan tail (`NPC.cs:59831-60284`) verbatim for the zombie family,
called from `update_zombie` at the C#'s position — after the chase /
discouraged arms and the num107 ladder, BEFORE the gravity + collision
integration (`AI_003_Fighters` ends `:60298`; `UpdateCollision`
integrates afterwards). The four blocks:

- **The flag5 ground probe** (`:59831-59867`): while `vy == 0` (the hop
  `flag` is false for every zombie kind — it is set only by the
  scarecrow 305-309 arm, `npc_ai3_speeds`' `fx.hop_flag`, dropped by
  `run_ai3_ladder`), probe the floor row `(bottom + 7)/16` and the head
  row `(top - 9)/16` across the body's column span; a solid head cell
  kills flag5, a solid floor cell sets it, a null cell inside the span
  arms the `flag23` early-return (`:59863-59866` — the C# returns from
  `AI_003_Fighters` itself; the port returns `true` and the caller still
  integrates, as `UpdateCollision` runs after `AI()` regardless). No
  floor + rising cancels the jump (`:59859-59862`).
- **The 1-tile step-up assist** (`:59872-59948`): while falling or level,
  probe the NEXT-x column `centre + (width/2 + 1) * sign(vx)` at the
  body's bottom row; a 1-tile ledge with clear head/body room lifts
  `position.Y` onto it (the `gfxOffY` record + `stepSpeed` 1/2 by the
  lift's <9px threshold), the 16.1px reach. This is the block that makes
  1-tile climbing WORK — the jump ladder alone does not handle 1-tile
  ledges (the unicorn machine's inline copy, `npc_ai_unicorn.rs:328-387`,
  is the shape precedent). The `gfxOffY`/`stepSpeed` writes land on the
  NPC fields; the render pass does not read `gfx_off_y` yet and the decay
  helper (`npc_ai_unicorn_b.rs:285`) is unwired — the lift itself is
  live, the visual offset is the documented remainder.
- **The door bash** (`:59949-60088`): a closed door (tile 10) / tall gate
  (388) in the ahead probe column ticks `ai[2]` each scan; at 60 the bash
  fires — `vx = 0.5 * -direction`, `ai[1] += 5` (door) / `+2` (gate),
  `ai[2]` resets, and at `ai[1] >= 10` the open arms. The boolean algebra
  is ported VERBATIM (not simplified): `flag24` = the type list
  (`:59996`, 35 types — 489 is NOT in it), `flag25` = the graveyard
  `Next(60)` roll, `flag26` = the target inside unbreakable walls,
  `flag27 = ((!bloodMoon || getGoodWorld) && !flag25) & flag24` (the
  non-blood-moon reset gate). On a normal night a flag24 type resets
  `ai[1]` to 0 before the +5 (never opens); on a blood moon flag27 is
  false for EVERY type, so `ai[1]` accumulates and the door opens. The
  world mutation (`WorldGen.OpenDoor`) rides the `Npc::wants_door_bash`
  request drained in `world_sim/npcs.rs` (the `wants_sphere` borrow-safe
  shape — `update_zombie` holds `&World` immutable); the drain plays the
  `KillTile(fail: true)` thud on every bash and, when open, calls
  `edit::open_door` (a refusal sets `ai[3] = num57`, `:60064`) + the
  `Door_Opened` cue, all on the `UpdateNPCs` stream.
- **The probe jump ladder** (`:60089-60203`): while moving WITH the
  facing (`spriteDirection` matches the velocity sign, `:60096`), the
  ahead column `centre + 15 * direction` at row `bottom - 15`: a 3-tile
  wall jumps -8, a 2-tile wall -7, a 1-tile wall -6 (`:60125`), a sunken
  floor -5 (`:60131`), a gap (directionY < 0, no bottom-slope support)
  leaps -8 with `vx *= 1.5` (`:60134-60139`); no obstacle resets the bash
  counters (`:60140-60144`). The parked re-hop (`flag6 && ai[3] == 1`,
  `:60145-60148`) is carried; the expert-mode / type-586 hop
  (`:60149-60203`) is skipped (no expertMode flag, 586 not a zombie kind).
  The else-flag8 reset (`:60280-60284`) clears the bash counters when no
  floor is under the body.

The collision-jump stand-in survives ONLY as the fallback for cells the
15px-ahead probe misses (a wall the probe did not name): blocked +
grounded + `vy >= 0` → -6. The `vy >= 0` gate keeps the scan's own jump
(still negative after the +GRAVITY) from being overwritten on the tick
it fires. The repointed `the_blocked_path_jump_is_minus_six` witness
stands the zombie flush against a TWO-tile wall so the scan's -6 tier
fires deterministically (a 1-tile wall is now stepped, not jumped).

### The verifier W1 fix wave (fix/verifier-w1-golem-plantera, 2026-11-19, code-only)

TR-VERIFY-W1's findings against this family, fixed on the branch
(code-only mode again — **no compiler invoked**, witnesses WRITTEN NOT
RUN):

- **W1-2 (MED) — the free head's noTileCollide toggle was dropped.**
  The C# (`NPC.cs:31363-31371`) toggles `noTileCollide` per tick: a
  BLOCKED `CanHit` line head→player sets it (and flag53); a CLEAR line
  while the flag rides AND `SolidTiles(position, width, height)`
  releases it. `SetDefaults` 249 (`:12207-12220`) sets `noGravity` but
  NOT `noTileCollide` — the free head normally tile-collides. The port
  raw-integrated through walls unconditionally. Fixed: the flag rides
  `local_ai[1]` (249 uses no localAI slot — the body/fist mapping
  convention); the toggle runs at the arm top (the C#'s position,
  BEFORE the hover/cadence machine), and the tail free-integrates only
  while the flag rides, otherwise running the fists' axis-separated
  collision pass (velocity zeroes on impact, collideX/Y latch).
  `SolidTiles`' tile scan rides the house `collides_rect` stand-in.
  Witness: `npc.rs::w1_2_the_free_head_toggles_tile_collide_on_the_blocked_line`
  (blocked→set+pin, clear+air→keeps, clear+solids→release, impact→
  zero+latch). The per-tick `TargetClosest()` (`:31377`) stays folded:
  solo impact is facing only, the tail's vx-sign facing stands in
  (the documented solo convention — the G2 census claim below).
- **W1-6 (LOW) — the invented `.max(0.001)` normalize guards dropped.**
  The C# divides by the RAW `(float)Math.Sqrt` at every one of the six
  sites (`:31196`, `:31251`, `:31299`/`:31325`, `:19321`, `:19382`,
  `:31459`, `:31560`) — coincident centres produce NaN/inf velocity in
  vanilla (NaN pass-through, NOT a SafeNormalize zero-fold: the source
  is a bare division, no guard). The guards were port inventions;
  removed for strict fidelity (behaviour differs only in the degenerate
  coincident case). The fist follow's `num3 / d` division is never
  reached at d == 0 anyway (the `d < 12 + num3` gate takes the contact
  arm first). The unwired `npc_ai_style47` reference keeps its guard —

damage — no special kill code exists.

### RNG by construction

Every `Main.rand` draw is consumed in C# order (each draw = one
`InternalSample`, `UnifiedRandom.cs:62-88`); the stream-clone witnesses
replay the draws against a clone (the style-52 pattern):

* `DoMagicEffect` (`:45832-45923`): per dust, the `NewDustPerfect` ARGUMENTS
  evaluate first — `NextVector2CircularEdge` (1, `Utils.cs:1271-1274` →
  `NextVector2Unit` `:1261-1264`), the velocity `NextFloat` (1), the colour
  `NextFloat` (1), the scale `NextFloat` (1) — then `Dust.NewDust`'s own 6
  (`Dust.cs:170-175`/`:190`: `Next(w-4)`, `Next(h-4)` with w/h clamped ≥ 5,
  `Next(-20,21)` ×2, `Next(3)`, `Next(-20,21)`). Effect 5 with 0 < progress
  draws `Next(86,92)` ONCE (`:45869`) even when progress ≥ 1 zeroes the
  count; progress == 0 draws NOTHING (the `customData` branch `:45902-45909`
  is dead code).
* case 0 trail (`:46040-46058`): per dust 6 (`NewDust`, w/h = 100) + 2
  (`NextVector2Circular`, `Utils.cs:1266-1269`) + 1 (velocity) + 1 (fadeIn)
  + 6 (`CloneDust` → `NewDust`, `Dust.cs:263-281`) = 16 ×2 = 32/tick, ticks
  11..149 (139 ticks × 32 = 4448 draws over the materialize).
* case 13 trail (`:46880-46898`): 1 (colour) + 6 (w/h = 200) + 2 + 1
  (velocity) + 1 (scale) + 1 (fadeIn) + 6 = 18 ×5 = 90/tick.
* gameplay: case 2 `NextFloatDirection` (`:46291`, +`NextFloat` `:46294`
  when phase-2 expert — BOTH consumed), case 5 `NextFloat` (`:46473`),
  case 7 the DISCARDED `NextFloat` (`:46553`).

**Dust-pool assumption (documented deviation)**: the pool is below the 50 %
`maxDustToDraw` threshold (the FIRST skip tier, `Dust.cs:139-143`) and
on-screen, so `Dust.NewDust`'s skip draws and early-outs (`Dust.cs:77-101`)

(`GameContent/ChildSafety.cs:33`) so its branch (`Dust.cs:194-213`) never

`TargetClosest()` (`:34641`) rides `npc_target::target_closest` with
aiStyle 68 (not the fighter 3, so the centre rule applies).

**Faithful pieces** (each cited at its site in the module):
- The perch's old-facing keep (`:34639-34645`): `num1000` is the OLD
  target, so a bird that already had a target keeps its direction even
  though `TargetClosest` re-faces.
- The wet swim gate (`:34646`): the probe column is the INTEGER division
  of the TRUNCATED probe X — `(int)(Center.X + (width/2 + 8) * direction)

  `> Main.maxTilesX - 5` (unlike InWorld's `>=`), the three

- The water line (`:34671-34698`) is the arm's OWN inline form — NOT
  `Collision.GetWaterLine`: no `y-2` dry gate, no InWorld guard, the

## The mana machinery (S1-P-i19)

**Headline finding — `DebugOptions.ManaV2` is the SHIPPED mana machine.** The
static ctor sets `ManaV2 = true` (`Testing/DebugOptions.cs:85`) and a census of
the whole decompile (game + ReLogic) finds NO write that ever sets it false —
no command, no config, no menu. The earlier ANALYSIS note ("a debug cheat, not
ported") was wrong: the 1.4.5 mana rework IS the default behaviour, and the
port's pre-i19 `CheckMana` implemented the legacy V1 refusal the source never
uses. `regen.rs::MANA_V2` folds the flag to a `true` constant; the V1 lanes
stay unreachable exactly as in the source.

## The magic guns + tomes use arms (S1-P-i22)

`Player.ItemCheck_Shoot`'s 14 magic guns + tomes (census + verdicts:
`docs/research/56-magic-guns-tomes-census.md`). The use-pass arms live in
`world_sim/editing.rs` (the if/else chain beside the gem-staff/blaze arms);
the 17 projectile rows + AI arms in `projectile/data.rs` + `projectile.rs`.

Deliberate deviations (the port's established conventions, not new gaps):

1. **Dust/sound RNG skipped pool-wide.** The C# projectile AI arms draw
   `Main.rand` for dust/gore/sound only (AI_005's :23883/:23973/:23983/
   :24035/:24039, AI_021's :25594, the 459 orb's :54678, the 442 Kill's
   :73531 Next(3,7)). The port's pool keeps ZERO RNG (the S1-D-5 slice-A
   precedent, `projectile_ai001_a.rs` module doc), so these draws are NOT
   consumed - the `UpdateProjectiles` stream stays untouched BY
   CONSTRUCTION. The ONE exception is the NettleBurst head's `Next(2)` type
   flip (`Projectile.cs:23709-23713`), which changes STATE (the kind), so it
   IS consumed on the pool's rng (the `ai_style4` arm takes the rng arg).
   The use-pass draws (the harp/guitar/poison/starfury/sky-fracture rolls)
   ride `UpdatePlayers` in C# order - the witnesses replay them.

   convention, `tr_core::damage::crit_roll` = Next(1,101)); the C# rolls at
   hit (`Projectile.cs:12890-12898`). Same stream, same count per shot.
3. **Hit-time multipliers NOT applied.** The 265 PoisonFang x0.75
   (`Projectile.cs:13414-13416`, a `this.damage` mutation that COMPOUNDS per
   hit), the 76/77/78 notes x0.95 (:13432-13436) and the 9 Starfury star

   port's `damage_pve` applies no per-kind hit multiplier today (only the
   flail family), so they are left unported and recorded as a gap in the
   census (research/56). The spawn carries the raw weapon damage. The
   Starfury's x1.5 USE-time damage (`Player.cs:47265`) IS applied at spawn
   (it is a use-pass fold, not a hit-time one).

   (`app/frame/draw.rs:735-746`): min(screen - 2*translation). The harp's

## The minion target command (S1-P-i27)

The summoner target lane, verbatim against `Player.cs`/`Projectile.cs`
(code-only mode — no compiler invoked, 28 witnesses written not run).

**The aim + maintenance.** `minion_npc_target_aim`
(`Player.MinionNPCTargetAim`, `Player.cs:56914-56933`) measures
`NPC.Hitbox.Distance(mouseWorld)` — the rectangle-to-point distance
(`Utils.cs:1507-1542`: 0 inside/touching, the axis bands, the four corner
distances), shared as `npc_ai_style64::rect_distance` (`pub(crate)`).
The scan re-reads the current best's distance each iteration (the C#
shape); the hitbox anchors are the `(int)` position/size
(`Entity.cs:171-176`). The `doNotDisableIfTheTargetIsTheSame` parameter
mirrors the C# signature — the only caller passes false
(`ItemCheck_MinionAltFeatureUse`, `:49777`); the whip's aiStyle-165
retarget is a plain write and never calls it. `update_minion_target`
(`UpdateMinionTarget`, `:56999-57028`) replaces the old invalidation
half: the rest point drops past 1000 px CENTRE distance
(`base.Distance`, `Entity.cs:195-198`), the attack target drops when
unchaseable or its HITBOX is past 3000 px from the player's centre. The
`whoAmI == Main.myPlayer` gate folds to the single local player.

**The rest-spot command.** `minion_rest_target_aim`
(`MinionRestTargetAim`, `:56935-56997`) walks the mouse's tile column:
the full-solid test (`nactive && tileSolid && !tileSolidTop`), the ≤20
up-scan (bounded `num2+num5 > 1`) and 20 down-scan, the clearance pick
`num3 = (num7 <= -num4) ? num7+3 : num4-2`, then the unbounded drop
until a 5-tile window holds a `WorldGen.SolidTileAllowBottomSlope`
(`WorldGen.cs:70167-70189` — the FULL form: solid-or-solidTop, the
platform-top-frame clause, no half-brick, not actuated; shared
`pub(crate)` from the AI_026 slice-C copy). The port caps the drop at
the world's bottom row (the out-of-world probe reads solid, so the C#
loop terminates there too). The spot `(tileX*16+8, row*16)` is kept
only within 1000 px of the player. Triggers: `key_double_tap_down`
(`KeyDoubleTap`, `:56764-56787`) fires the aim for `setForbidden`;
`key_hold_down` (`KeyHoldDown`, `:56894-56912`) clears the spot at
holdTime ≥ 60 for `setStardust`/`setForbidden`. The driver
(`update_minion_rest_command`, `:25022-25073`'s down-cardinal half)
mirrors the 15-tick double-tap window, the press edge
(`controlDown && releaseDown`) and the hold counter; the
`releaseDown = !controlDown` latch refresh (`:27636`) folds to the
driver's tail (the only down-cardinal consumer in the port).
`Main.ReversedUpDownArmorSetBonuses` (`Main.cs:273`, the settings
toggle) flips the cardinal to UP, disabling the DOWN command. Both set
flags re-derive per tick (`ResetEffects` `:18743`/`:18745`, the
armor-set block's Forbidden 3776/3777/3778 + Stardust 3381/3382/3383
triples, `DataStructures/ArmorSetBonuses.cs:482-483`).

**The summoner accessory fold.** The `UpdateEquips` tail
(`Player.cs:12970-12984`): `accSilverBracer` adds `tagEffectDuration +=
2f` + `maxTagEffects++` (the `minionDamage += 0f` half is a verbatim
no-op), `accMobiusStrip` adds `maxTagEffects++` + `whipRangeMultiplier
+= 0.1f`, `accWickedArmlet` adds `maxTagEffects++`. Grants: 6156 Silver
Bracer (`:14510`), 6158 Mobius Strip (`:14513`), 6159 Wicked Armlet
(`:14516`), 6162 Ouroboros Ring (`:14519` — the Mobius flag; the
`accSnakeBand` half unported), 6163 Twilight Grasp (`:14523` — BOTH
flags), 6179 Armlet of Ruin (`:14585` — the armlet flag; the
`accArmletOfRuin` tag-damage half unported), 6182 Wicked Claws
(`:14601-14603` — the armlet flag + `meleeSpeed += 0.12f`; the
`autoReuseGlove` half unported, the Titan Glove precedent), 6183 Silver
Shield (`:14605-14609` — the bracer flag beside its knockback/fire-walk
row in `accessory_defense.rs`). The C# `TagEffectStack` reads the
PLAYER's `maxTagEffects`/`tagEffectDuration` live
(`TagEffectStack.cs:47`/`:133`); the port keeps copies on the stack, so
`ResetEffects` syncs the bases (`reset_player_scalars`, `:18517-18518`)
and the fold adds once per tick after every grant
(`add_player_scalars`). The whip range: base 1f (`:18498`), the Tiki
helm +0.1 (`:13852-13855`) and Stardust body/legs +0.15
(`:13876-13881`) ride `grant_summon_caps`' armor loop, the Tiki SET
+0.2 rides `tr_core::armor_sets::SetStats::whip_range`

## The pickaxe mining census (S1-P-i29, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

`task/S1-P-i29-pickaxe-mining` censuses the pickaxe/drill mining interaction
against `Player.ItemCheck` and ports the WRONG/missing halves. **Code-only
mode: no compiler invoked; the witnesses are WRITTEN, NOT RUN.** Scope: the
pickaxe/drill ONLY — the axe chop (i30) and the hammer slope/pound (i31) keep
their pre-i29 time-based pacing and are recorded as follow-ups.

### The C# chain (the source of truth)

- `ItemCheck_UseMiningTools` (`Player.cs:45584-45644`): the tool gate
  (`pick/axe/hammer > 0`, `:45595`), the reach gate
  (`IsTargetTileInItemRange`, `:45599` → `:46313-46316` →
  `IsInTileInteractionRange` `:32025` → `TileReachCheckSettings.GetTileRegion`
  `TileReachCheckSettings.cs:45-54` → `Collision.InTileBounds`
  `Collision.cs:3776`), the `toolTime == 0 && itemAnimation > 0 &&
  controlUseItem` action gate (`:45608`/`:45626`).
- `ItemCheck_UseMiningTools_ActuallyUseMiningTool` (`:45646-45782`): the
  tool/tile match (`:45656` — a pick mines the non-axe/non-hammer tiles, an
  axe the `tileAxe` tiles, a hammer the `tileHammer` tiles), the pick arm
  (`:45772-45780` — `PickTile(x, y, sItem.pick)` then
  `itemTime = (int)(useTime * pickSpeed)`).
- `PickTile` (`:53757-53826`) + `PickTile_DetermineDamage` (`:53828-53844`):
  the mystic-snake-rope 504 refusal (`:53760`), the `GetPickaxeDamage` call,
  the `CanKillTile` zero (`:53832`), the getGoodWorld ×2 (`:53836`), the
  `DoesPickTargetTransformOnKill` preview-zero (`:53840`), the `HitTile`
  accumulation to 100 (`:53769`), the `ClearMiningCacheAt` on break
  (`:53773`), the `KillTile(fail: true)` fail tick (`:53815`).
- `GetPickaxeDamage` (`:53902-54045`): the noFail 100 head, the multiplier
  ladder (the nested ternary at `:53909`), the zero-damage tier-gate
  else-chain (`:53910-53971`), the soft-tile second add (`:53972`), the
  desert-fossil +5 (`:53976`), the rope/stalactite/crimson-grass instant 100
  (`:53980`), the mannequin/weapon-rack redirects (`:53984-54043`).
- The `toolTime` cadence (`:43576-43587`): `!channel → toolTime = itemTime`;
  `channel → toolTime--`, wrap to `useTime - 1`. `ItemCheck_StartActualUse`
  arms `toolTime = 1` for the tools (`:51660-51663`).
- `HitTile` (`HitTile.cs:9-477`): the 500-slot book, the LRU `SortSlots`
  (`:208-238`), the `AddDamage` zero-on-buffer guard + the `updateAmount:false`
  preview (`:189-206`), the TTL decay ladder (`:285-333` — `<12` −10, `<24`
  −7, `<36` −5, `<48` −2 per prune), the gone-tile/wall clear.
- The drill channel: `StartChanneling(sItem)` (`:52958-52968`) latches
  `Player.channel`; the drill projectile's aiStyle-20 machine
  (`Projectile.cs:25481-25584`) aims at the mouse while held, kills itself on
  the release (`:25549`), and holds the item animation via
  `SetDummyItemTime(2)` (`:25563` → `Player.cs:4432-4441`).

### What was WRONG / missing in the port (the census verdicts)

1. **WRONG — the mining model was time-per-tile, not damage-per-hit.** The
   pre-i29 arm accumulated `mine_timer += dt` to a `hardness` threshold
   (`base * 35/pick * pickSpeed`). The C# accumulates `GetPickaxeDamage`
   damage into the `HitTile` book until 100. **Fixed**: `tr_core::hit_tile`
   ports the book; `pick_tile_hit` accumulates the real damage; the break
   fires at `>= 100`.
2. **WRONG — `pick_can_mine` was a partial gate table.** It missed the
   chlorophyte-200, mythril/orichalcum-110, adamantite/titanium-150,
   lihzahrd-210, hellforge-underworld, trap-row and dungeon-x-band gates, and
   the whole damage-multiplier ladder. **Fixed**: `tr_core::tool::pickaxe_damage`
   ports `GetPickaxeDamage` verbatim; `pick_can_mine` is now the
   `damage > 0` projection (the depth-only dungeon approximation kept for the
   tile-target gate, the full path carries the x-band).
3. **WRONG — the reach was a circle.** The pre-i29 gate used
   `(tile_range_x + 1) * TILE_PX` radius. The C# is a rectangle
   (`tileRangeX + tileBoost` × `tileRangeY + tileBoost`, clamped 20).
   **Fixed**: `tile_in_reach_rect` ports `GetTileRegion` + `InTileBounds`;
   `mining_tile_range` adds the Extendo Grip/Gizmo Pack/Grand Design +3/+2
   (`:13040-13044`) and the held Toolbox +1/+1 (`:14954-14958`).
4. **WRONG — the mining cadence ignored `useTime`/`toolTime`.** **Fixed**:
   the `toolTime` mirror/countdown (`:43576-43587`) + the
   `itemTime = (int)(useTime * pickSpeed)` re-arm (`:45779`).
5. **MISSING — the drill channel.** The drills (385/386/388/1189/1196/1203/
   1231/2774/2779/2784/3464/579/2798) are `channel` items with `pick > 0`;
   the port treated them as generic throws. **Fixed**: `drill_channel_start`
   spawns the aiStyle-20 drill projectile once on the press; `ai_drill`
   (`projectile.rs`) ports the hold/aim/release; the channel block holds the
   swing at the dummy 2 ticks. The drill `proj_data` rows + the aiStyle-20/75
   dispatch arms are added.
6. **MISSING — the grass/moss conversion.** `DoesPickTargetTransformOnKill`
   (`:54047`) + `KillTile(fail: true)` (`WorldGen.cs:63715-63735`) convert a
   grass tile to its soil at 100 damage instead of breaking it. **Fixed**:
   `does_pick_target_transform` + `convert_grass_tile`.
7. **MISSING — the `pickSpeed` 0.3 floor** (`:25972-25975`) and the Mining
   buff 104 (`:10136`) / Ancient Chisel (`:13032-13035`) folds. **Fixed**:
   `Player::pick_speed` clamps at 0.3; the buff/accessory arms add to
   `pick_speed_bonus`.

### Deliberate deviations (recorded)

- **The axe/hammer arms keep the time-based pacing.** The i30 (axe) and i31
  (hammer/slope) tasks own the `tileAxe`/`tileHammer` hit-buffer models
  (`Player.cs:45665-45771`). The demon-altar smash keeps its pre-i29
  `SmashAltar` wiring; the wall hammer keeps its time-based dig. A pick
  refuses the axe/hammer tiles (the `:45656` match), so the pick side is
  faithful even though the chop/slope pacing is not yet the C#'s.
- **The `HitTile` draw-side fields are render-only.** `crackStyle`'s roll
  (`HitTile.cs:36-45`, the static `HitTile.rand` + the no-repeat loop) stays
  in the crack overlay's world-seeded `mine_crack_rng` (the S1-G-1 wave C
  determinism deviation); the `AddDamage` wobble-direction `Main.rand.
  NextFloat()` draw (`:66`) and the `DrawFreshAnimations` miner's wobble
  (`:335-471`) are not drawn. The sim book therefore takes **no RNG** — the
  mining tick adds no draws to any stream. The C#'s wobble draw rides the
  `UpdatePlayers` swap; its absence is a render-only deviation (the same
  class as the crack-style seed).
- **The drill projectile's per-tick jitter + dust are render-only.** The
  `velocity.X *= 1 + Next(-3,4)*0.01` wobble (`Projectile.cs:25575`) and the
  1-in-6 dust (`:25576-25583`) are not ported (the port draws no drill dust);
  the `ai_drill` hold/aim/release/position-pin are faithful. The Laser Drill
  (445, aiStyle 75) holds its channel like the drills; its full `AI_075`
  laser AI (the tile-target snap, the reach clamp, the beam light,
  `:66244-66358`) is a follow-up.
- **The `pick_can_mine` dungeon gate stays depth-only** for the tile-target
  gate (`cursor_cell_is_tile_target`); the full `pickaxe_damage` path carries
  the 0.35/0.65 x-band. The two agree on every tile the port's worldgen

- **The `noBuilding` gate is unmodelled** (the port has no `noBuilding`
  state — the frozen/webbed gate already refuses the use); the DD2

- **The per-tick `KillTile(fail: true)` sound/dust** has no port path (the

## The bug net (S1-P-i36, task/S1-P-i36-bug-net, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

**Census verdict.** The bug-net use was ENTIRELY MISSING from the port —
no `ItemCheck_CatchCritters`/`CatchNPC`/`ReleaseNPC`/`catchItem`
machinery and no sim-side swung-item rectangle (the melee arm is the
cursor-point approximation, `editing.rs`'s documented stand-in). The
three net ITEM rows were already faithful (1991: 25/25 scale 1 rare 0;
3183: 18/18 scale 1.15 rare 4; 4821: 21/21 scale 0.85 rare 3; all
useStyle 1, damage −1, autoReuse, useTurn, UseSound Item1 —
`Item.cs:21305-21315`/`:29541-29553`/`:39480-39492`), and the `itemdata`
`make_npc` column was populated but `registry::make_npc` was a stub
returning 0. So this task ports the missing machinery, not wrong
constants.

## The light-item family (S1-P-i42, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

Branch `task/S1-P-i42-torch-glowstick` (worktree TR-i42). **CODE-ONLY mode**:
file reads/writes + git only — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/dotnet/graphify,
**no compiler invoked**. Scope: the torch/glowstick/flare LIGHT items — the
torch placement (wall/tile/underwater variants), the glowstick throw (aiStyle
14, sticky/bouncy), the flare gun (aiStyle 33), and the held-light source.
Census first; the WRONGs fixed verbatim with C# cites.

### Census verdicts

**Torch placement — three WRONGs fixed.**
1. *The style never rode the tile.* The legacy single-tile write
   (`edit/place.rs::place_tile`) wrote `frameX = frameY = 0` for every torch,
   dropping `Item.placeStyle`. The C# `WorldGen.PlaceTile` case 4
   (`WorldGen.cs:59798-59842`) writes `frameY = 22 * style` (`:59839`) — the
   style column `CheckTorch` preserves and `TileLightScanner` reads
   (`tile_light/scanner.rs`'s `fy / 22` arm). A Blue Torch (427, style 1)
   placed as a plain torch and lit white. **Fix**: a dedicated
   `edit::place_torch` arm (`place_item_tile` dispatches kind 4 to it) writes
   `frameY = 22 * style`, runs the support gate (`:59835`) and the liquid gate
   (`:59454-59467`), then `CheckTorch` for the attachment frameX.
2. *The liquid gate was absent.* The C# refuses a torch in a liquid cell
   unless the style is 8/11/17 (the `ItemID.Sets.WaterTorches`,
   `ItemID.cs:1372` — Cursed/Ichor/Coral), and even those check the sub-tile's
   `WaterPlacement` (`:59462-59466`). The port placed any torch underwater.
   **Fix**: `place_torch`'s liquid gate — styles 8/11/17 resolve their

### The bounce chain order (load-bearing)

`HandleMovement`'s blocked-move chain (`Projectile.cs:18398-19853`) checks the
outer TYPE chain before the aiStyle chain. The 515-517 arm (`:18479-18489`,
both axes ×−0.9 gated |last|>1) takes the bouncy glowstick BEFORE the
